UK garage, abbreviated as ukg, is a type of electronic music that came from England in the early 1990s. It mixes styles like garage house, R&B, jungle, and dance-pop. UK garage usually has a beat with shuffled 4/4 rhythm and syncopated hi-hats, cymbals, and snares. Sometimes, it includes irregular kick drum patterns. Vocals in UK garage are often chopped up and their pitch or time is changed to fit the rhythm, usually at about 130 beats per minute. UK garage led to subgenres like speed garage and 2-step. By the mid-2000s, it was mostly replaced by styles like bassline, grime, and dubstep. During the mid-2000s, UK garage declined, and UK funky, a related style, emerged.
Fowler is a town in Center Township, Benton County, Indiana, United States. In 2010, the population was 2,317. It is part of the Lafayette, Indiana metropolitan area.
Oppen is a municipality in Gros-de-Vaud district, which is in the canton of Vaud in Switzerland.

Louis Antoine Godey was born on June 6, 1804, and died on November 29, 1878. He was an American editor and publisher. He is famous for starting "Godey's Lady's Book," which was the first successful American women's fashion magazine.

Mikhail Alexandrovich Bakunin, born in 1814 and died on July 1, 1876, was a Russian revolutionary and anarchist. He founded collectivist anarchism and is considered one of the most influential figures in the anarchist movement. Bakunin was also an important ideologue in Europe, with many followers in Russia and Europe. Bakunin grew up on a family estate called Pryamukhino in the Tver region. He studied in Moscow from 1840 and then in Berlin, hoping to become a professor. In Paris, he met Karl Marx and Pierre-Joseph Proudhon, who greatly influenced him. His growing radicalism ended his chances of becoming a professor. He was expelled from France for opposing Russia's invasion of Poland. In 1849, he was arrested in Dresden for his role in the 1848 Czech rebellion and was sent back to Russia. He was imprisoned in Saint Petersburg, then in the Shlisselburg fortress from 1854, and later exiled to Siberia in 1857. He escaped through Japan to the United States, then to London, where he worked with Alexander Herzen on a journal called "Kolokol" (The Bell). In 1863, he joined a rebellion in Poland but failed to reach it. Instead, he spent time in Switzerland and Italy. In 1868, Bakunin joined the International Working Men's Association, leading an anarchist group that grew quickly. A major conflict arose at the 1872 Hague congress between Bakunin and Marx. Marx believed in using the state to create socialism, while Bakunin and his anarchists advocated replacing the state with self-managed workplaces and communes. The anarchist group lost the debate when Bakunin was absent. In 1870, Bakunin wrote two major works, "Statism and Anarchy" and "God and the State." Despite his declining health, he continued to support worker and peasant movements. He took part in an uprising in Lyon, France, and tried to join an anarchist rebellion in Bologna, Italy, but returned to Switzerland due to his health. Bakunin is remembered as a key figure in anarchism, opposing Marxism, especially the dictatorship of the proletariat. His work "God and the State" is widely translated and still in print. He influenced many modern anarchists, including Noam Chomsky. His biographer Mark Leier noted that Bakunin's ideas impacted many thinkers, from Peter Kropotkin to the Spanish anarchists during the civil war, Herbert Marcuse, E.P. Thompson, Neil Postman, and others, to today's anti-globalization anarchists.

The Parliament of Albania, or Kuvendi, is the main group of people who make laws for Albania. It has 140 members chosen every four years by all citizens. The Parliament is led by a Speaker and at least one Deputy Speaker. They use a system where parties list candidates, and these are chosen based on votes. There are 12 areas where elections happen, each related to a part of Albania. The Parliament can change Albania's borders or the constitution, pass laws, approve the government, watch over how the government works, declare war, stop fighting, make budgets, and check the government's financial reports. It also holds referendums, does elections, and makes decisions as needed by the constitution. The Parliament chooses the President of Albania too. After elections, the first Parliament meeting happens within 20 days, with the President as Speaker. Laws passed by the Parliament are published in the Official Journal of Albania. The oldest Parliament with records was in Lezhë in 1444. It was called the League of Lezhë, led by Gjergj Kastrioti Skënderbeu, and was a group against the Ottoman Empire.
Leslie Orgel, a British chemist born on January 12, 1927, and died on October 27, 2007, is famous for his ideas about how life began.
pittefaux is a commune in Pas-de-Calais, which is in Hauts-de-France, a region in France.

Tapioca is a starch from the roots of the cassava plant, which is also known as manioc or manihot esculenta. This plant is originally from the north and central-west parts of Brazil. However, it spread to other parts of South America. The plant was taken to the West Indies, Africa, and Asia by Portuguese and Spanish explorers. Cassava is a shrub that grows well in warm areas. It can handle poor soil better than many other food plants. For many people in tropical countries, tapioca is a main food source, but it only provides carbohydrates and lacks protein, vitamins, and minerals. In other places, tapioca is used to make foods thicker.
Flavio Bucci was born on May 25, 1947, and died on February 18, 2020. He was an Italian actor, voice actor, and film producer.
Zoran "Bata" Mirković, born on September 21, 1971, is a retired Serbian footballer and currently a manager.
Carhaix-Plouguer is a commune in Finistère, which is in western Brittany, France.
Shadow Hills is a neighborhood in the Verdugo Mountains and the northeastern part of San Fernando Valley. It is in the city of Los Angeles, California.

"With my own eyes" is a song by a German group called Sash! It came out on September 4, 2000, through a record company named x-it records. The song is from their third album, "Trilenium." It features a Finnish singer named Inka Auhagen. The song was popular in Europe and reached number 10 on the UK singles chart. It was Sash!'s last top 10 hit on that chart until 2008.

"Just a Girl" is a song by American band No Doubt from their third album, "Tragic Kingdom," released in 1995. It came out as the first single in the U.S. on September 21, 1995. Gwen Stefani and Tom Dumont wrote it, and Matthew Wilder produced it. It appeared on their 2003 greatest hits album, "The Singles 1992-2003." The song is about Stefani's life as a woman and her struggles with strict parents. It was the first song Stefani wrote without help from her brother Eric. Critics praised the song for its lyrics and Stefani's singing voice. It helped make No Doubt famous. In the U.S., it reached number 23 on the Billboard Hot 100 and entered several other charts. It was also popular in other countries, reaching the top ten in Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, Norway, Scotland, and the U.K. A music video for the song, directed by Mark Kohr, shows Stefani singing in a clean restroom while the male band members are in a dirty one. They eventually dance together. Stefani wore a popular outfit in the video. No Doubt and Stefani performed the song in many live shows, including during their 1995-1997 "Tragic Kingdom World Tour," the 2002 "Rock Steady Tour," and the 2016 "This Is What the Truth Feels Like" tour. Stefani named her 2018-2020 Las Vegas residency after the song. It has also been covered by other musicians.

The anus is a hole at the end of an animal's digestive system, opposite the mouth. Its job is to help the animal get rid of waste. This waste includes things the animal can't digest, like bones, leftover food parts like cellulose, harmful materials, and extra bacteria. Some animals, like amphibians, reptiles, and birds, use a single opening called the cloaca for waste, mating, and laying eggs. Monotremes, which are a type of mammal, also have a cloaca, which they inherited from ancient animals. Marsupials have one opening for waste and a separate one for reproduction. Most placental mammals have separate openings for different functions: one for poop and pee, and another for pee and reproduction. The development of the anus was a big step in how animals evolved. It seems to have developed at least twice in different groups of animals. This development was linked to other important changes, like the body structure and other body parts that could change and specialize.

A lawn mower is a machine that cuts grass to keep it even. The height of the grass can be adjusted by the user, often with a lever. The mower can be pushed manually, or it can have a motor powered by electricity, a battery, or an internal combustion engine. Small mowers are pushed by the operator, while larger ones can be ridden or driven. Some mowers are automatic, while others need to be guided by a person. There are two main types of blades used in lawn mowers. Single-blade mowers that spin around a vertical axis are called rotary mowers. Mowers with a cutting bar and multiple blades that spin around a horizontal axis are called cylinder or reel mowers. There are different kinds of mowers for different needs. Small push mowers are used for small yards. Larger push mowers with motors are used for bigger lawns. Riding mowers, which look like small tractors, are used for very large lawns. Big multi-blade mowers mounted on tractors are used for large areas like golf courses, but are not good for tricky terrain.
Alma, formerly known as Mound City and Rantoul, is a village in Marion County, Illinois, United States. According to the 2000 census, the population was 386.
cyclostome is a biological term, which comes from the Greek words for "round mouth." It is used in a few different ways.

Emlain Kudo Kabua, born in February 1928, was the first lady of the Marshall Islands. She was the wife of former Marshall Islands president Amata Kabua and the mother of President-elect David Kabua. Emlain Kabua served as the first first lady from 1979 to 1996. She also designed the flag of the Marshall Islands.

The Jurassic period is 56 million years long and started after the Triassic period ended. It lasted until the beginning of the Cretaceous period. It is part of the Mesozoic era, also known as the Age of Reptiles. It began with a major extinction event. Two other smaller extinction events happened during the Jurassic: one in the early part and another at the end. The Jurassic is divided into three time periods: Early, Middle, and Late. In geology, it is split into the Lower, Middle, and Upper Jurassic rock layers. The name Jurassic comes from the Jura Mountains in Europe. Limestone from this period was first found there. By the start of the Jurassic, a big landmass called Pangaea was breaking into two parts: Laurasia in the north and Gondwana in the south. This created more coastlines and made the climate wetter. Many deserts turned into rainforests. On land, dinosaurs became the main animals. They replaced other reptiles like dinosauromorphs and crocodylomorphs. Birds also appeared, coming from a branch of dinosaurs. Lizards and early mammals, including some primitive placental mammals, also evolved. Crocodiles started living in water. The seas had many reptiles like ichthyosaurs and plesiosaurs. Pterosaurs were the main flying animals.

Chakotay is a character in a TV show called "Star Trek: Voyager." He is played by an actor named Robert Beltran. Chakotay is the leader of the ship's crew. He was one of the first Native American characters in a Star Trek story. To make Native Americans feel inspired, the people who made the show chose him to be a main character. They asked a Native American writer named Jamake Highwater to help create Chakotay's story. At first, Chakotay's Native American tribe wasn't clear, but it was later decided he was Hopi. He first appeared in the show's first episode. Chakotay was in the main group of actors for the whole show, and his last appearance was in the final episode. He had an ongoing story about his girlfriend Seska until she died. Chakotay didn't want to work with the Borg because of his past experiences. By the end, he and another character, Seven of Nine, became a couple. After the ship returned, Chakotay became the captain. But his relationship with Seven ended. People liked Chakotay as an example for Native Americans in science fiction, calling him "ground-breaking."

Desoto is a city in Dallas County, Texas, in the United States. In 2010, it had 49,047 people. Desoto is a suburb of Dallas. It is part of the Southwestern area, including Desoto, Cedar Hill, Duncanville, and Lancaster.

Canillo is one of the parishes in Andorra. Canillo is also the main town in this parish. The parish is seen as the religious center of Andorra. It has a sanctuary and chapel dedicated to Our Lady of Meritxell, the patron saint of Andorra. It also has a well-preserved Romanesque church called Sant Joan de Caselles. In 2011, Canillo had 4,826 people. Even though it is a tourist place, the parish still has many farming and livestock activities.

A defoliant is a chemical used to make plant leaves fall off. It is sprayed or dusted on plants. Defoliants are used to remove weeds in farmland and lawns. They helped increase food production during the mid-20th century, part of the Green Revolution. Defoliants were also used in wars to destroy enemy crops and hideouts. The United Kingdom used them during the Malayan Emergency, and the United States during the Vietnam War.

Mount Jackson is a town in Shenandoah County, Virginia, United States. In 2010, it had 1,994 people. For travelers on Highway I-81, Mount Jackson is easy to find. Exit 273 leads to a water tower painted like a basket of apples. The town has a history as an important commercial and railroad center. It also has connections to the Civil War and is part of a historic area listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

Washington County is a county in North Carolina, U.S. In 2010, it had 13,228 people. Its main town is Plymouth. The county was created in 1799 from part of Tyrrell County. It was named after George Washington. There are three towns in Washington County. Plymouth is the main town. The other towns are Roper and Creswell. Washington County is famous for its fertile farmland, large forests, and many lakes. The Roanoke River and Albemarle Sound are to the north. Lake Phelps, at 16,000 acres, is in Creswell and part of Pettigrew State Park. Somerset Place, a restored old plantation, is also on Lake Phelps. In the south of the county, the Pungo area of the Pocosin Lakes National Wildlife Refuge is known for the best bear watching in North Carolina. This area has the world's largest black bears and the highest bear population. The North Carolina Black Bear Festival, which wins awards, happens in Plymouth every June.

Philip Kotler, born on May 27, 1931, is an American author, consultant, and professor. He taught at the Kellogg School of Management at Northwestern University from 1962 to 2018, as the S. C. Johnson & Son Distinguished Professor of International Marketing. Kotler defined the marketing mix. He wrote over 80 books, including "Marketing Management," "Principles of Marketing," and "Kotler on Marketing." Kotler describes strategic marketing as connecting society's needs with industrial responses. He helped create social marketing, which aims to encourage healthier and safer lifestyles. He also introduced the concepts of demarketing, prosumers, atmospherics, and societal marketing. Many scholars call him "the father of modern marketing." His recent works focus on economic justice and the problems of capitalism. He published "Confronting Capitalism: Real Solutions for a Troubled Economic System" in 2015, "Democracy in Decline: Rebuilding Its Future" in 2016, "Advancing the Common Good" in 2019, and "Brand Activation: From Purpose to Action" in 2018.

Joseph Patrick Kennedy III, born on October 4, 1980, is an American lawyer and politician. He has been a U.S. representative since 2013. Kennedy works for the Democratic Party and represents a district that covers parts of Boston and the state's south coast. He used to work as an assistant district attorney in Massachusetts. Kennedy is the son of Joseph P. Kennedy II and a grandson of Robert F. Kennedy. He is also a grandnephew of John F. Kennedy and Ted Kennedy, and a great-grandson of Joseph P. Kennedy Sr. Born in Boston, Kennedy grew up there with his twin brother, Matthew Rauch Kennedy. After graduating from Stanford University, he volunteered in the Dominican Republic for two years. He later got his law degree from Harvard in 2009. In early 2012, he left his job to run for a U.S. House seat. Kennedy won and started his job in January 2013. He is part of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce. In 2019, Kennedy said he would run for the Democratic nomination for the U.S. Senate in Massachusetts, against the current senator, Ed Markey.

Safety was Coldplay's first public release. They recorded it over a weekend in May 1998. The band and their manager, Phil Harvey, paid about £1500 for it. Only around 50 copies reached record stores. Most of the copies were given to record companies, friends, and family. The songs from this EP appear unchanged in Coldplay's later releases. "Bigger Stronger" and "Such a Rush" are on "The Blue Room EP." "No More Keeping My Feet on the Ground" was a bonus track on the single "Yellow." The lead singer, Chris Martin, was photographed by John Hilton, a friend of the band.

Shemiranat County is in Tehran Province, Iran. The county's capital is Shemiran, which is part of Tehran. In 2006, the county had 37,778 people living in 11,178 families. For the census, Shemiran and Tajrish, which are sometimes included in the county, are counted as part of Tehran. The county is divided into two districts: Rudbar-e Qasran and Lavasanat. Shemiranat County has four cities: Tajrish, Fasham, Shemshak, and Lavasan.

Penn is an American TV show. It's a sitcom with a family that doesn't get along living in the White House. Jenna Elfman, Bill Pullman, and Josh Gad star in the show. Josh Gad, along with Jason Winer and Jon Lovett, created the family and the main way the show is structured. NBC decided to make more shows in May 2012. The show came on in December 2012 and ended in March 2013. NBC stopped the show after one season on May 9, 2013.

The Barents Sea is a part of the Arctic Ocean, located north of Norway and Russia. It is split between Norwegian and Russian waters. The sea is named after Willem Barentsz, a Dutch explorer. It is a relatively shallow sea, with an average depth of a certain amount. It is important for fishing and looking for oil and gas. The Barents Sea is surrounded by the Kola Peninsula to the south, the Norwegian Sea to the west, and islands like Svalbard, Franz Josef Land, and Novaya Zemlya. Novaya Zemlya, which extends from the Ural Mountains, separates the Barents Sea from the Kara Sea. The Barents Sea has become known as "turning into the Atlantic" because of warmer temperatures. Global warming has reduced ice and changed water layers, which might affect weather in Europe and Asia.

A migraine is a type of headache that hurts a lot and usually affects one side of the head. The headache feels like a throbbing pain and can last from a few hours to three days. People with migraines might also feel sick to their stomach, vomit, or be sensitive to light, sound, or smells. Moving around makes the pain worse. In some cases, before the headache starts, people see flashes or have other visual disturbances. About one-third of people who have migraines experience something called an aura. This is a short period of vision changes that tells them a headache is coming. Sometimes, the aura happens with little or no headache. Migraines can run in families, and changes in hormones can also play a role. Before puberty, slightly more boys than girls get migraines, but two to three times more women than men have them after puberty. The risk of migraines usually decreases during pregnancy and after menopause. Doctors suggest taking simple pain relievers like ibuprofen or paracetamol for the headache, medications for nausea, and avoiding things that trigger the headache. For some people, special medications like triptans or ergotamines may be needed. Adding caffeine to the treatment can also help. There are also medicines that can prevent migraines, such as metoprolol, valproate, and topiramate. About 15% of people around the world have migraines. They often start during puberty and are worst during middle age. As of 2016, migraines are one of the leading causes of disability. An early description similar to migraines can be found in the Ebers Papyrus, written around 1500 BC in ancient Egypt. The term "migraine" comes from the Greek "hemikrania," which means "pain in half of the head."

hashish, or hash, is a drug made from the resin of the cannabis plant. It can be inhaled from a small piece, usually in a pipe, bong, vaporizer, or joint, or eaten after a process called decarboxylation. For smoking, it's often mixed with other herbs. The resin is called trichomes and it contains high levels of THC, a key ingredient. Hashish can range from 4% to 15% in purity in Europe. It can be solid or a paste-like substance, depending on how it's made. In 2008, hashish was the main form of cannabis used in Europe, while herbal cannabis was more common in North America.

A SIM card, short for Subscriber Identity Module, is a small chip used in mobile phones to store important information. It holds your phone number and helps identify you when you make calls. Some SIM cards can also save contact details. GSM phones always need SIM cards, but CDMA phones need them only for certain models. SIM cards can also be used in satellite phones, smartwatches, computers, or cameras. The SIM card is part of a bigger card called UICC, which is like a smart card made of plastic with special contacts and chips inside. SIM cards can be moved between different phones. The first UICC cards were about the size of credit cards, but they have gotten smaller over time. The electrical parts stay the same, so a larger card can be cut into a smaller one. A SIM card has a unique number (ICCID), your phone number (IMSI), security details, temporary network information, access to services, and two passwords: one for regular use (PIN) and one for unlocking (PUK). In Europe, the SIM card number (SSN) might also have an article number (IAN or EAN) for prepaid services.

Habib Mohebian, also known as Habib, was an Iranian singer-songwriter. He was born on September 27, 1947, in Tehran, Iran. In his last years of high school, he became very interested in music and playing the guitar. He entered a national competition on radio and TV and was chosen as one of 16 candidates. After two years of training, he joined the military and performed in officer clubs and throughout Iran. Habib then lived in the provinces of Western and Eastern Azerbaijan and eventually moved to Tehran. Later, he went to the United States but returned to Iran in 2009. Habib passed away on June 10, 2016, in Ramsar, Mazandaran, Iran, due to a heart problem.

Guanajuato is a city and a place where people live in central Mexico. It's the capital of the state named Guanajuato. The city is part of a bigger area called the Bajío. Guanajuato is in a small valley, making its streets narrow and twisty. Most streets are narrow alleys where cars can't fit, and some are long stairs going up the mountains. Many city streets are partly or fully underground. In the historic center, there are many small squares and old buildings from the colonial times. These buildings are made of pink or green stone. Guanajuato grew because of the minerals found in the nearby mountains. During the colonial period, the city was very important because of its mines, especially the La Valenciana mine, which produced a lot of silver. The city has a museum with naturally mummified bodies found in the cemetery. It also hosts a big festival called the International Cervantino, inviting artists and performers from all over the world. Guanajuato was the place where the first battle of the Mexican War of Independence took place. The city was named a World Heritage Site in 1988.

caniformia is a group within carnivora that includes animals like dogs, bears, wolves, foxes, raccoons, badgers, seals, and mustelids. Seals, walruses, and sea lions also belong to this group. This group mainly came from North America and northern Eurasia. Caniformia is different from feliformia, which includes cat-like animals such as cats. Feliformia mostly came from Africa and southern Asia.

Florence County is in South Carolina, U.S. In 2010, it had 136, 885 people. The main city is Florence. Florence County is part of the Florence, South Carolina area. About 60% of the county's people live in towns.

Adam Lyons Schlesinger was an American musician and producer who lived from October 31, 1967, to April 1, 2020. He played many instruments and wrote songs. He won three Emmy awards, a Grammy award, and an ASCAP award. He was also nominated for Academy, Tony, and Golden Globe awards. Adam was part of the bands Fountains of Wayne, Ivy, and Tinted Windows. He also helped write songs and produce music for the band Fever High. He grew up in Manhattan and Montclair, New Jersey. Adam died during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States because of complications from the virus.
The Manitoba Liberal Party is a political party in Manitoba, Canada. It started in the late 1800s, after the province was created in 1870.

Gerald Elliot "Jerry" Heller was an American music manager and businessman. He was famous for managing West Coast rap and gangsta rap pioneers N.W.A and Eazy-E. In the 1960s and 1970s, he became well-known for bringing Elton John and Pink Floyd to America for their first big tours. He also worked with many other artists like Journey, Marvin Gaye, and Van Morrison. In the 1980s, Heller worked with R&B and hip-hop acts such as Michel'le, World Class Wreckin' Cru, J.J. Fad, The D.O.C., Egyptian Lover, and La Dream Team. He played a big part in the growth of West Coast rap music. He managed Ruthless Records with Eazy-E and signed or worked with artists like N.W.A, the Black Eyed Peas, Above the Law, The D.O.C., and Bone Thugs-n-Harmony. Later, Eazy-E introduced Dr. Dre to Ruthless Records, bringing The D.O.C. and Above the Law.

Dwijen Sharma was born on May 29, 1929, and died on September 15, 2017. He was a naturalist and science writer from Bangladesh. In 1987, he received the Bangla Academy Literary Award. In 2015, the government of Bangladesh gave him the Ekushey Padak for his work in language and literature.

Patrick Alan Nunnelee was an American businessman and politician. He served as a U.S. representative from 2011 until his death in 2015. Before that, he worked in the Mississippi State Senate from 1995 to 2011, representing the 6th district. He was a Republican.

Kathleen Marie Ireland, born on March 20, 1963, is an American model and actress who later became an author and entrepreneur. She was a supermodel in the 1980s and 1990s, famous for appearing in 13 straight "Sports Illustrated" swimsuit issues. In 1993, she started a brand marketing company called Kathy Ireland Worldwide (KIWW). This company made her one of the richest former models in the world. By 2015, she had a personal fortune of $420 million. In 2012, products from her company were worth $2 billion.

Atal Bihari Vajpayee was an Indian leader who was Prime Minister of India three times. He first served for 13 days in 1996, then for 13 months from 1998 to 1999, and had a full term from 1999 to 2004. He was a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the first non-Indian National Congress Prime Minister to complete a full term. Vajpayee was a poet and writer and served in the Indian Parliament for over 50 years, being elected ten times to the Lok Sabha and twice to the Rajya Sabha. He represented Lucknow and stopped active politics in 2009 due to health. He helped start the Bharatiya Janata Sangh (BJP) and was its president from 1968 to 1972. In 1977, Vajpayee became Minister of External Affairs under Morarji Desai. After leaving the cabinet in 1979, the Janata Party collapsed. BJP was formed in 1980 with Vajpayee as its first president. As Prime Minister, Vajpayee led nuclear tests in 1998 and tried to improve relations with Pakistan by visiting Lahore. After the Kargil War in 1999, he worked to restore ties with Musharraf. In 2014, his birthday was named Good Governance Day. He received India's highest civilian honor, the Bharat Ratna, in 2015. Vajpayee passed away on August 16, 2018, due to age-related illness.

Mashhad is the second-largest city in Iran and the capital of Khorasan-e Razavi province. It is located in the northeast of the country. In 2016, it had a population of 3,001,184, including the areas of Mashhad Taman and Torqabeh. The city is named after the shrine of Imam Reza, the eighth Shia Imam, who was buried in a village in Khorasan. This village later became known as Mashhad, meaning "place of martyrdom." Millions of pilgrims visit the shrine every year. Harun al-Rashid, an Abbasid caliph, is also buried there. Mashhad has been ruled by different groups over time. It was prosperous during the Mongol period. Mashhad is also called the City of Ferdowsi, after the Iranian poet who wrote the "Shahnameh." The poet Mehdi Akhavan-Sales and traditional singer Mohammad-Reza Shajarian are from Mashhad. They are buried in Tus, an old city considered the main origin of Mashhad. On October 30, 2009, Iran's President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad declared Mashhad to be "Iran's spiritual capital."

Angalifu, pronounced "ang-uh-leef-oo" (around 1970 - December 14, 2014), was a northern white rhinoceros at the San Diego Zoo Safari Park. At the time of his death, he was one of six living northern white rhinoceroses in the world, one of two living males, and the only male on the American continents. He lived longer than Sudan, but not Najin or Fatu. Angalifu was born in the wild around 1970. He was captured and sent to the Khartoum Zoo in Khartoum, Sudan. In 1990, he was loaned to the San Diego Zoo Safari Park. Angalifu lived there until he died of old age on December 14, 2014, at 44 years old.

Central Connecticut State University (CCSU) is a public university in New Britain, Connecticut. It was founded in 1849 as the State Normal School and is Connecticut's oldest publicly funded university. CCSU has four schools: the Ammon College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences, the School of Business, the School of Education and Professional Studies, and the School of Engineering, Science, and Technology. CCSU has 11,822 students, including 9,546 undergraduates and 2,276 graduate students. More than half of the students live off campus, and 96 percent are Connecticut residents. The school is part of the Connecticut State Colleges and Universities system (CSCU), which also includes Eastern, Western, and Southern Connecticut State Universities. Together, these universities have a total of 32,722 students.

The House of Savoy is a royal family that started in 1003 in Savoy, a historical region. The family grew stronger over time, ruling a small area north-west of Italy. By 1713, they became the absolute rulers of the Kingdom of Sicily. In 1720, they got control of Sardinia, which they ruled directly. Through a branch called Savoy-Carignano, the House of Savoy helped unite Italy in 1861 and ruled the Kingdom of Italy until 1946. They also briefly ruled the Kingdom of Spain in the 19th century. The Savoy kings of Italy were Victor Emmanuel II, Umberto I, Victor Emmanuel III, and Umberto II. Umberto II was the last king, ruling for a few weeks before the Italian Republic was declared in 1946.

In 1976, voters chose the Democratic Party's nominee for president. Former Georgia governor Jimmy Carter won the nomination through primary elections and caucuses. The Democratic National Convention, held in New York City from July 12 to 15, 1976, finalized this process.

Sir Georg Solti, born György Stern, was a Hungarian-born British conductor, famous for his work with opera companies in Munich, Frankfurt, and London, and as the music director of the Chicago Symphony Orchestra. He was born in Budapest and studied with Béla Bartók, Leó Weiner, and Ernő Dohnányi. In the 1930s, he worked as a répétiteur at the Hungarian State Opera and at the Salzburg Festival for Arturo Toscanini. Due to the rise of Nazi influence in Hungary and anti-Jewish laws, he fled in 1938. After conducting a season at the Royal Opera House in London, he went to Switzerland during World War II. There, he earned a living as a pianist. In 1946, he became the musical director of the Bavarian State Opera in Munich. In 1952, he moved to Oper Frankfurt, where he stayed for nine years. He became a citizen of West Germany in 1953. In 1961, he became the musical director of the Royal Opera Company in London, improving its standards. He became a British citizen in 1972. In 1969, he became the music director of the Chicago Symphony Orchestra, a position he held for 22 years. He then became the orchestra's music director laureate until his death. During his time, he also served as the music director of the Orchestre de Paris from 1972 to 1975 and as the principal conductor of the London Philharmonic Orchestra from 1979 to 1983. Known for his intense conducting style, he recorded many works several times over his career, producing over 250 recordings, including 45 complete opera sets. His recording of Wagner's "Der Ring des Nibelungen" is famous and was voted the greatest recording ever made twice, in 1999 and 2012. Throughout his career, he received numerous awards, including a record 31 Grammy Awards.

Justin Wakeland High School is a public high school in Frisco, Texas, United States. It is a 5A school according to the University Interscholastic League (UIL). The school is part of the Frisco Independent School District and is one of ten high schools in the district. It opened on August 14, 2006. Most sophomores and juniors came from Frisco High School because the city expanded. New freshmen mostly come from Griffin Middle School, Cobb Middle School, and Staley Middle School. In 2015, the school was rated "Met Standard" by the Texas Education Agency.

An oil is a thick, liquid substance that doesn't mix with water and is good at mixing with other oils. Oils are mostly made of carbon and hydrogen and can be easily set on fire. They also help things stick to surfaces. Most oils are liquids at room temperature and are called unsaturated lipids. Oils can come from animals, plants, or oil from the ground. They are used for cooking (like olive oil), heating (like heating oil), medicine (like mineral oil), and making things move smoothly (like motor oil). Oils are also used to make paints, plastics, and other materials. Some oils are used in religious ceremonies to clean things.

Roberto Farias was born on March 27, 1932, and died on May 14, 2018. He was a Brazilian film director, producer, and screenwriter. During his career, he directed 15 films. In 1982, his film "Pra Frente, Brasil" was shown at the 33rd Berlin International Film Festival. Farias's brother, Reginaldo Faria, is also a film director and actor. The 's' in Reginaldo's surname was added by mistake when his name was registered.
Bollène (in Provencal, called "bouleno") is a village in the Vaucluse area of Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur in southeastern France.

Sarrebourg is a town in northeastern France, in the Moselle department of Grand Est. It is located near the upper part of the Saar River. In 1895, people found an ancient building called a mithraeum at Sarrebourg, where a path from the Vosges Mountains ends.

Keminmaa is a municipality in Finland. It has a population of (unspecified) and covers an area of which some is water. The population density is unknown. Neighboring municipalities are Kemi, Simo, Tervola, and Tornio.

Noel George Williams, born on September 19, 1943, and known as King Sporty, was a Jamaican DJ, reggae musician, and record producer. He worked for the Tashamba and Konduko labels. King Sporty is famous for co-writing the song "Buffalo Soldier," which became popular thanks to Bob Marley.

In Norse mythology, Niflheim, which means "world of mist," is a cold realm. It sometimes connects with other places like Niflhel and Hel. The name "Niflheim" appears in only two texts: "Gylfaginning" and "Hrafnagaldr Óðins." Niflheim is mainly a place of ice and cold, with frozen rivers called Élivágar and a well named Hvergelmir, from which all rivers originate. According to "Gylfaginning," Niflheim was the second of two primordial realms that emerged from Ginnungagap, the icy void. The other realm was Muspelheim, the land of fire. When the cold from Niflheim mixed with the heat from Muspelheim, it created a "creative vapor." Later, Niflheim became the home of Hel, a goddess who was the daughter of Loki. It was also the afterlife for those who did not die heroically or in a notable way.

A sloppy joe is a sandwich made with ground beef or pork, onions, tomato sauce or ketchup, and seasonings like worcestershire sauce. It is served on a hamburger bun. The dish came from the United States in the early 1900s.
Paul Malékou was born on November 17, 1938. He was Gabon's foreign minister in 1968. Malékou was born in Fougamou, Gabon. From 1975 to 1983, he worked as director-general of Asecna.

The Reinheitsgebot is a set of rules about beer ingredients in Germany and former Holy Roman Empire states. A well-known version was made in Bavaria in 1516. Similar rules existed before this. Today's rules are different from the 1516 Bavarian ones.

John "Ace" Cannon, born on May 5, 1934, and died on December 6, 2018, was an American saxophonist. He played with Bill Black's band and started his solo career in 1961 with a record called "Tuff." This record reached number 17 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 in 1962. The following year, the single "Blues (Stay Away from Me)" reached number 36. In April 1965, he released "Ace Cannon Live," recorded live in Hi Records' studio, which Nick Pesce said was the first such album ever recorded. Cannon was inducted into both the Rock and Soul Hall of Fame and the Rockabilly Hall of Fame in 2000. In 2007, his hometown, Calhoun City, Mississippi, held its first annual Ace Cannon Festival. He was also inducted into the Mississippi Musicians' Hall of Fame in 2008. After traveling a lot, he moved back to Calhoun City in the late 1980s and lived there until his death. He played music many times each year and enjoyed playing golf at his home course. He passed away at his home on December 6, 2018, at the age of 84.

an Buruk, born on October 19, 1973, is a Turkish football manager and former player. He currently manages Istanbul Başakşehir in Süper Lig. Buruk played as a midfielder for Galatasaray, Inter Milan, Beşiktaş, and Istanbul B.B. He also played for the Turkey national team 56 times.
George Foster Peabody was an American banker and philanthropist. He lived from July 27, 1852, to March 4, 1938.

Michael Corbett Shannon, born on August 7, 1974, is an American actor, producer, director, and musician. He was nominated twice for the Academy Award for best supporting actor for his roles in "Revolutionary Road" (2008) and "Nocturnal Animals" (2016). He also received Screen Actors Guild and Golden Globe nominations for his role in "99 Homes" (2014) and a Tony Award nomination for "Long Day's Journey into Night" (2016). Shannon started his film career in 1993 with "Groundhog Day" and became famous for his role in "8 Mile" (2002). He has acted in both comedies and dramas, such as "Pearl Harbor" (2001), "Bad Boys II" (2003), "Bug" (2006), "Before the Devil Knows You're Dead" (2007), "The Grey" (2011), "The Iceman" (2012), "Premium Rush" (2012), "Man of Steel" (2013), "The Shape of Water" (2017), and "Knives Out" (2019). He often works with director Jeff Nichols, appearing in all his films: "Shotgun Stories" (2007), "Take Shelter" (2011), "Mud" (2012), "Midnight Special" (2016), and "Loving" (2016). He is also known for his role as Nelson Van Alden in the HBO series "Boardwalk Empire" (2010-2014), for which he was nominated for three Screen Actors Guild awards.

Osama bin Laden, the founder of al-Qaeda, a militant group, was killed in Pakistan on May 2, 2011, around 1:00 AM PKT (20:00 UTC, May 1) by U.S. Navy SEALs. The operation, called Operation Neptune Spear, was led by the CIA and involved other special forces. SEAL Team Six, the 160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment, known as the Night Stalkers, and CIA operators participated. This operation ended a 10-year search for bin Laden, who was involved in the September 11 attacks on the U.S. The SEALs took bin Laden's body to Afghanistan for identification and buried it at sea within 24 hours, following Islamic tradition. Al-Qaeda confirmed his death on May 6 through posts on their websites and vowed revenge. Other militant groups in Pakistan also promised to retaliate against the U.S. and Pakistan. Most Americans supported the raid. However, some criticized not capturing bin Laden alive, even though he was unarmed. The U.S. did not release any photos or DNA evidence of his death to the public. After the raid, the Pakistani government formed a commission to investigate the incident. The resulting report revealed that Pakistan's military and intelligence agencies failed to find bin Laden for nine years.

Suzy Delair, born Suzette Pierrette Delaire on December 31, 1917, and died on March 15, 2020, was a French actress, dancer, singer, and comedian who performed in vaudeville.

Gary Charles Peters Sr., born on December 1, 1958, is an American politician. He has been serving as a U.S. senator from Michigan since 2015. Peters is a member of the Democratic Party. Before that, he was a U.S. representative from 2013 to 2015. The district he represented includes parts of Detroit, Grosse Pointe, Hamtramck, Southfield, and Pontiac. Peters worked in the U.S. Navy Reserve and was an investment advisor for 22 years. He also had a short time working in academia. He served on the Rochester Hills city council from 1991 and represented the 14th district in the Michigan Senate from 1995 to 2002. In 2002, he ran for Michigan attorney general as a Democrat but lost to the Republican Mike Cox. Peters then became the commissioner of the Michigan Lottery under Governor Jennifer Granholm from 2003 to 2008. He left this job to run for Congress. In 2014, Peters was elected to the U.S. Senate seat that was vacated by retiring Democrat Carl Levin. He won the Democratic primary without opposition and defeated Republican Terri Lynn Land in the general election. Peters was the only non-incumbent Democrat to win a Senate election that year.
A playwright is someone who writes plays.

A text editor is a computer program that edits plain text. Sometimes, people call these programs "notepad" software, similar to Microsoft Notepad. Text editors come with operating systems and software development tools. They can be used to change various files, like configuration files, documentation files, and programming code.

Hans Gericke was an architect and urban planner from Germany. He was born on July 27, 1912, in Magdeburg, which was in the Province of Saxony, Prussia, part of the German Empire. In 1953, he became the deputy director of the institutes for the theory and history of architecture at the German Academy of Architecture. From 1958 to 1965, he worked as a chief architect in East Berlin, which was in East Germany. He received many awards for his work. Gericke passed away on February 15, 2014, at the age of 101.

The University of New South Wales (UNSW; now branded as UNSW Sydney since 2017) is a public research university in Sydney's Kensington suburb. In 2012, UNSW had the highest median ATAR score of any university in New South Wales (NSW) and attracted the most top-500 students from the state. Established in 1949, UNSW ranks fourth in Australia and 43rd in the world according to the 2020 QS World University Rankings. The university has nine faculties and offers bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees. Its main campus is in Kensington, about 7 km (4.3 miles) from Sydney's central business district. The Creative Arts faculty, known as UNSW Art & Design, is in Paddington. UNSW Canberra is at the Australian Defence Force Academy in Canberra. Subcampuses are in the CBD, Randwick, and Coogee. Research stations are spread across New South Wales. UNSW is part of the Group of Eight, a group of top Australian research universities, and Universitas 21, a global network of research universities. It has partnerships with over 200 universities worldwide.
Sigourney is a city in Keokuk County, Iowa, United States. In 2010, it had 2,059 people. Sigourney is also the county seat of Keokuk County.

Hurricane Maria was a very strong category 5 hurricane that hit Dominica, St. Croix, and Puerto Rico in September 2017. It was the worst natural disaster ever recorded in those islands and the deadliest Atlantic hurricane since 2004. It was also the most intense tropical cyclone in 2017. Hurricane Maria was the 13th named storm, the 8th straight hurricane, the 4th major hurricane, and the 2nd category 5 hurricane of the 2017 Atlantic hurricane season. At its worst, it caused a lot of damage and many deaths in the northeastern Caribbean. It made things harder to recover from in areas that had already been hit by Hurricane Irma. Maria started from a wave of warm, wet air and became a tropical storm on September 16, east of the Lesser Antilles. It quickly got stronger as it approached the islands. It became a category 5 hurricane just before hitting Dominica on September 18, the first category 5 hurricane to hit the island. After weakening slightly over Dominica, it reached its strongest point over the eastern Caribbean with winds of 175 mph and a pressure of 908 mbar. On September 20, it weakened as an eyewall replaced its eye, becoming a high-end category 4 hurricane when it hit Puerto Rico. Interaction with land weakened it further, but it regained strength as it moved northeast of the Bahamas. It moved slowly to the north and weakened to a tropical storm on September 28. It accelerated and became extratropical over the open Atlantic on September 30 and dissipated by October 2. Hurricane Maria caused very bad damage to Dominica, which lost all communication. Most buildings and infrastructure were damaged or destroyed, and the island's trees were mostly gone. Guadeloupe and Martinique also had flooding, damaged roofs, and uprooted trees. Puerto Rico suffered catastrophic damage and a big crisis. Most of the island's population faced flooding and a lack of resources. The storm caused the worst electrical blackout in US history, and many homes and businesses still had no power in June 2018. Maria was the third strong hurricane to hit the Leeward Islands in two weeks after Hurricane Irma and Hurricane Jose passed close by. After almost a year, Puerto Rico updated its death toll from 64 to 2,975, making the total 3,059. This includes 2,975 in Puerto Rico, 65 in Dominica, 5 in the Dominican Republic, 4 in Guadeloupe, 4 in the US, 3 in the US Virgin Islands, and 3 in Haiti. Hurricane Maria is the deadliest hurricane in Dominica since 1834 and in Puerto Rico since 1899. The initial death count of 64 was revised because doctors did not know how to properly report deaths after the hurricane.

The bishop is a piece in chess. Each player has two bishops at the start. One bishop begins near the king, the other near the queen. White bishops start on c1 and f1. Black bishops start on c8 and f8.

Alexander Pope, born on May 21, 1688, and died on May 30, 1744, is considered one of the greatest English poets, especially from the early 1700s. He is known for his satirical and discursive poetry, including "The Rape of the Lock," "The Dunciad," and "An Essay on Criticism." He also translated Homer. Pope is the second most quoted writer in the English language, after Shakespeare, as noted in "The Oxford Dictionary of Quotations." Some of his verses have even become common sayings (e.g., "damning with faint praise"). He mastered the heroic couplet, a form of poetry. Pope faced many challenges. He was a Catholic, which meant he couldn't live near London or go to public school or university because of strict laws. He was mostly self-taught, taught to read by his aunt and learning languages like French, Italian, Latin, and Greek on his own. He discovered Homer at age six. As a child, he survived being trampled by a cow but later developed tuberculosis in his spine and suffered from severe headaches. In 1709, at 21, he published "Pastorals," his first major poems, which made him famous. By 23, he had written "An Essay on Criticism," published in 1711, a poetic manifesto that gained him many important friends, like Joseph Addison and Richard Steele, who were writing "The Spectator." John Dennis, upset by a satirical portrait of him, hated Pope for life and criticized him, but Pope responded with satire. Pope's most famous work, "The Rape of the Lock," published in 1712, explores themes of individualism and materialism. In 1717, he published poems about love, including "Verses to the Memory of an Unfortunate Lady" and "Eloisa to Abelard." He never married but had a strong friendship with Lady M. Montagu and Martha Blount. As a satirist, Pope had enemies. He carried pistols once because of his sharp satires. After 1738, he mostly worked on revising and expanding his poem "The Dunciad." In 1742, he replaced one character with another, Colley Cibber, as the "King of Dunces," but the real target was the politician Robert Walpole. His health declined, and on his deathbed, his doctor told him he was feeling better, to which Pope replied, "Here am I, dying of a hundred good symptoms."
macaye is a commune in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department in southwestern France.

Victor Amadeus II, born on May 14, 1666, and died on October 31, 1732, was the Duke of Savoy from 1675 to 1730. He also had other titles like Marquis of Saluzzo, Duke of Montferrat, Prince of Piedmont, and Count of Aosta, Moriana, and Nice. Louis XIV arranged his marriage to keep French influence in Savoy, but Victor Amadeus soon moved away from French control. When his father died in 1675, his mother, Marie Jeanne Baptiste of Nemours, was the regent. She remained influential until 1684 when Victor Amadeus forced her to stop being involved. Victor Amadeus fought in the War of the Spanish Succession and became King of Sicily in 1713. However, he had to give up this title and became King of Sardinia instead. Victor Amadeus left a big cultural impact in Turin, rebuilding the royal palace and other important buildings there. He is buried in the Basilica of Superga.

Antonio Maceda Francés was born on May 16, 1957. He was a Spanish retired footballer. Although he was a central defender, he was famous for scoring goals. He began his career with Sporting de Gijón and ended it with Real Madrid, where he struggled with injuries. Maceda played for the Spanish national team about 40 times. He also participated in two World Cups and the 1984 European Championship.

Johan Cédric Micoud, born on July 24, 1973, was a French footballer. He mostly played as an attacking midfielder. People thought he was skilled and good at taking free kicks. He played professionally for 16 years, mainly in Italy and Germany. Micoud played for France about 20 times and was part of the national team for the 2002 World Cup and Euro 2000. He helped France win the Euro 2000 tournament.

The Delaware River is a big river on the eastern coast of the United States. It flows through four states: Delaware, New Jersey, New York, and Pennsylvania. The river starts in the Catskill Mountains in New York and empties into Delaware Bay, where its waters enter the Atlantic Ocean near Cape May, New Jersey, and Cape Henlopen, Delaware. Including Delaware Bay, the river is about long. The Delaware River is part of the "Great Waters" recognized by the America's Great Waters Coalition. It has two main branches. The west branch starts near Mount Jefferson in Schoharie County, and the east branch begins at Grand Gorge in Delaware County. These branches meet near Hancock in Delaware County and form the main river, which flows south. The river forms borders between Pennsylvania and New York, all of the border between New Jersey and Pennsylvania, and most of the border between Delaware and New Jersey. At Morrisville, Pennsylvania, and Trenton, New Jersey, the river meets the tidal section, where it was used for shipping and transportation, helping the growth of cities like Trenton, Camden, and Philadelphia. Before European settlers arrived, the Lenape Native Americans called the river Lenapewihittuk, meaning "Lenape River," or Kithanne, meaning "the largest river." In 1609, a Dutch expedition led by Henry Hudson visited the river. Hudson, an English navigator, was looking for a route to China but his exploration led to Dutch settlement in North America. Early Dutch and Swedish settlements were established along the lower part of the river and Delaware Bay. Both called the river the "South River," compared to the Hudson River, known as the "North River." After the English took control in 1664, the river was named "Delaware" after Sir Thomas West, 3rd Baron De La Warr, who was the first royal governor of Virginia and protected the colony during the first Anglo-Powhatan War.

Avram Noam Chomsky, born on December 7, 1928, is an American linguist, philosopher, and political activist. He is known as the father of modern linguistics and a major figure in analytic philosophy. Chomsky is also one of the founders of cognitive science. He teaches at MIT and the University of Arizona. He has written over 100 books on topics like linguistics, politics, and war. Born to Jewish parents in Philadelphia, Chomsky grew interested in anarchism from bookstores in New York. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania. In 1955, he earned his doctorate with his theory of transformational grammar. He began teaching at MIT in the same year. His 1957 book, "Syntactic Structures," changed how people study language. He also developed theories like universal grammar and minimalist programs. Chomsky criticized behaviorism, especially B.F. Skinner's work. He opposed the U.S. involvement in the Vietnam War, writing "The Responsibility of Intellectuals" in 1967. Chomsky was arrested for his activism and was on President Nixon's enemies list. He worked on exposing the Indonesian occupation of East Timor and supported freedom of speech, including for holocaust denial. Since retiring from MIT, Chomsky has continued to speak out against things like the 2003 Iraq war and the Occupy movement. He has influenced many fields of study and is known for his views on U.S. foreign policy and capitalism. His ideas are popular in anti-capitalist and anti-imperialist movements but have been criticized as anti-American.

Frederick Nelson Pyatt, born on September 9, 1953, is a Canadian former professional ice hockey player. He was born in Port Arthur, Ontario. In 1973, Pyatt was chosen by both the Detroit Red Wings of the National Hockey League and the Minnesota Fighting Saints of the World Hockey Association. He also played for the Washington Capitals and the Colorado Rockies. Pyatt is the father of Jesse and former NHL players Tom and Taylor Pyatt.
Higden is a town in Cleburne County, Arkansas, United States. In 2010, it had 120 people.

The health services functional constituency, previously known as the health constituency, is a group in Hong Kong's Legislative Council elections. It was first created for the 1988 Legislative Council election. This group includes health professionals. It has one of the largest electorates among functional constituencies. The group has been controlled by pro-democracy candidates since it was formed.
Plougastel-Daoulas is a commune in Finistère, which is in Brittany, in Northwestern France.

Hara Pattanaik, also known as Hari Patnaik, was an Odia film actor, director, and screenplay writer. He acted in over 60 Odia movies and directed about 19 others. Pattanaik helped introduce other actors like Anubhav Mohanty, Sabyasachi Mishra, and Babushaan. He passed away from cancer on January 13, 2015.

Wandsworth is a borough in southwest London and part of inner London. It borders Lambeth to the east, Merton and Kingston upon Thames to the south, Richmond upon Thames to the west, and across the River Thames, Hammersmith and Fulham, Kensington and Chelsea, and Westminster. The local authority is Wandsworth London Borough Council.

The Pauline epistles, also called the letters of Paul, are thirteen books in the New Testament that are attributed to Paul the Apostle. Some of these letters might not actually be written by him. These letters are some of the earliest known Christian documents. They tell us about early Christian beliefs and debates. The Pauline epistles are important for understanding Christian beliefs and ethics. The letter to the Hebrews, even though it doesn’t have Paul’s name, was long thought to be written by him. However, many now believe it was not. Most experts agree that Paul wrote seven of these letters, but four others might not have been written by him. Two letters might also be written by someone else. Paul may have had a secretary who helped write some of these letters. Modern editions usually put the Pauline epistles between the Acts of the Apostles and the Catholic epistles. However, some old Greek manuscripts place the Pauline epistles at the end of the New Testament.

Halloween is an American horror series with eleven movies, plus novels, comic books, toys, and a video game. The movies mostly focus on a serial killer named Michael Myers. Michael was put in a hospital as a child because he killed his sister, Judith Myers. Fifteen years later, he escapes and goes to the fictional town of Haddonfield, Illinois, to hurt people on Halloween. The first movie, "Halloween," came out in 1978 and was made by John Carpenter. It inspired many other horror movies. Eight more movies followed. In 2007, Rob Zombie made a new version of the first movie. Two years later, he made another movie based on his version. In 2018, a new movie that doesn't connect to the other movies was released. Two more movies, "Halloween Kills" and "Halloween Ends," are coming out in 2021 and 2022. Together, all the movies earned over $640 million. The original movie and the 2018 movie got good reviews, but the other movies didn't do as well.

Francis George Steiner, who lived from April 23, 1929, to February 3, 2020, was a literary critic, essayist, philosopher, novelist, and educator. He wrote about language, literature, and their relationship to society, as well as the impact of the Holocaust. An article in The Guardian called him a "polyglot and polymath." His admirers consider him one of the great thinkers in today's literary world. A. S. Byatt, an English novelist, described him as a "late, late, late Renaissance man, a European metaphysician with an instinct for the driving ideas of our time." Harriet Harvey-Wood, a former literature director of the British Council, said Steiner was a "magnificent lecturer—prophetic and doom-laden [who] would turn up with half a page of scribbled notes, and never refer to them." Steiner taught at the University of Geneva from 1974 to 1994, at the University of Oxford from 1994 to 1995, as a professor of poetry at Harvard University from 2001 to 2002, and was an extraordinary fellow at Churchill College, Cambridge, since 1969.

Anseba Region is one of the six areas in northern Eritrea. Its capital and biggest city is Keren. The region is named after the Anseba River, which flows through much of it. The average height is around 1,800 meters. It's warmest in May, with temperatures up to 38°C, and coldest in December to February, dropping to freezing. Anseba gets about 250 mm of rain and the soil is good for farming. In 2005, there were 549,000 people living there, up from 484,200 in 2001. The population grew by 11.80%. The region covers 23,200 km², with about 23 people per km². The country and Anseba Region are ruled by the People's Front for Democracy and Justice (PFDJ), which started as the Eritrean Liberation Front. Elections are held regularly, but only PFDJ can run. Everyone, regardless of ethnicity or religion, can vote. However, other parties cannot compete, and PFDJ representatives oversee the elections.
Here are people who were born, grew up in, or became famous while living in the state of New Hampshire.

Jamstik is a brand of small, portable guitars that connect to apps. Zivix, a music technology company in Minneapolis, Minnesota, makes Jamstik. They are made in the United States, designed in Minneapolis and produced in South Dakota.

The House of Windsor is the royal family that rules the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth countries. In 1901, after Queen Victoria's son Edward became king, the family name changed from Saxe-Coburg and Gotha to Windsor because of how people felt about Germany during World War I. Since then, four British kings and queens have been from the House of Windsor: George V, Edward VIII, George VI, and Elizabeth II. Today, the Queen of Windsor is the head of state in sixteen countries, including the UK, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. She also has connections to three Crown Dependencies, fourteen British Overseas Territories, and two associated states of New Zealand.

Kimberley Gail Marsh, born on June 13, 1976, is an English actress and TV presenter. She gained fame in 2001 by joining the band Hear'say after appearing on "Popstars," a reality TV show. Hear'say had some success, with two UK number one singles and an album that topped the charts. In 2002, Marsh left the band to focus on a solo career. She released an album called "Standing Tall" in 2003, which reached number nine in the UK charts and had two top ten singles. From April 2006 to December 2019, Marsh acted as Michelle Connor in the TV show "Coronation Street." She won awards for her performances, including Best Newcomer at the 2007 British Soap Awards and the 2007 National Television Awards, and Best Female Dramatic Performance at the 2017 British Soap Awards. In 2010, she was fourth place in "Popstar to Operastar," a show where popular singers learned to sing opera.

Monday Night Raw is an American wrestling show. It airs on USA Network every Monday from 8:00 to 11:00 PM EST in the United States. Raw is also the name of the wrestling brand where wrestlers work. The show first came out on January 11, 1993, and it is one of the two main shows, along with Friday Night Smackdown. Raw has the longest history of any weekly wrestling show. In 2000, Raw moved to Spike TV from USA Network. It went back to USA Network in 2005 and is still there. All episodes of Raw can be watched on the WWE Network. Recent episodes are available 30 days after they air. Since 1993, Raw has been shown live in 208 different places in 11 countries: the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Afghanistan, Iraq, South Africa, Germany, Japan, Italy, and Mexico.

The Animals were an English band that played rhythm and blues and rock music. They formed in Newcastle upon Tyne in the early 1960s. In 1964, they moved to London after gaining fame. Known for their strong, bluesy sound and Eric Burdon's deep voice, they had big hits like "House of the Rising Sun," "We Got to Get Out of This Place," and "Don't Let Me Be Misunderstood." They made tough, rock songs and also played rhythm and blues. They were part of the British bands that became popular in the United States. The band members changed a lot in the mid-1960s and had problems with business. After changing their name to Eric Burdon and the Animals, they moved to California and became successful with psychedelic and hard rock music. They had hits like "San Francisco Nights" and "When I Was Young." The band broke up at the end of the 1960s. In 1968, the original members played together for a one-time concert. They also played together briefly in 1975 and 1983. Some of the original members have played together under different names since then. The Animals were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1994.

Salt Lake County is in Utah, a U.S. state. In 2010, it had 1,029,655 people, and by July 1, 2019, the number grew to 1,160,437. Salt Lake City is the biggest city and the county seat. It's also the capital of Utah. Salt Lake County was formed in 1850. It's the 37th most populous county in the U.S. and one of only four in the Rocky Mountains with over 700,000 people, along with Denver, El Paso, and Clark counties. Salt Lake County covers parts of the Salt Lake Valley, the Oquirrh Mountains, and the Wasatch Range. It also includes part of the Great Salt Lake. The county is known for its ski resorts, and Salt Lake City hosted the 2002 Winter Olympics. Salt Lake County is central to the Salt Lake City metropolitan area.

Charles Edward Daniels was an American singer, songwriter, and musician. He was famous for his music in southern rock, country, and bluegrass. His most famous song was "The Devil Went Down to Georgia," which was a number-one hit in country music. Daniels started singing and playing music in the 1950s. He was recognized for his talent and was inducted into the Cheyenne Frontier Days Hall of Fame in 2002, the Grand Ole Opry in 2008, the Musicians Hall of Fame and Museum in 2009, and the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2016. He lived from October 28, 1936, to July 6, 2020.

sirdavidia is a genus of flowering plants. It was described on February 4, 2015, by scientists from France, Gabon, and Cameroon. The scientists are Thomas L.P. Couvreur, Raoul Niangadouma, Bonaventure Sonké, and Hervé Sauquet. They named the genus in honor of Sir David Attenborough. The type species, sirdavidia solannona, was found in Gabon's Crystal Mountains National Park on November 15, 2013, at elevations between 300 and 600 meters. The species name comes from the flower's similarity to those of the solanum plants.
Angkaliya Curtis, born around 1928, is an Australian Aboriginal artist. She paints animals from the central Australian desert.
Thirty-two is the number that comes after thirty-one and before thirty-three.

La Bollène-Vésubie is a town in the Alpes-Maritimes area, which is in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur region of southeastern France. The people who live there are called bollénois. In the Niçois dialect of langue d'oc, the town is called la Boulèna, and the inhabitants are called "lu boulenasc".

Silent Hill: Downpour is a survival horror video game. Vatra Games made it, and Konami Digital Entertainment released it. It's the eighth game in the Silent Hill series and came out in March 2012. The story takes place in Silent Hill, the made-up American town in the series. The main character, Murphy Pendleton, goes into the town and enters another world. He uncovers his own hidden memories. The game is played from a third-person perspective and uses 3D graphics. Critics thought the game was good, praising its atmosphere and story. They also liked that it returned to the series' focus on survival and exploration. However, they criticized the monsters, combat, and technical problems. Since its release, a fix has been released to address these issues.

Toy Purina lived from 1760 to 1799. She was a medicine woman from the Tongva nation, also called Gabrieliño because of their connection to San Gabriel Mission. Toy Purina opposed Spanish missionaries who ruled California. In 1785, she helped plan a rebellion against San Gabriel Mission. She recruited six of the eight villages that joined the attack.
killing me softly could mean: gradually making me sad or unhappy.

Wii Music is a music game for Nintendo's Wii console. It came out in Japan and North America in October 2008, and in Europe and Australia the next month. The game is part of Nintendo's Touch! Generations brand and the Wii series. In Wii Music, you control members of an on-screen band and make new arrangements of popular songs. You choose instruments like guitars, drums, or keyboards and use the Wii Remote and Nunchuk to play them. The game lets you try different ways to play songs without scoring you. Nintendo said Wii Music brings the fun of music to your home without needing expensive lessons. It was one of the first games shown for the Wii, first shown in 2006 and then more details in 2008. When the game came out, some people liked it, but others didn't. It got scores of 64.34% on Gamerankings and 63 on Metacritic. People said it was easy to play and had not-so-accurate controls. Its music was mostly old and free. Because of this, Wii Music is seen as less successful than other Wii games, selling about 2.65 million copies by March 2009.
