UGT, or uses and gratifications theory, helps us understand why and how people choose media to meet their needs. This theory focuses on what people do with media, not what media does to people. It suggests that media is widely available, and people choose to use it to gain knowledge, relax, stay connected with others, have fun, or escape. Unlike other theories, UGT believes that people are not just passive consumers of media. Instead, they actively decide what media to use and how to integrate it into their lives. According to UGT, people choose media to satisfy their desires and needs, which means media competes with other sources for attention. Today, UGT is useful because it provides a way for researchers to look at media choices and impacts.

Liberty X, originally called Liberty, were a British-Irish group with members Michelle Heaton, Tony Lndon, Kevin Simm, Jessica Taylor, and Kelli Young. They formed after the "Popstars" ITV talent show because the five finalists, including Liberty X, didn't make it into the group Hear'say. Liberty X had ten top-20 UK singles and several hits worldwide, more successful than Hear'say. They had to change their name due to another act using the same name. Liberty X released their first album "Thinking It Over" on May 27, 2002. Their biggest hit "Just a Little" was very successful internationally. They released their second album "Being Somebody" on November 3, 2003, but it was not as successful as their first. The group disbanded in early 2007 but reformed in 2008 for a one-off performance in Belfast. In 2012, Liberty X reformed for an ITV2 documentary series "The Big Reunion" with other groups. They planned to give fans a proper goodbye but ended up signing with 365 Artists Management for their future.

Splosion Man is a 2.5D action platform video game. It was made by Twisted Pixel Games for the Xbox 360. You can get it through Xbox Live Arcade, which lets you download games. It came out on July 22, 2009, during the 2009 Xbox Live Summer of Arcade. In the game, you play as Splosion Man, who is an escaped science experiment. He can explode many times. You control him to go through obstacles and traps to leave the fictional Big Science laboratory. Splosion Man got good reviews. Xbox Live players chose it as the best original game for Xbox Live Arcade in 2009. It was also listed as the 11th best game in the history of Xbox Live Arcade by IGN. In 2009, it was the 13th best-selling game. By the end of 2011, it had sold over 487,000 copies. A sequel called Ms. Splosion Man came out on July 13, 2011.

Hanau is a town in Main-Kinzig-Kreis, Hesse, Germany. It is about 25 kilometers east of Frankfurt am Main and part of the Frankfurt Rhine-Main area. Hanau has a railway junction and a port on the Main River, making it an important transport center. The town is famous as the birthplace of Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm and Franciscus Sylvius. Since the 16th century, Hanau has been a center for working with precious metals, with many goldsmiths. It is home to Heraeus, a large family-owned company in Germany. Hanau used to be the seat of the Counts of Hanau. During World War II, a British air raid in 1945 caused a firestorm, killing one-sixth of the remaining population and destroying most of the old city. In 1963, Hanau hosted the third Hessentag state festival. From 2005 to 2020, Hanau was the administrative center of Main-Kinzig-Kreis. On February 19, 2020, a gunman attacked two hookah lounges in Hanau, killing nine people from outside Germany and also shot his mother before killing himself.

Joseph René Marcel Pronovost was a Canadian ice hockey player and coach, born on June 15, 1930, and passed away on April 26, 2015. He played as a defenceman for 20 NHL seasons from 1950 to 1970. Pronovost played for the Detroit Red Wings and Toronto Maple Leafs, appearing in 1,206 games. He was a top defenceman and was chosen for four NHL All-Star teams, playing in 11 All-Star games. He was part of four Stanley Cup-winning teams with the Red Wings, including their first in 1950. He won another Stanley Cup with the Maple Leafs in 1967. Pronovost was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame as a player in 1978. After retiring, Pronovost became a coach. He coached the junior Hull Olympiques and Windsor Spitfires for several seasons. He was the head coach of the Chicago Cougars for the World Hockey Association's first season in 1972-73 and coached the Buffalo Sabres for 104 games between 1977 and 1978. He was also an assistant coach for the Red Wings. Pronovost worked for the NHL Central Scouting Bureau for five years until 1990. He then became a scout for the New Jersey Devils, a role he kept until he helped the Devils win three Stanley Cups, including the last one in 2003. His career spanned 53 years between his first and last Stanley Cup wins, a record.

Barsha Lekhi, born on May 5, 1993, in Saptari, Nepal, is a beauty queen and environmental activist. She won Miss Nepal 2016. In 2016, she also got the Missosology People's Choice Award. She represented Nepal at the Miss International contest in Japan in October 2016. Barsha studied environmental science at Patan Multiple Campus. She worked for the NEFIN-REDD/CC partnership program. Currently, she is studying for her master's degree in environmental science at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

The Standard Model is a theory that describes three fundamental forces in the universe: electromagnetic, weak, and strong interactions. It doesn't include gravity. This model also lists all known elementary particles. It was created over many years in the latter half of the 20th century by scientists around the world. By the mid-1970s, it was mostly complete. The existence of quarks confirmed it. Later, the top quark, tau neutrino, and Higgs boson were discovered, which further supported the model. The model has also accurately predicted properties of weak neutral currents and W and Z bosons. While it works well, it can't explain everything. It doesn't fully explain why the universe has more matter than antimatter, doesn't include a complete theory of gravity, and doesn't account for the universe's accelerating expansion. It also lacks a particle to explain dark matter. The model doesn't fully describe neutrino behavior either. Scientists continue to develop more complex theories based on the Standard Model to explain unexplained phenomena like dark matter and neutrino changes.
This is a list of 309 communes in the Nièvre department of France.
Vincenzo Bettiza was born on June 7, 1927, and died on July 28, 2017. He was an Italian novelist, journalist, and politician who was born in Yugoslavia.

Robie Creek is a place in Boise County, Idaho, United States. The population was 1,162 in 2010. Robie Creek has a recreation area with swimming, a play area for children, and a boat launch and dock. There are toilet facilities, but no cell phone service.
His comic books tell stories about modern East Asian history, but they show Japan in a very good light.

In quantum field theory, the Casimir effect and the Casimir–Polder force are forces coming from a quantized field. They are named after the Dutch physicist Hendrik Casimir, who predicted them in 1948. In 1997, an experiment by S. Lamoreaux measured these forces, getting within 5% of the predicted value. The Casimir effect happens because conductors and dielectrics change the energy of the electromagnetic field. Since the energy value depends on the shapes and positions of these materials, the Casimir effect causes forces between them. Any material that supports vibrations has a similar effect. For example, beads on a string, or plates in turbulent water or gas, show the Casimir force. In modern physics, the Casimir effect is important for the chiral bag model of nucleons. It is also significant in some areas of micro- and nanotechnology.
John Samuel Mbiti, born in Kenya, was a Christian philosopher and writer. He became an ordained Anglican priest and later a canon.
Babbie is a town in Covington County, Alabama, United States. In 2010, it had 603 people. Babbie became a town in 1957.
Central pier is one of three piers in Blackpool, England. It was built in 1868.

William Friedkin, born on August 29, 1935, is an American film and TV director, producer, and writer. He is famous for the "New Hollywood" movement in the 1970s. Friedkin began his career with documentaries in the early 1960s. He is best known for directing the action movie "The French Connection" in 1971, which won five Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Best Adapted Screenplay, and Best Director. His other famous work is the horror movie "The Exorcist" from 1973, for which he was nominated for Best Director. Other films he directed include "The Boys in the Band" in 1970, "Sorcerer" in 1977, "Cruising" in 1980, "To Live and Die in LA" in 1985, "Bug" in 2006, and "Killer Joe" in 2011.

"What I've Done" is a song by American rock band Linkin Park. It was released as the first single from their album "Minutes to Midnight" in 2007 and is the sixth track. The song is in the key of G minor. It came out as a radio single on April 1, 2007, as a digital download on April 2, and as a CD single on April 30, 2007. A live version of the song was nominated for "Best Hard Rock Performance" at the 52nd Grammy Awards but didn't win. The song also serves as the main theme for the 2007 science fiction film "Transformers" and is on the album "Minutes to Midnight" (2007). It has sold five times platinum in the US and is the band's most commercially successful song, though not the most famous. "What I've Done" was included in the video game "Guitar Hero World Tour" and later in a Linkin Park DLC pack for "Rock Band 3". The song is also a bonus track for the UK single of "Iridescent." An instrumental version is used by Sky UK as background music for their interactive services.

Wittmund is a "district" in northwest Lower Saxony, Germany. It is located on the North Sea coast in East Friesland. The neighboring districts, going clockwise from the east, are Friesland, Leer, and Aurich.

"A combatant" is someone who can fight in a war. According to article 43(2) of Additional Protocol I to the Geneva Conventions of 1949, members of a country's military forces are combatants and can take part in fighting. Combatants are usually allowed to be attacked by the other side, just because they are combatants, to stop them from helping their own side. Besides fighting, if captured, combatants have the right to be treated as prisoners of war. All combatants must follow the rules of war. Breaking these rules does not mean a combatant stops being a combatant or loses the right to be treated as a prisoner of war if they are captured.

Oliver Burgess Meredith (November 16, 1907 – September 9, 1997) was an American actor, director, producer, and writer. He was active for over six decades and was considered a great actor. A member of the Actors Studio, he won several Emmy awards. He was the first male actor to win the Saturn Award for best supporting actor twice and was nominated for two Academy Awards. Meredith became famous for his roles as George Milton in "Of Mice and Men" (1939), Ernie Pyle in "The Story of G.I. Joe" (1945), and the narrator in "A Walk in the Sun" (1945). Later in his career, he appeared on "The Twilight Zone" and played the villain the Penguin in "Batman" (1960s) and the boxing trainer Mickey Goldmill in the "Rocky" films. He was nominated for the Academy Award for best supporting actor for his roles in "The Day of the Locust" (1975) and "Rocky" (1976). Meredith also acted in comedies like "Foul Play" (1978) and fantasy films like "Clash of the Titans" (1981). He narrated many films and documentaries, including one in 1983. He was known for his roles in plays by Shakespeare, O'Neill, and Beckett.

Melissa Ellen Gilbert, born on May 8, 1964, is an American actress, director, and producer. She was also the president of the Screen Actors Guild from 2001 to 2005. Gilbert began her acting career as a child in the 1960s, appearing in commercials and TV shows. From 1974 to 1984, she played Laura Ingalls Wilder on the TV series "Little House on the Prairie." During this time, she also starred in popular TV movies like "The Diary of Anne Frank" and "The Miracle Worker." As an adult, she continued to act in TV movies and did voice work for animations, such as playing Barbara Gordon/Batgirl. In 2009, she appeared in the musical "Little House on the Prairie" on stage. In 2012, she was a contestant on "Dancing with the Stars." Her autobiography "Prairie Tale: A Memoir" came out in 2009. She also wrote children's stories and a cookbook. Gilbert tried to become a member of Congress in 2016 but had to stop because of injuries from an accident in 2012.

Eduardo Horacio Laborde was an Argentine rugby player. He played three games for the national team "Los Pumas" in the 1991 Rugby World Cup. Eduardo died in February 2015. A bicycle he was riding crashed into another vehicle in the town of Pinamar.

Actinium is a chemical element with the symbol Ac and atomic number 89. It was first discovered by André-Louis Debierne in 1899. Friedrich Oskar Giesel later found it independently in 1902 but didn't know it was already known and named it emanium. Actinium is part of the actinide series, a group of 15 similar elements between actinium and lawrencium in the periodic table. Sometimes, actinium is considered the first of the 7th-period transition metals, though lawrencium is less often given that position. Actinium is a soft, silvery-white metal that reacts quickly with oxygen and moisture in the air, forming a white coating of actinium oxide. This coating prevents further oxidation. Actinium mostly takes the +3 oxidation state in its chemical compounds, similar to most lanthanides and many actinides. Actinium is found in tiny amounts in uranium and thorium ores. The main isotope, actinium-227, has a half-life of about 21.772 years and mostly emits beta particles, sometimes alpha particles. Actinium-228 is another isotope, beta active with a half-life of 6.15 hours. One tonne of natural uranium contains about 0.2 milligrams of actinium-227, and one tonne of thorium contains about 5 nanograms of actinium-228. Actinium's properties are very similar to lanthanum, making it hard to separate from the ore. Instead, actinium is made in small amounts in a nuclear reactor. Due to its scarcity, high cost, and radioactivity, actinium has no significant industrial uses. It is used mainly as a neutron source and in radiation therapy.
Here is a list of notable deaths in June 2018. Each day's entries are alphabetized by last name. A typical entry includes the following information in this order:
Churdan is a city in Greene County, Iowa, United States. It had 386 people living there in 2010.

Robert Brown was a Scottish football player and manager. He was born on March 19, 1923, and passed away on January 15, 2020. Brown played as a goalkeeper for Queen's Park, Rangers, and Falkirk. He also played for the Scottish national team five times. After his playing career, Brown managed St. Johnstone and the Scottish national team from 1967 to 1971. In 2015, he was inducted into the Scottish Football Hall of Fame.

West Hanningfield is a small village in south Essex, England. It is about southeast of the county town, Chelmsford. The village is part of the Chelmsford borough and the Rayleigh parliamentary constituency. It is north of Hanningfield Reservoir. Nearby villages include South Hanningfield, Stock, Rettendon, and East Hanningfield. It is also close to Chelmsford suburbs Galleywood and Great Baddow. The local pub is called the Three Compasses. The village has a primary school, a village hall, and a hairdresser. Lord Hanningfield, a former leader of Essex County Council, lives there. St Mary and St Edward Church, in the village's east, is a Grade II* listed building. It was built around the 12th century, with changes in the 18th and 19th centuries. The church tower, made of wood and likely from the early 13th century, has timbers dated from 1382 to 1414. Bells cast in 1676, a rare example of complete 17th-century bells, are in the church. The church is important because of its history.
Marie Dubois, born Claudine Lucie Pauline Huzé, was an actress from Paris. She was born on January 12, 1937, and died on October 15, 2014. She was French.

Charles Joseph Scarborough was born on April 9, 1963. He is an American cable news host. Now, he co-hosts "Morning Joe" on MSNBC with his wife Mika Brzezinski. He previously hosted "Scarborough Country" on the same network. Before that, he was a lawyer and a politician. He served in the United States House of Representatives from 1995 to 2001 as a Republican for Florida's 1st district. Scarborough also worked as a visiting fellow at the Harvard Institute of Politics at the Harvard Kennedy School of Government. In 2011, he was named one of the most influential people in the world by Time magazine.

The North Mississippi Allstars is an American southern rock/blues band from Hernando, Mississippi. They were formed in 1996. The band includes two brothers: Luther Dickinson (guitar, fiddle, vocals) and Cody Dickinson (drums, keyboards, electric washboard, vocals). Duwayne Burnside, who used to play second guitar, is the son of R.L. Burnside and has played on some of their songs.

Alaska Airlines is a big American airline based in Seattle, Washington. It is the fifth-largest airline in the United States, measured by the number of planes, passengers, and destinations. Alaska Airlines, along with its partners Horizon Air and SkyWest Airlines, runs a large network of domestic routes, mainly connecting cities in the Pacific Northwest and Alaska to more than one hundred destinations in the United States, Hawaii, Canada, Costa Rica, and Mexico. The airline has five main hubs, with its main hub at Seattle/Tacoma airport. As of 2020, Alaska Airlines has over 16,000 employees. It has also been ranked as having the highest customer satisfaction among traditional airlines for twelve years by J.D. Power and Associates. Alaska Airlines plans to join the oneworld alliance by the end of 2020.

Bari was a province in the Apulia region of Italy. Its capital city was Bari. The province had an area and a population of 1,594,109 in 2005. On January 1, 2015, it became the Metropolitan City of Bari.

Gameshark is a brand name for cheat devices used in video games for different consoles and Windows computers. Currently, Mad Catz owns the Gameshark brand. They made Gameshark products for Sony PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo game consoles. Players use cheat codes from Gameshark discs or cartridges to put cheats into the console's memory. When the game starts, the cheats are applied.

In 2018 FIFA World Cup qualification, UEFA Group B had six teams: Portugal, Switzerland, Hungary, Faroe Islands, Latvia, and Andorra. The first round draw was on July 25, 2015, at the Konstantinovsky Palace in St. Petersburg, Russia. Portugal won the group and qualified directly for the 2018 FIFA World Cup. Switzerland came second in the group and advanced to the play-offs. They won against Northern Ireland and qualified for the tournament.

jump blues is a fast version of blues. Small groups usually play it, often with horn instruments. It became popular in the 1940s and led to rhythm and blues and rock and roll. People started enjoying jump blues again in the 1990s, part of a swing music revival.

Edmond Maires was a French labor union leader. He worked as the secretary general of the French Democratic Confederation of Labour (CFDT) from 1971 to 1988. He did not like strikes and believed in sharing work equally.

Hilbert spaces, named after David Hilbert, are like extended versions of the spaces we know, such as the two-dimensional plane and three-dimensional space. They use the rules of vectors and calculus, but can have any number of dimensions, whether finite or infinite. A Hilbert space is a special kind of space where you can measure lengths and angles. Also, it's complete, meaning it has all the limits needed for calculus. These spaces appear naturally in many areas of math and physics, often as big spaces of functions. The early 20th century saw important work on Hilbert spaces by David Hilbert, Erhard Schmidt, and Frigyes Riesz. They are crucial in solving partial differential equations, understanding quantum mechanics, analyzing signals, studying heat transfer, and explaining thermodynamics. The term "Hilbert space" was coined by John von Neumann to describe the abstract concept behind these applications. Hilbert spaces helped make functional analysis a very successful field. Examples of Hilbert spaces include spaces of square-integrable functions, spaces of sequences, and spaces of generalized functions. Just like in a simpler space, in a Hilbert space, you can use the Pythagorean theorem and the parallelogram law. Projecting perpendicularly onto a subspace, similar to dropping a triangle's altitude, is important for solving optimization problems. Each element in a Hilbert space can be described by its coordinates, much like how we use Cartesian coordinates in the plane. In some cases, especially with infinite dimensions, Hilbert spaces can be thought of as spaces of infinite sequences that are square-summable. Linear operators in Hilbert spaces are transformations that stretch the space in different directions, which can be understood by studying their spectrum.
Annapolis is a small place in Crawford County, Illinois, United States. It is located northwest of Robinson. Annapolis has a post office with the zip code 62413. In 2010, the population was 55.

Nelson Lagoon is a small town in the Aleutians East Borough of Alaska. The population was 52 in 2010, down from 83 in 2000. Established around 1960, it's the newest community in the area. Nelson Lagoon is the only Aleut settlement along the Bering Sea coast. It's located on the northern coast of the Alaska Peninsula, on a narrow sand spit separating the lagoon from the Bering Sea. The town is in a rich salmon fishing area. In the late 1990s, they built a dock, boat ramp, harbormaster's office, and warehouse. Nelson Lagoon has good docking facilities and storage for boats and equipment. There's also a 4,000-foot-long, lighted gravel runway for planes. In March 2016, the town was covered by ash during a big eruption of nearby Mount Pavlof.

The president of Crimea was the leader of the Crimean Republic from February 16, 1994, until March 17, 1995. The position was ended because it went against Ukraine's constitution. The first election for Crimean president happened on January 16, 1994. In the second round on January 30, 1994, Yuriy Meshkov, a Russian supporter, won with 72.9% of the votes. He was the only person to be Crimean president.

Susanna "Susan" Kohner was born on November 11, 1936. She is an American former actress who worked in films and TV. She is famous for her role as Sarah Jane in the movie "Imitation of Life" in 1959. For this role, she was nominated for an Oscar and won a Golden Globe. In the movie, she played a light-skinned Black woman who "passed" for white when she was a child and young adult. In 1964, Kohner married John Weitz, a menswear designer and writer. After that, she stopped acting to focus on her family. Her two sons, Paul Weitz and Chris Weitz, became film directors, producers, screenwriters, and sometimes actors.

Eurovision disco (or eurodisco) is a type of electronic dance music from Europe. It came from disco in the late 1970s and includes pop and rock elements. Many eurodisco songs have English lyrics, but singers often speak other languages. Eurodisco includes styles like Europop and eurodance. Its main sub-genres are space disco from the late 1970s and italo disco from the early 1980s. The genre became less popular after 1986, when electronic rock and hi-nrg gained more attention. However, italo disco saw a small revival in the late 1990s.

Quorn is a small town and railhead in the Flinders Ranges in northern South Australia, northeast of Port Augusta. In 2021, the town had 1,230 people, with 1,131 in its main area. Quorn is where the Flinders Ranges Council is based. It is part of the Stuart state district and the Grey federal district. The town is famous for its pretty setting and old buildings, attracting tourists and filmmakers. It is also the end point of the Pichi Richi railway.

St. Paul is a town in southern Madison County, Arkansas, United States. In 2010, it had 113 people. St. Paul is near the northwest Arkansas region. The town was created in 1887 when the railroad reached that place.

Gumpei Yokoi was a Japanese video game designer. He worked for Nintendo for a long time. Yokoi is famous for creating the Game & Watch handheld system. He also invented the "cross" shaped control pad. He was the original designer of the Game Boy. Yokoi produced several popular and well-received video game franchises, including Metroid and Kid Icarus.

Toxic chemicals were used as weapons for thousands of years, but the first large-scale use was during World War I. Chemical weapons were mainly used to make soldiers feel scared, hurt, and kill those who were hiding behind defenses. The gas clouds moved slowly, so they were very effective. Different types of gases were used, from tear gas to more dangerous ones like phosgene, chlorine, and mustard gas. This chemical warfare was a big part of the first big and total war of the 20th century. About 90,000 people died from gas attacks, out of 1.3 million injured. Unlike other weapons, gas had countermeasures like gas masks. As gas usage increased later in the war, its effectiveness decreased. The widespread use of chemical weapons and advances in explosives led to World War I being called "the chemist's war." Its use was illegal because it broke rules set in 1899 and 1907. Public anger over the use of gas led to less chemical weapon use in World War II.
Dows is a city in Franklin and Wright counties, in the state of Iowa. In 2010, it had 538 people living there.

Metropolis is a city in Illinois, located along the Ohio River in Massac County. According to the 2010 United States Census, it has 6,537 people. Metropolis is the county seat of Massac County. It is also part of the Paducah, KY-IL micropolitan statistical area, in southern Illinois.

Thomas Hodgkin lived from August 17, 1798, to April 5, 1866. He was a British doctor. People think he was one of the best pathologists of his time and a leader in stopping illnesses before they start. He is famous for describing a disease called Hodgkin's disease in 1832. This disease affects the lymph nodes and blood. Hodgkin's work showed that pathologists could play an important role in patient care. He worked at Guy's Hospital around the same time as Thomas Addison and Richard Bright.

Chaim Yisroel Belsky was an American rabbi who lived from August 22, 1938, to January 28, 2016. He was an Orthodox and Haredi Jewish leader who lived in Brooklyn, New York. He taught at Yeshiva Torah Vodaas and was the rabbi for a summer camp network run by Agudath Israel of America. For over 28 years, he worked as a senior kashrut advisor for the OU. He was known for his deep knowledge of Torah and his wide-ranging general knowledge and practical experience. Some people criticized him for comments he made about accusations of sexual abuse against a Jewish camp worker.

Football is the most popular sport in Austria. The Austrian Football Association, called ÖFB, was created in 1904 and has been part of FIFA since then. Despite being very popular, Austria's national team hasn't done well in tournaments. Their only European Championship was in 2008, when they were co-hosts, but they didn't advance. In 2016, they played in a qualifier but finished last. In the World Cup, Austria has had better results. They were fourth in 1934 and third in 1954. They didn't enter the World Cup in 1930. They didn't qualify for the World Cup in 1966, 1970, 1974, 1986, 1994, 2002, 2006, 2010, and 2014. They withdrew in 1938 and 1950, and were eliminated at the group stage in 1958, 1978, 1982, 1990, and 1998.

Milan Michálek, born on December 7, 1984, is a Czech professional ice hockey player. He plays as a left winger and is currently not signed to any team. He last played for the Toronto Maple Leafs in the NHL. He was chosen sixth overall in the 2003 NHL draft by the San Jose Sharks. His older brother, Zbyněk Michálek, is a defenceman who played in the NHL for the Arizona Coyotes.

Mel Campos López, Jr., was born on September 1, 1935, and died on January 1, 2017. He was a Filipino politician. He served as the mayor of Manila from 1986 to 1987 and again from 1988 to 1992. He was also an assemblyman in the Batasang Pambansa from 1984 to 1986. Additionally, he was the chairman of the Philippine Sports Commission.
Saint-Paul-mont-Penit is a commune in Vendée, which is in the Pays de la Loire region in western France.

Hainan Airlines Co., Ltd. (HNA) is an airline based in Haikou, Hainan, People's Republic of China. It is the largest civilian airline and majority state-owned company in the country. HNA is the fourth-largest airline in China by the size of its fleet and the tenth-largest in Asia by the number of passengers carried. It offers scheduled domestic and international flights on 500 routes from Hainan and nine other locations on the mainland. It also provides charter services. The main base of Hainan Airlines is Haikou Meilan International Airport, with hubs at Beijing Capital International Airport and Xi'an Xianyang International Airport, and several focus cities. Hainan Airlines is a Skytrax 5-star airline.

In Nova Scotia, Canada, Halifax Regional Municipality had municipal elections on October 21, 2000. These elections happen every four years since 1996, when Halifax, Dartmouth, Bedford, and parts of Halifax County merged. The council has 23 councillors and a mayor. All positions were up for election. There are no political parties at the municipal level in Nova Scotia, so candidates run as independents.

Leon Norman Cohen (born September 21, 1934, died November 7, 2016) was a Canadian singer, songwriter, poet, and novelist. His work talked about religion, politics, being alone, feeling sad, love, relationships, losing things, death. Cohen was inducted into several halls of fame, received a high civilian honor, and won awards for his literature. He started writing poetry and novels in the 1950s and early 1960s, and began his music career in 1967 at age 33. His first album, "Songs of Leonard Cohen," was released in 1967. He followed with "Songs from a Room" (1969), "Songs of Love and Hate" (1971), and "New Skin for the Old Ceremony" (1974). In 1977, his album "Death of a Ladies' Man," produced by Phil Spector, changed his sound. In 1979, "Recent Songs" blended his style with jazz, Asian, and Mediterranean influences. His famous song "Hallelujah" was first released in 1984. "I'm Your Man" in 1988 marked his move to electronic music. In 1992, "The Future" had dark lyrics about politics and society. Cohen returned to music in 2001 with "Ten New Songs," which was popular in Canada and Europe. His 11th album, "Dear Heather," came out in 2004. Between 2008 and 2013, he had successful tours and released three albums in the last five years of his life: "Old Ideas" (2012), "Popular Problems" (2014), and "You Want It Darker" (2016), the last released three weeks before his death. A posthumous album, "Thanks for the Dance," was released in November 2019, his 15th studio album.

Russian Mission is a city in Kusilvak Census Area, Alaska. A fur trading post was there in 1842. After Alaska was bought by the United States in 1867, the city was officially called Russian Mission in the early 1900s. Alcohol is not allowed there. In 2010, the population was 312, up from 296 in 2000.

Ningbo is a city in northeast Zhejiang province, People's Republic of China. It is a sub-provincial city and includes urban districts, three satellite cities, and several rural counties, including islands in Hangzhou Bay and the East China Sea. Its port, the Port of Ningbo–Zhoushan, is one of the busiest in the world. The city has a separate state-planning status. According to the 2010 census, the total population of Ningbo was 7.6 million, with 3.5 million in the built-up area made up of six urban districts. To the north, Hangzhou Bay separates Ningbo from Shanghai. To the east lies Zhoushan in the East China Sea. To the west and south, Ningbo borders Shaoxing and Taizhou. The city is also the birthplace of Chinese nationalist leader Chiang Kai-shek.

George Dureau lived from December 28, 1930, to April 7, 2014. He was an American artist. His career was known for drawing charcoal sketches and taking black and white photos. He often photographed poor white and black athletes, as well as dwarfs and amputees. It is said that Robert Mapplethorpe was inspired by Dureau's photos of amputees and dwarfs. These photos showed the subjects as real, complex, and full of human emotions, both vulnerable and playful.

The Boutonne is a long river in the Deux-Sèvres and Charente-Maritime areas of western France. It starts in a village called Chef-Boutonne. The river mostly flows southwest. It joins the Charente River near Cabariot.

Wastewater, or sewage, is water used by a community. It includes greywater from sinks, bathtubs, and dishwashers, and blackwater from toilets. Also, it has soaps, detergents, and toilet paper. This water travels from buildings through plumbing into sewers or onsite sewage facilities. In sewers, it can mix with surface water. Most wastewater worldwide is not treated, causing pollution, especially in poorer countries. An estimate is that 90% of wastewater is released untreated. Sewage is an older term now replaced by "wastewater." In American English, sewage and sewerage are often used the same way. However, in technical and professional terms, "sewerage" refers to the pipes and systems used to carry sewage.
Athies is a commune in the Pas-de-Calais department in northern France.

In Ireland, the term "gaeltacht" refers to districts where Irish is the main language spoken at home. It can also describe all such districts together. The Irish government first officially recognized these districts in the 1920s, during the early days of the Irish Free State. This recognition was part of a policy to bring back the Irish language, following a revival movement. Today, there are concerns about the decline of the Irish language. A 2015 study found that out of 155 electoral divisions in the gaeltacht, only 21 have Irish spoken daily by more than two-thirds of the population. Some experts believe that two-thirds is a crucial level for the language's survival.
Here is a list of notable deaths in February 2018. Each day's entries are in alphabetical order by last name. A typical entry includes the following information:
Domecy-sur-le-Vault is a town in the Yonne department, which is in Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, in central France. It is famous for the Château de Domecy-sur-le-Vault.

Cozy Powell, born Colin Trevor Flooks on December 29, 1947, and passed away on April 5, 1998, was an English rock drummer. He played with many famous rock bands and artists, such as the Jeff Beck Group, Rainbow, Gary Moore, Robert Plant, Brian May, Whitesnake, Emerson, Lake & Powell, and Black Sabbath. Powell appeared on at least 66 albums and contributed to many others. Many rock drummers look up to him as a major influence.
Strausberg is a town in Brandenburg, Germany. It is 30 kilometers east of Berlin and has 25,594 people living there. Strausberg is the biggest town in the Märkisch-oderland district.

Shawn Colvin, born on January 10, 1956, as Shawna Lee Colvin, is an American singer-songwriter and musician. She has been making solo music for many years. Colvin is famous for her song "Sunny Came Home," which won a Grammy Award in 1997.

Sir John Berry Hobbs, known as Jack Hobbs, was an English cricket player who played for Surrey from 1905 to 1934 and for England in 61 test matches between 1908 and 1930. He was called "the master" and is considered one of the best batsmen in cricket history. Hobbs scored 61,760 runs and hit 199 centuries. He was a right-handed batsman and sometimes bowled as well. He was also a good fielder, especially at cover point. Born in 1882 in poverty, Hobbs wanted to be a cricketer from a young age. His early batting was not good, but he improved suddenly in 1901, which caught the attention of local teams. In 1903, with the help of England batsman Tom Hayward, Hobbs joined Surrey. His first-class debut was impressive, scoring 88 runs. He then scored a century in his next game. Over the next few seasons, Hobbs became a good county player and made his test debut in 1908, scoring 83 runs. His performance improved, especially against South African spin bowlers. In 1911-12, he scored three centuries against Australia and was considered the world's best batsman. During the First World War, Hobbs played in the Royal Flying Corps. He returned in 1919 and continued to be successful in both test and domestic cricket until his retirement. His success came from his quick footwork, ability to play many shots, and good placement of the ball. Hobbs was one of the first batsmen to do well against spin bowlers. He adapted his technique and became a more cautious player after his appendicitis in 1921. He then played more consistently and scored a lot in both test and domestic cricket. He had some of his best innings during this period. Hobbs' success was due to his quick steps, ability to play different shots, and placing the ball well. He opened the batting and had good partnerships with other players, such as Tom Hayward, Andy Sandham, Wilfred Rhodes, and Herbert Sutcliffe. The partnership with Sutcliffe remains the most successful for the first wicket in test history. Hobbs lived comfortably with his wife Ada after retiring. They had a long marriage, and she helped support them through his income from Surrey, commercial deals, and his shop. Hobbs also worked in journalism after cricket. He was knighted in 1953, the first professional cricketer to be honored this way. Hobbs passed away in 1963, aged 81, just a few months after his wife.
Riceville is a city in Howard and Mitchell counties, in the state of Iowa. The population was 785 according to the 2010 census.

A reasonable accommodation is a change made to make a system fair for someone based on their needs. These needs can be different, like religious beliefs, physical challenges, mental health issues, emotions, school requirements, or work needs. Laws often require these changes. Different countries have their own ways to provide these accommodations. The United Nations uses this term in their convention on the rights of people with disabilities. They say not making such accommodations is discrimination. They define a "reasonable accommodation" as:

william john fairbairn, nicknamed bulldog, was born on january 7, 1947. he was a professional ice hockey player. fairbairn played as a right wing and was in the nhl for 10 seasons. most of his career was with the new york rangers. later, he played for the minnesota north stars and st. louis blues. fairbairn stopped playing early in the 1978-79 season. during his career, he scored 162 goals.
Rockville is a village in the town of Vernon, in Tolland County, Connecticut, United States. In 2010, it had 7,474 people. Rockville became a city in 1889. Since 1965, it has been part of Vernon.

The Central Bohemian region is an administrative area in the Czech Republic, in the middle part of historical Bohemia. Its main city, Prague, is in the center but is not part of this region; it is a separate region. The Central Bohemian region is in the heart of Bohemia and is the largest region in the Czech Republic, covering about 11,014 km², which is almost 14% of the country. It surrounds Prague and shares borders with seven other regions: Liberec to the north, Hradec Králové to the northeast, Pardubice to the east, Vysočina to the southeast, South Bohemia to the south, Plzeň to the west, and Ústí nad Labem to the northwest.
Bournos is a commune in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department, in southwestern France.

The Berlin State Opera is a famous building on Unter den Linden Boulevard in the center of Berlin. It was built between 1741 and 1743 by Frederick the Great, based on designs by Georg Wenzeslaus von Knobelsdorff. The opera house was in the royal Prussian opera house before the war. It was damaged during World War II but was rebuilt from 1951 to 1955. It's known as "Lindenoper." It is special because it is the first theater in the world that stands alone as a big, important building in a city.
Joseph Bonnel was a French football player who played as a midfielder. He was part of France's team in the 1966 FIFA World Cup. He scored 3 goals in that season.

Kieren John Perkins, OAM, was born on August 14, 1973. He is an Australian former swimmer. Perkins won four Olympic medals and set world records in three events. He was one of the best long-distance swimmers in the world. Perkins won two Olympic gold medals in the 1500-meter freestyle in 1992 and 1996, and a silver medal in 2000.

Heidi Alexander, born on April 17, 1975, is a British Labour Party politician. She works as the deputy mayor for transport in London under Sadiq Khan. She is also the deputy chair of transport for London. Heidi was an MP for Lewisham East from the 2010 general election. She left that job in May 2018 to join the mayoral team. She was named shadow secretary of state for health on September 13, 2015, but quit the shadow cabinet on June 26, 2016.

Fernando Bernabé Agüero Rocha was born on June 11, 1917, in Managua and died on September 27, 2011. He was a Nicaraguan politician and started the Social Conservative Party in 1988. In 1967, Agüero ran for president as part of the Conservative 1966 National Opposition Union (UNO) against the Somoza regime. His campaign included a rally in Managua that was violently suppressed. In 1971, Agüero signed the controversial Kupia Kumi pact with Anastasio Somoza Debayle.

Ahmed Osman (Arabic: أحمد عصمان; born January 3, 1930) was the prime minister of Morocco from November 2, 1972, to March 22, 1979. He was married to Princess Lalla Nuzha of Morocco from 1964 to 1977. Princess Lalla Nuzha is a sister of King Hassan II. Ahmed Osman also founded the National Rally of Independents. He worked as the secretary general of the Ministry of National Defence from 1959 to 1961 and as an ambassador to the Federal Republic of Germany from 1961 to 1962 and to the United States from 1967 to 1972. He served as the under secretary of the Ministry of Mines and Industry from 1962 to 1964 and as president of the Moroccan General Navigation Company from 1964 to 1967. He was prime minister from 1972 to 1979. He became the president of the National Rally of Independents in 1977 and the president of the National Assembly from 1984 to 1992.

Binoculars, or field glasses, are two telescopes placed side-by-side and aligned to point in the same direction. This lets the viewer use both eyes when looking at distant objects. Most binoculars are held with both hands, but they come in different sizes, from small ones like opera glasses to larger, fixed models. Unlike a single telescope, binoculars give users a 3D image. For objects closer by, the two views from each eye create an impression of depth.

Tondiarpet taluk is a taluk in the city district of Chennai, in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It was created in December 2013 from parts of the old Fort-Tondiarpet taluk. This taluk includes the Tondiarpet neighborhood.

Australian convict sites are a world heritage property. There are 11 remaining penal sites. They were originally built in the British Empire between the 18th and 19th centuries. These sites are on fertile coastal areas in Sydney, Tasmania, Norfolk Island, and Fremantle. They show examples of large-scale transportation of convicts and the spread of European power through convict labor. The sites were first added to Australia's national heritage list in 1995 and later to the world heritage list. Work began in 1995. In January 2008, a nomination was made. It failed, and the nomination was changed.
Brooks County is the name of two counties in the United States.
Pantheon can mean: A building, often a large, important one A place to remember important people

Joel Murray, born on April 17, 1963, is an American actor. He has played important roles in TV shows like "Mad Men," "Grand," "Love & War," "Dharma and Greg," and "Shameless." He has also acted in movies such as "God Bless America" and "Monsters University."
Serrières-de-Briord is a village in Ain, which is in eastern France.

The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks is an action-adventure game made by Nintendo for the Nintendo DS. It was part of the Zelda series and came out in December 2009. Later, in October 2016, it was available again on the Wii U. Like other Zelda games, Spirit Tracks has a cartoon-like look. The main character, Link, rides a steam train with a cannon to explore the game world. In the game, players can also control phantoms and play a flute called the spirit flute. Spirit Tracks is special because it has different endings depending on how you play the game. These endings change what happens to Link in the end.

William Frederick Fraser, born on July 8, 1960, and died on June 28, 2019, was from Northern Ireland. He supported people hurt by violence from Irish Republican groups. Fraser started and led a group called Families Acting for Innocent Relatives (FAIR). He was also a leader in the Love Ulster campaign and the Belfast city hall flag protests. In 2019, journalist Mandy McAuley said the Ulster Defence Association got weapons from the Ulster Resistance in the late 1980s. Fraser was the person who gave the weapons to them. McAuley said this was true based on information from multiple sources. The weapons connected to at least 70 murders by paramilitary groups.

The Terminal is a 2004 movie. It's a comedy-drama film. Steven Spielberg directed it and acted with Tom Hanks, Catherine Zeta-Jones, and Stanley Tucci. The story is about an Eastern European man who gets stuck at John F. Kennedy Airport in New York. He can't enter the U.S., and he can't go back to his home country because of a problem there. This film is partly based on a real story. In 1988, a man named Mehran Karimi Nasseri stayed in Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport for 18 years. After finishing another movie, "Catch Me If You Can," Spielberg decided to make this one. He wanted a film that could make people laugh and feel good. Since no airport was willing to help, they built a full set inside a hangar. Most outdoor scenes were filmed at Montreal–Mirabel International Airport. The movie came out in North America on June 18, 2004. People had mixed feelings about it, but it did well at the box office, making $77.9 million in the U.S. and $219.4 million worldwide.

The Ringmaster is the second album by the American hip hop group Insane Clown Posse, released on March 8, 1994, by Psychopathic Records. They recorded it in 1993 at the Tempermill studio. This album is part of their carnival-themed stories. Its songs talk about the Ringmaster, a leader in the carnival who judges people's souls after death, made from the listener's own bad actions. The Ringmaster was made by producer Mike E. Clark, who worked with the group for many years. It includes guest appearances by Capitol E and Jumpsteady. In 1998, Island Records reissued the album, and it became a gold record in the U.S. The original version also got a gold certification in 2004.

Cristian Eugen Chivu, born on October 26, 1980, is a former Romanian footballer. He mostly played as a left back and sometimes as a central defender. He started his career at his hometown club FC Resita and then moved to FC Universitatea Craiova in 1998. A year later, he joined Ajax in the Netherlands. As a captain at Ajax, his performances led to an €18 million transfer to Roma in 2003. At Roma, he won the Coppa Italia in his last of four seasons before moving to Inter. He played for Inter until retiring in 2014. During his time at Inter, he won three major titles: the Italian league, the domestic cup, and the UEFA Champions League in 2010. Chivu played for Romania 75 times between 1999 and 2010, and was part of their teams for the UEFA European Championships in 2000 and 2008. After retiring, he became a football analyst for Sky Sport and Fox Sports and is also a technical observer for UEFA.

Hammurabi was the sixth king of Babylon, from about 1792 BC to 1750 BC (middle chronology). His father, Sin-muballit, gave up the throne because he was sick. Hammurabi then conquered Elam and several city-states: Larsa, Eshnunna, and Mari. He made Ishme-dagan I, the king of Assyria, pay tribute, and forced his son, Mut-ashkur, to do the same. This expanded Babylonian rule over much of Mesopotamia. Hammurabi is famous for creating the Code of Hammurabi, said to come from the god Shamash. Unlike earlier laws, his code focused more on punishing the criminal, not just compensating the victim. It listed specific punishments for each crime and assumed people were innocent until proven guilty. Though the punishments were very strict by today’s standards, they aimed to limit revenge. The Code of Hammurabi and the Ten Commandments in the Torah share many similarities. Hammurabi was believed to be a god during his lifetime and after. He was seen as a great conqueror and spreader of civilization, making people respect Marduk, the main god of Babylon. Later, his military achievements were less emphasized, and he was seen mainly as a lawgiver. Babylonians used his reign to measure events from the past. Even after his empire fell, Hammurabi was still seen as a good king, and rulers across the region claimed him as an ancestor. Hammurabi was found by archaeologists in the late 1800s and is considered important in the history of laws.

Townsville is a city on the northeastern coast of Queensland, Australia. It's the largest city north of the Sunshine Coast and had about 180,820 people in 2018. Locals call it the unofficial capital of North Queensland. Townsville has important government and business offices. It's in the dry tropics region, close to part of the Great Barrier Reef. Townsville is a big industrial city with a large zinc refinery, a nickel refinery, and other similar businesses. The port is growing to handle bigger ships from Asia and the world's largest passenger ships. Its location near Asia makes it important for trade, especially with China. There are many fun places to visit. The Strand is a long beach and garden area. Riverway is a park by the Ross River. Reef HQ is a big aquarium with animals from the Great Barrier Reef. The Museum of Tropical Queensland shows relics from a sunken British warship. Castle Hill, or Cootharinga, is a famous landmark for exercise. The town has a sports reserve. Magnetic Island is a large nearby island, mostly a national park.

A resistance movement is when some people in a country try to oppose the government or an occupying power, and disrupt the normal way of life. They might use peaceful methods, like protests, or use force, like fighting back. Sometimes, during a war, they might use both methods. Resistance movements can operate differently in different areas or phases. There is a debate about whether armed resistance is legal in international law. This debate started in 1899 when countries agreed on some rules for war. The rules said that fighters who were not part of the official army (francs-tireurs) could be treated differently. Later, in 1977, there was an agreement that said people fighting against foreign rulers or unfair governments could be protected. However, the terms were not clear, making it hard to decide who was a legitimate fighter. Depending on how a government sees things, a resistance group might be seen as a terrorist group. This depends on whether the group's fighters are seen as legal or illegal, and whether they have the right to fight against an occupying government. The decision is mostly based on political views.

Schifflange is a town in southwestern Luxembourg. It is part of the canton of Esch-sur-Alzette. The town of Schifflange, located in the western part of the commune, has 9,332 people living there. Schifflange became a separate town on August 15, 1876, when it was split from the commune of Esch-sur-Alzette. The law to create Schifflange was approved on July 6, 1876.

A corroboree is a meeting for Australian Aboriginal people. It can be a special, religious ceremony, a happy celebration, or related to fighting. The word came from the local Dharug language. A corroboree often has dancing, music, special clothes, and body paint. Now, it can mean any big, loud gathering.

Holley is an unincorporated community and census-designated place in Santa Rosa County, Florida, United States. The 2019 census counted 2,425 people there. Florida State Road 87 goes through Holley. Holley is usually seen as part of the bigger community of Navarre. Holley is included in the Holley-Navarre census area and uses the Holley-Navarre fire and water systems. Holley's voters are part of Navarre's voting area. Major neighborhoods in Holley are Gordon Evans Road, Nelson Street, and Bob Tolbert Road. These areas are growing quickly.

In 2018, a new academy prize in literature was created because the Nobel Prize in Literature was not given that year and was delayed to 2019. Maryse Condé won the prize on October 12, 2018. The new academy stopped existing in December 2018. They invited people worldwide to vote for 47 writers chosen by Swedish librarians. Four writers were chosen as finalists: Maryse Condé, Neil Gaiman, Haruki Murakami, and Kim Thúy. Murakami asked to be removed from the list because he preferred to focus on writing without media attention. Maryse Condé received the new academy prize in literature. In 2018, a non-profit organization called the new academy was set up to give out this prize. It was not connected to the Nobel Foundation or the Swedish Academy.

Shikabala, whose full name is Mahmoud Abdelrazek Hassan Fadlala (born March 5, 1986), is an Egyptian footballer. He plays for Zamalek in the Egyptian Premier League and for the Egypt national team. Shikabala started his career at Zamalek and has played there for many years. He is considered one of the club's legends. He also played for PAOK and Sporting CP. He usually plays as a right-winger but can also play as a central attacking midfielder or a left winger.
Guerbigny is a commune in the Somme department in Hauts-de-France, which is in northern France.

Merrimack County is in New Hampshire, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 146, 445 people, making it the third-largest county in New Hampshire. Concord is the county seat and capital city of New Hampshire. Merrimack County was formed in 1823 from parts of Hillsborough and Rockingham counties. It is named after the Merrimack River. The county is part of the Concord, NH micropolitan area, which is part of the Boston-Worcester-Providence, MA-RI-NH-CT combined statistical area. In 2010, the center of New Hampshire's population was in Merrimack County, specifically in the town of Pembroke.

"Time of the Season" is a song by the British rock band The Zombies. It appears on their 1968 album "Odessey and Oracle." The song was written by Rod Argent, who played keyboards. They recorded it at Abbey Road Studios in August 1967. Over a year later, it became a surprise hit in the United States. It reached number three on the Billboard Hot 100 and number one on the Cashbox chart. This song has become one of The Zombies' most popular and well-known songs.

Stagecoach is a transport company based in Perth, Scotland. It runs buses and coaches in the United Kingdom. It also used to operate in many other places like Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, and Oceania. Its stock is traded on the London Stock Exchange.

State of Georgia is an American TV show about comedy. It stars Raven-Symoné, Majandra Delfino, and Loretta Devine. The show is about half an hour long and has multiple camera angles. Raven-Symoné plays Georgia, an actress with a big personality. Georgia's best friend is Jo, played by Majandra Delfino. Jo is a science enthusiast. They try to do better in their careers and personal lives in New York City. The show was on ABC Family from June 29 to August 17, 2011. The first episode was watched by 1.32 million people. ABC Family stopped the show on September 16, 2011, because it didn't get many viewers.

Roman Stanley Gribbs was an American politician born on December 29, 1925, and died on April 5, 2016. He was the mayor of Detroit from 1970 to 1974. Later, he became a judge on the Michigan Court of Appeals. Gribbs was the last white mayor of Detroit, as the city was becoming mostly black. Detroit elected Mike Duggan as mayor in 2013.

Loretta Lynn, born April 14, 1932, is an American country music singer and songwriter. She has had multiple gold albums in her 60-year career. She is famous for songs like "You Ain't Woman Enough (To Take My Man)", "Don't Come Home a-Drinking (With Lovin' on Your Mind)", "One's on the Way", "Fist City", and "Coal Miner's Daughter". Lynn was in a 1980 film with the same name. She has won many awards, including from the Country Music Association and the Academy of Country Music. She is the most awarded female country recording artist and the only female ACM artist of the decade (1970s). Lynn has 24 number one hit singles and 11 number one albums. She still tours, performs at the Grand Ole Opry, and releases new albums.

Chiang Ching-kuo was a Taiwanese politician born on April 27, 1910, and died on January 13, 1988. He was the son of Chiang Kai-shek, the former president of the Republic of China. Ching-kuo had many important jobs in the Republic of China government. He was the premier from 1972 to 1978 and became president in 1978 until he died in 1988. When Ching-kuo was young, he studied in the Soviet Union in 1925. His father, Chiang Kai-shek, was part of an alliance with the Chinese Communist Party at that time. Ching-kuo met and married Faina Vakhreva there. In 1937, when war was coming between China and Japan, Ching-kuo and his wife were sent to China by Stalin. During the war, Ching-kuo's father started to trust him more. He gave Ching-kuo more important jobs, like managing administration. After World War II, Ching-kuo was in charge of cleaning up corruption in Shanghai. He did this very strictly. In 1949, when the communists won, the Chiang family and their government moved to Taiwan. Ching-kuo first controlled the secret police. He used arrests and torture to control things tightly. Later, he became Minister of Defense (1965-1969), Vice-premier (1969-1972), and Premier (1972-1978). In 1975, after his father's death, Ching-kuo led the Nationalist Party as chairman. He was elected president in 1978 and again in 1984. During his time, the government became less strict and more open to different opinions. Ching-kuo also focused on winning the support of people from Taiwan and not just those from mainland China. He made it easier for Taiwanese people to have more important roles, including his successor Lee Teng-hui.

Maizery used to be a small village in Moselle, a place in northeastern France. On June 1, 2016, Maizery joined with another village called Colligny to form a new village. In 2017, the new village had 182 people living there.

Squash is a game played with a ball and racquets in a court with four walls. Two players take turns hitting the ball against the walls. The goal is to make the ball bounce in a way that the opponent cannot return it. About 20 million people play squash regularly in more than 185 countries. A group called the World Squash Federation organizes the sport. They are part of the International Olympic Committee, but squash is not yet an Olympic event. People keep trying to get it included in the Olympics.

The Eastern Chalukyas, also known as the Chalukyas of Vengi, were a dynasty that ruled parts of South India from the 7th to the 12th centuries. They began as governors of the Chalukyas of Badami in the Deccan region. Later, they became independent rulers and governed the Vengi region in present-day Andhra Pradesh until 1189 CE. They continued to rule as vassals of the Cholas until 1189 CE. Their first capital was Vengi city (now Pedavegi near Eluru), later moved to Rajamahendravaram (now Rajahmundry). The Eastern Chalukyas were often involved in wars with the more powerful Cholas and Western Chalukyas over control of Vengi. During their 500 years of rule, Vengi was united, and Telugu culture, literature, poetry, and art flourished, especially in the later part of their rule.

Sidney Sheldon, born on February 11, 1917, and passed away on January 30, 2007, was an American writer, director, and producer. He was famous in the 1930s, working on Broadway plays and later in motion pictures. He wrote a successful comedy called "The Bachelor and the Bobby-Soxer" in 1947, which won him an Oscar in 1948. Sheldon also worked in television for 20 years, creating shows like "The Patty Duke Show" (1963-1966), "I Dream of Jeannie" (1965-1970), and "Hart to Hart" (1979-1984). After turning 50, he started writing best-selling romantic suspense novels, including "Master of the Game" (1982), "The Other Side of Midnight" (1973), and "Rage of Angels" (1980). His 18 novels have sold over 300 million copies in 51 languages. Sheldon is often mentioned as one of the top ten best-selling fiction writers of all time.

Rivers that join other rivers are listed based on where they meet, with those closer to the sea appearing earlier. Some rivers not entirely in Germany, like the Meuse, are mentioned for their German tributaries. These are noted in italics. Only rivers longer than their major tributaries are included.
