The University of Costa Rica, or UCR (in Spanish: "Universidad de Costa Rica"), is a public university in Costa Rica, a country in Central America. Its main campus, called Ciudad Universitaria Rodrigo Facio, is in San Pedro Montes de Oca, in the province of San José. It is the oldest and biggest university in Costa Rica, started in 1843 as "Universidad de Santo Tomás." It is one of the most important research universities in the country and Central America, and is considered one of the most prestigious and recognized in Latin America. About 45,000 students study there each year.

On a sailing vessel, a forestay keeps the mast from falling backwards. It is attached to the top of the mast or between 1/8 and 1/4 of the way down from the top. The other end of the forestay is attached to the boat's bow. Often, a sail called a jib or genoa is attached to the forestay. In a cutter rig, the jib or jibs are attached to stays in front of the forestay, sometimes going from the mast to a bowsprit. The sail on the forestay is then called a staysail. A forestay can be made from stainless steel wire, solid stainless steel rod, carbon rod, or ultra high molecular weight polyethylene on a modern yacht or high-performance racing boat. On older ships, it might be made from galvanized wire or natural fibers.

A video game developer makes video games. They can work alone or in big companies. In small companies, one person might do everything. In bigger companies, different people handle tasks like programming, designing, creating art, and testing. Most game developers get help with money and marketing from companies that publish games. Those who work alone are called indie developers. Developers can make games for different consoles like Nintendo Switch, Xbox One, or PlayStation 4, or for computers and phones. They can focus on specific types of games, like role-playing games or first-person shooters. Some also help move games to different systems or change languages. Sometimes, developers do regular software work too. Many game publishers have their own development teams, but are mainly seen as publishers. Developers can be private companies, like Bungie, which created the Halo series for Xbox.

Paul Gust Vallas, born on June 10, 1953, is an American politician. He was the superintendent of the Bridgeport public schools and the Recovery School District of Louisiana. Vallas was also the CEO of the School District of Philadelphia and the Chicago Public Schools. He worked as the budget director for the city of Chicago. In 2002, Vallas tried to become the Democratic governor of Illinois but did not succeed. He ran for Lieutenant Governor of Illinois with Pat Quinn in 2014, but lost to Bruce Rauner and Evelyn Sanguinetti. In 2019, Vallas ran for Mayor of Chicago, finishing ninth with 5.43% of the vote. He did not advance to the runoff and supported Lori Lightfoot.

Devonté Hynes, born David Joseph Michael Hynes on December 23, 1985, is an English singer, songwriter, record producer, and director. He was a member of the band Test Icicles from 2004 to 2006. Hynes played guitar, synth, and sang occasionally. Test Icicles released one full album in 2005. After leaving the band, he made two solo albums as Lightspeed Champion. Then, he released four albums as Blood Orange between 2008 and 2018. Hynes has also written, played, or produced music for artists like Tinashe, Solange Knowles, Connan Mockasin, Tei Shi, Sky Ferreira, FKA Twigs, HAIM, Florence and the Machine, Carly Rae Jepsen, Diana Vickers, The Chemical Brothers, Kylie Minogue, ASAP Rocky, Mac Miller, Blondie, and Mariah Carey.

James Henry Hammond was born on November 15, 1807, and died on November 13, 1864. He was an attorney, politician, and planter from South Carolina. Hammond worked as a U.S. representative from 1835 to 1836. He was the 60th governor of South Carolina from 1842 to 1844. He also served as a U.S. senator from 1857 to 1860. He was known as a strong supporter of slavery before the American Civil War. Hammond owned a large amount of property, including 22 square miles, several plantations, and houses. He had more than 300 slaves. Through his wife’s family, he was Wade Hampton II’s brother-in-law and the uncle of Wade Hampton III and other children. There was a scandal when it was discovered that Hammond had raped four teenage girls from the Hampton family. This initially seemed to end his career. However, he was later elected as a U.S. senator.

Shawnee is a city in Pottawatomie County, Oklahoma, United States. In 2010, its population was 29,857, which was 4.9 percent more than the 28,692 in 2000. The city is part of the Oklahoma City-Shawnee area. It is the county seat of Pottawatomie County and the main city in the Shawnee micropolitan area. Shawnee is near Interstate 40. It is about 45 minutes east of downtown Oklahoma City. To the east and northeast, it is 112 miles from the McClellan-Kerr Arkansas River Navigation System, which connects to the Gulf of Mexico.

Pleasant Hill is a city in Polk County, Iowa, United States. In 2010, the population was 8,785. It is part of the Des Moines–West Des Moines metropolitan area. In July 2005, Pleasant Hill got a zip code, 50327.

In Belgium, the monarchy is a constitutional, hereditary, and popular system where the current leader is called the "King" or "Queen of the Belgians." The king or queen is the head of state. Belgium has had seven kings or queens since independence in 1830. The current king, Philippe, became the king on July 21, 2013, after his father gave up the throne.

Hoyerswerda is a major town in the Bautzen district, in the state of Saxony, Germany. It is in the Sorbian-speaking area of Upper Lusatia. Hoyerswerda has two parts: the old town with many old houses and sights, and the new town with modern buildings. Before renovations, many old apartment blocks were there. The town has many lakes, marshes, and waterways because it is in Lusatia. This attracts holidaymakers and cyclists who use new paths near the lakes.

Aurelius Ambrosius, known as Ambrose in English (397 AD), was a bishop of Milan and a theologian. He lived in the 4th century and was one of the most important church leaders of that time. Ambrose was working as a Roman governor in Milan when he suddenly became the bishop in 374, chosen by the people. As bishop, he fought against arianism, a religious belief, and tried to help resolve the conflict between Emperor Theodosius I and Magnus Maximus, a rival emperor. Tradition says Ambrose helped create "antiphonal chant," a singing style where one part of the choir responds to another, and wrote "Veni Redemptor Gentium," a Christmas hymn. He also had a big influence on St. Augustine of Hippo. In Western Christianity, Ambrose was considered one of the four main teachers of the faith. The Catholic Church, Eastern Orthodox Church, Anglican Church, and some Lutheran groups consider him a saint. He is also the patron saint of Milan.
Burgistein is a town in the Thun area of the Bern canton in Switzerland.
Kellinghusen is a town in Steinburg district, which is in Schleswig-Holstein.

Cearbhall Ó Dálaigh was born on February 12, 1911, and passed away on March 21, 1978. He was an Irish politician, judge, and lawyer. Ó Dálaigh served as the fifth president of Ireland from December 1974 to October 1976. He worked as a judge at the European Court of Justice from 1973 to 1974. From 1961 to 1973, he was the chief justice of Ireland. He was also a judge at the Supreme Court from 1953 to 1973. Ó Dálaigh was attorney general of Ireland from 1946 to 1948 and again from 1951 to 1953. Sometimes, his name is written as Carroll O'Daly, which he used in his legal career.

The Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARM) was a special region in the Philippines, mainly in Mindanao, with five provinces where most people were Muslim: Basilan (excluding Isabela City), Lanao del Sur, Maguindanao, Sulu, and Tawi-Tawi. It had its own government. Cotabato City was often considered its capital, even though it wasn't part of the region. In 2008, the province of Shariff Kabunsuan was removed from ARM after a court said it shouldn't exist. In 2012, President Aquino wanted peace and planned to change the name to Bangsamoro Autonomous Region. In 2018, President Duterte signed a new law, the Bangsamoro Organic Law (BOL), to create a new region called Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM). ARM stopped officially existing after BOL was approved, and BARMM will take over. The BOL was officially ratified on January 25, 2019, after a public vote.
Michel Jeury, born on January 23, 1934, and passed away on January 9, 2015, was a French writer of science fiction. He was well-known in the 1970s. He also wrote under a different name, Albert Higon.

The flag of Myanmar, also known as Burma, was adopted on October 21, 2010. This new flag replaced the old one used since 1974. The new flag was introduced at the same time as changes to the country's name, which were set out in the 2008 constitution. The flag has three horizontal stripes: yellow, green, and red. In the middle, there is a white star with five points. The colors have special meanings: yellow stands for solidarity, green for peace and tranquility, and red for courage and decisiveness.

The Song of Songs, also known as the Song of Solomon or Canticles, is a unique book in the Hebrew Bible. It does not focus on laws, covenants, or the God of Israel, nor does it teach wisdom like Proverbs or Ecclesiastes. Instead, it celebrates love and sexuality, with the voices of two lovers praising each other, expressing desire, and inviting each other. The lovers are in harmony, each wanting the other and enjoying their intimacy. Jerusalem's women join the lovers in the story, acting as an audience that helps the reader participate in the lovers' romantic encounters. In modern Judaism, this book is read on Sabbath during Passover. Passover marks the start of the grain harvest and also remembers the Exodus from Egypt. Jewish tradition sees the book as an allegory of God's relationship with Israel. Christianity views it as an allegory of Christ and his "bride," the Church.

The G7 is a group of seven countries that work together on economics. These countries are Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States. As of 2018, these seven countries own about 317 trillion dollars and make up more than half of the global wealth. They also account for over 46% of the global GDP when measured in nominal values and more than 32% of the global GDP based on purchasing power. The European Union can join the G7 meetings as a guest. Each year, the G7 holds a summit where the leaders from these seven countries meet.
Awista Ayub (born around 1979) is an Afghan writer. She founded the Afghan Youth Sports Exchange in the United States.

Page County is in Iowa, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 15, 932 people. The county seat is Clarinda. It was named after Captain John Page of the 4th U.S. Infantry. He was badly hurt in a battle called Palo Alto.

Orestes "Minnie" Miñoso (born Saturnino Orestes Armas Miñoso Arrieta, November 29, 1925 – March 1, 2015) was a Cuban professional baseball player. He started playing in the Negro Leagues in 1946 and was an all-star third baseman for the New York Cubans. In 1949, he joined the Cleveland Indians of Major League Baseball (MLB) and later became an all-star left fielder for the Chicago White Sox. Miñoso was the first black Cuban in MLB and the first black player for the White Sox. In 1951, he played in his first MLB All-Star game. He was an American League (AL) All-Star for seven seasons and a three-time Gold Glove winner. He hit over.300 for eight seasons. Miñoso led the AL in triples and stolen bases three times each and in hits, doubles, and total bases once each. He and Willie Mays are credited with helping make speed an important part of baseball offense in the 1950s. Miñoso was known for reaching base, leading the AL in times hit by pitch ten times, and holding the league record for career times hit by pitch from 1959 to 1985. He was a great defender, leading AL left fielders in assists six times and in putouts and double plays four times each. Miñoso was very popular and played a key role in making the "Go-Go" White Sox a top team in the 1950s and 1960s. He set the White Sox record for career home runs from 1956 to 1974. After retiring from MLB in 1964, he played and coached in Mexico until 1973. He rejoined the White Sox as a coach and made brief appearances as a player in 1976 and 1980. He became the third player to get a hit after the age of 50 and the second player to appear in MLB in five decades. Miñoso's White Sox uniform number 9 was retired in 1983, and a statue of him was unveiled at U.S. Cellular Field in 2004. He was elected to the Cuban Baseball Hall of Fame in 1983 and to the Mexican Professional Baseball Hall of Fame in 1996. In 2014, he was considered for the National Baseball Hall of Fame but was not inducted in 2015.

Maaloula, or Maʿlūlā, is a town in the Rif Dimashq governorate of Syria. It is about 56 km northeast of Damascus. The town is built on a mountain, more than 1,500 meters above sea level. Maaloula is famous for being one of three villages where people still speak Western Neo-Aramaic. The other two villages are nearby: Jubb'adin and Bakhah.

Barrie is a city in central Ontario, Canada, near Lake Simcoe. It is part of Simcoe County but operates independently. Barrie is in a historically important area called Huronia and is part of the densely populated Greater Golden Horseshoe. As of 2016, Barrie had 141,434 people, making it the 34th largest city in Canada. The Barrie area grew quickly, becoming more popular as a place for people from Toronto to live. Barrie has easy access to Toronto and is about 100 kilometers north of it. The city first became settled during the War of 1812. It was named after Sir Robert Barrie in the 1830s. By the 1980s and 1990s, Barrie's population tripled. High-rise buildings and new beaches made Barrie popular for tourists. The city has a mix of jobs, with many people working in healthcare, education, and technology. Barrie is known for tourism and as a gateway to cottage country. Winters are cold and snowy, while summers are warm and humid.
Lie Sang Bong is a Korean fashion designer. He makes clothes for famous singers and actresses like Beyoncé, Rihanna, Lady Gaga, and Lindsay Lohan.

The River Shannon, the longest river in Ireland, is part of a basin covering one-fifth of Ireland's land area. It divides western Ireland, mainly the province of Connacht, from the east and south, which include Leinster and most of Munster. County Clare, although west of the Shannon, is part of Munster. The river acts as a major barrier, with only about thirty-five crossing points between Limerick city in the south and Dowra in the north. Named after the Celtic goddess Sionna, the Shannon has been an important waterway since ancient times, first mapped by Ptolemy. The river flows south from a source in County Cavan, turns west, and empties into the Atlantic Ocean through a long estuary. Limerick city is where the freshwater river meets the saltwater of the estuary. The river is tidal east of Limerick up to the Ardnacrusha dam.
Faverolles is a commune in France. It is in the Aisne department and the Hauts-de-France region, in the northern part of the country.

irma schultz keller, born on October 1, 1965, is a Swedish actress and pop singer. She has appeared in many Swedish movies and TV shows. She also acted in American productions like a horror movie and a miniseries. She studied at the Swedish National Academy of Mime and Acting and graduated in 1999. On March 3, 2007, irma keller and uno svenningsson performed a song called "God Morgen" in Melodifestivalen 2007. They performed as the duo Uno & Irma and made it to the second chance round. However, they lost to sonja alden in the first round and were eliminated from the contest.
afrodisiac can mean: a substance or food believed to increase sexual desire.

The Fahrenheit scale is a temperature measurement system. It was created in 1724 by Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit, who lived from 1686 to 1736. He used degrees Fahrenheit (symbol: °F) to measure temperature. Some accounts say he set the lower point at 0 °F, which is the freezing point of a mixture of water, ice, and ammonium chloride (a type of salt). He estimated the average human body temperature to be around 96 °F (about 2.6 °F less than today's value). He also noted 32 °F as the temperature of ice water. Now, the Fahrenheit scale is officially defined by two fixed points: 32 °F for the freezing point of pure water and 212 °F for the boiling point of water, both at sea level and under standard atmospheric pressure (180 °F apart). This scale was the first standardized temperature system widely used, though its use has decreased. Today, Fahrenheit is the official temperature scale in the United States, its territories, Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia, the Marshall Islands, the Cayman Islands, and Liberia. In some Caribbean islands, like Antigua and Barbuda, and countries like the Bahamas and Belize, both Fahrenheit and Celsius are used. A few British overseas territories, including the British Virgin Islands, Montserrat, Anguilla, and Bermuda, still use both scales. In the United Kingdom, degrees Fahrenheit are sometimes given along with degrees Celsius, as some people are more familiar with Fahrenheit. Most countries now use the Celsius scale, renamed from the centigrade scale in 1948 to honor Anders Celsius.

Diana Serra Cary, born Peggy-Jean Montgomery, was an American child film actress. Known as Baby Peggy, she also performed in vaudeville and wrote books. She was the last silent film star from Hollywood and the last person with a big career in silent films. Baby Peggy was one of three major American child stars during Hollywood's silent film era, alongside Jackie Coogan and Baby Marie. Between 1921 and 1923, she starred in over 150 short films for the Century Film Corporation. In 1922, she received many fan letters and was called "the million dollar baby" because of her high salary. Despite her fame and money as a child, she became poor in the 1930s and worked as an extra. As an adult, she wrote books and became a historian of silent films. She wrote a historical novel called "The Drowning of the Moon." She also helped protect the rights of child actors.

The Chinese Convert is a famous 1687 painting by Godfrey Kneller. It shows Chinese man Michael Alphonsius Shen Fu-tsung. King James II ordered the painting after meeting Shen Fu-tsung in 1685 during his visit to England. The king liked Shen so much that he had his portrait made and hung it in his bedroom. This portrait is still at Windsor Castle. Shen also visited Oxford and helped organize Chinese books at the Bodleian Library. Shen left China in 1681 with Philippe Couplet SJ for a trip to Europe. Couplet wanted to promote the China mission and talk to Pope Innocent XI about it. Couplet planned to take five Chinese candidates for the priesthood, including Wu Li (Simon de Cunha) and Shen Fuzhong (Michael Shen). In the end, only Michael Shen and another young candidate went with Couplet. This was possible because Michael Shen was a young Jesuit candidate, and in 1685, King James II was a Roman Catholic who allowed Jesuits at court. A year later, in 1688, King James II was overthrown by the Protestant William III. However, the meeting between King James II, Michael Shen Fuzong, and artist Godfrey Kneller led to the famous painting "The Chinese Convert."

Knott's Berry Farm is a theme park in Buena Park, California, run by Cedar Fair. In 2018, it was the twelfth-most-visited park in North America, with about 4 million visitors a year. The park has 40 rides, including roller coasters, family rides, dark rides, and water rides. The park started in the 1920s as a roadside berry stand owned by Walter Knott on State Route 39 in California. By the 1940s, a restaurant, shops, and other attractions were added to entertain more visitors, including a replica ghost town. Over the next two decades, the site became a modern amusement park, and an entrance fee was introduced in 1968. In 1997, Cedar Fair bought the park for $300 million. Two years earlier, in 1995, Knott's food business was bought by Conagra, Inc.

Ahmed Ben Bella was an Algerian politician and revolutionary. He was born on December 25, 1916, and died on April 11, 2012. Ben Bella was also a socialist and a soldier. He was the first president of Algeria, serving from 1963 to 1965.
Enrique Floriano Millán was born on October 9, 1982, in Lorca, Murcia. He is a vision-impaired swimmer from Spain. His swimming category is B2/S12.

Suva is Fiji's capital and largest city. It is on the southeast coast of Viti Levu, in the Rewa province, central division. In 1877, Suva became the capital because the old European town, Levuka, was too small. The government moved to Suva in 1882. According to the 2017 census, Suva had 93,970 people. Including nearby towns, the greater Suva area had 185,913 people. With nearby towns Lami, Nasinu, and Nausori, Suva and these towns together have about 330,000 people, which is more than a third of Fiji's population. Suva is important for politics, the economy, and culture in Fiji and the South Pacific. It hosts many regional offices of big companies and international organizations. Suva is also known for its art and fashion scenes.

In the United States, state courts handle most civil and criminal cases. These courts deal with disputes that have a connection to a specific state. Federal courts, which are smaller and have fewer judges, handle different types of cases. State courts are based on common law and use their state's laws and procedures. They follow their state's constitution, laws, and decisions from higher courts within the state. Federal laws are also applied when necessary. A judge usually decides cases in state courts. The judge hears trials for criminal or civil cases. However, most cases do not go to trial. Lower court decisions can be reviewed by a state court of appeals. The highest court for appeals is the state supreme court, which oversees the whole court system. For cases involving federal law, the state's highest court's final decision, or a refusal to hear an appeal, can be appealed to the U.S. Supreme Court. The U.S. Supreme Court can choose whether to hear these cases.

Vancouver is a big city in western Canada, located in British Columbia. It is the largest city in the province. In 2016, there were 631,486 people living in the city, an increase from 603,502 in 2011. The greater Vancouver area had 2,463,431 people in 2016, making it the third-largest in Canada. Vancouver is very crowded, with over 5,400 people per square kilometre. It is the fifth-most densely populated city in North America. Vancouver has many people from different backgrounds: 52% of its residents are not native English speakers, 48.9% speak neither English nor French, and 50.6% belong to visible minority groups. Vancouver is often named one of the best cities in the world for living and quality of life. The city plans to become the greenest in the world by 2020. Vancouver was originally called Gastown and started as a small settlement near Hastings Mill, built in 1867. The city was renamed Vancouver in 1886, due to a deal with the Canadian Pacific Railway. The railway reached the city by 1887. Vancouver's natural seaport on the Pacific Ocean was crucial for trade between Asia-Pacific, East Asia, Europe, and eastern Canada. Vancouver has hosted many important events, like the 1954 Commonwealth Games, UN Habitat I, Expo 86, APEC Canada 1997, the 1989 and 2009 World Police and Fire Games, matches of the 2015 FIFA Women's World Cup, and the 2010 Winter Olympics and Paralympics, which were held in Vancouver and Whistler, a nearby resort town. In 1969, Greenpeace was founded in Vancouver. The city is also known for being the home of Ted Talks since 2014. Port Metro Vancouver is one of the largest ports in North America, handling a lot of shipping. While forestry is its biggest industry, Vancouver is famous for tourism and for being a film production center, known as "Hollywood North."

Final Straw is Snow Patrol's third studio album and their first with a major label. It was released in the UK and Ireland on August 4, 2003, and in the US in 2004. The album brought the band their first big success outside Northern Ireland and Scotland. After its release, five singles came from it over 14 months. It was the first album with Nathan Connolly as the lead guitarist and the last with Mark McClelland as the bassist. In 2004, the UK version was re-released with two extra tracks, but the US version didn't have these bonus tracks. The album was also released in SACD and DualDisc with 5.1 surround mixes.
Sorel Etrog was born in Romania and later became an Israeli-Canadian artist, writer, and philosopher. He is known for his sculptures. He focused on modern art and contemporary sculptures.

Naughton is a village and former civil parish in Suffolk, England. Now it is part of the civil parish called Nedging-with-Naughton, in the Babergh district. Naughton is northwest of Ipswich and southwest of Stowmarket. Historically, Naughton was in the Cosford hundred of Suffolk. In 1935, the civil parish merged with Nedging. In 1931, the population of Naughton was 98. Naughton is where two roads meet. The Whatfield Road comes from the southwest and goes north to Nedging Tye. The New Road comes from the southeast. There is a 14th-century church called St. Mary's, made of flint. The church is in the center of the village, just west of where the roads meet.

Washburn County is in the state of Maine, U.S. In 2010, it had 32, 856 people, which made it the least populous county in Maine. Its main town is Machias. The county was created on June 25, 1789. It shares a border with New Brunswick, a part of Canada. Sometimes, it's called "Sunrise County" because it has the easternmost point in the U.S. Some people say the sun first rises here in the 48 states. Many small towns near the sea have fishing as their main job. Tourism is also important near the shore, but not as much as in other parts of the state. Blueberries are very important for the local economy.
Rubén Galván can be about: One person Multiple people with the same name

The Camp David Accords were signed on September 17, 1978, by Egyptian President Anwar Sadat and Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin. They met for secret talks at Camp David, a U.S. president's retreat in Maryland, for 12 days. President Jimmy Carter was present when they signed two important agreements at the White House. The second agreement, called "A Framework for the Conclusion of a Peace Treaty Between Egypt and Israel," directly led to the 1979 Egypt-Israel Peace Treaty. Sadat and Begin shared the 1978 Nobel Peace Prize for this achievement. The first agreement, known as "A Framework for Peace in the Middle East," dealt with Palestinian territories but was not discussed with Palestinians. It was criticized by the United Nations. Historian Jørgen Jensehaugen says that when Carter left office in January 1981, this agreement was still in place.

Richard Lester Liebman, born on January 19, 1932, is known as Dick Lester. He is a retired film director living in the United Kingdom. Lester directed the Beatles in the 1960s and worked on "Superman" films in the 1980s. He is also connected to the London Film School as an honorary associate.
The Royal New Zealand Navy (RNZN) is part of New Zealand's defense force. Its ships are called "Warriors of the Sea of New Zealand." Currently, it has eight ships in its fleet.

The Detroit Pistons are an American basketball team based in Detroit. They play in the National Basketball Association (NBA) and compete in the Eastern Conference Central Division. Their home games are at Little Caesars Arena in Midtown. The team started in Fort Wayne, Indiana in 1941 as the Fort Wayne Pistons. They won two championships in the National Basketball League (NBL) in 1944 and 1945. In 1948, they joined the Basketball Association of America (BAA). The NBL and BAA merged to form the NBA in 1949, and the Pistons became part of the new league. In 1957, the team moved to Detroit. The Pistons have won three NBA championships: in 1989, 1990, and 2004.

Maximilian Kolbe, born Rajmund Kolbe on January 8, 1894, and later known as Saint Maximilian Kolbe, was a Polish Catholic priest and Franciscan friar. During World War II, in a German death camp called Auschwitz, which was in occupied Poland, he volunteered to die instead of a stranger. Maximilian was active in promoting the veneration of the Virgin Mary and started a monastery near Warsaw. He also ran several organizations and publications. On October 10, 1982, Pope John Paul II declared him a saint and a martyr of charity. The Catholic Church honors him as the patron saint of amateur-radio operators, drug addicts, political prisoners, families, journalists, prisoners, and the pro-life movement. John Paul II called him "the patron saint of our difficult century." His feast day is August 14, the day he died. Because of his work to promote devotion to Mary, he is known as "the apostle of consecration to Mary."

The Renault FR1 was a single-decker coach made by Renault Trucks Bus Division in France from 1987 to 1997. It had a 6-cylinder Renault engine with 9,834 cc displacement. There were three models: TE, TX, and GTX. You could choose 1 or 2 doors. In 1997, the model was updated and renamed Renault Iliade to replace the normal FR1.

Snakes are long, legless, and eat meat. They are cold-blooded, have no legs, and are covered in scales. Some snake species have more flexible jaws, letting them eat food larger than their heads. Their organs, like kidneys, are stacked instead of side by side, and most only have one lung. Some have tiny vestigial legs near their bottom. Lizards have evolved into legless forms many times, like snakes, through similar adaptations. Some legless lizards have eyelids and ears, unlike most snakes. Snakes live almost everywhere except Antarctica, including many islands. Some species can grow to be very long, like the reticulated python, which can be over 20 feet long. The smallest snake, the Barbados thread snake, is just a few inches long. Fossils suggest snakes evolved from lizards that burrowed or lived in water, possibly during the Jurassic period, with the oldest snake fossils dating back millions of years. Modern snake diversity emerged after a big extinction event around 66 million years ago. Some of the earliest written records of snakes come from ancient Egyptian papyri. Most snakes are harmless, but they can eat prey alive or squeeze them to kill. Only some snakes have venom strong enough to harm humans.

Kambaata is a highland East Cushitic language, part of the Afro-Asiatic family. It is spoken by the Kambaata people. There are different dialects: Kambaata, Tambaro, Alaba, and K'abeena. Kambaata is one of the official languages in Ethiopia. This language has many verbal affixes. When added to verb roots, these affixes cause many sound changes. Kambaata follows the SOV order (subject-object-verb). Its phonemes include five distinct vowels (both long and short), ejectives, a retroflexed implosive, and a glottal stop. The New Testament and some parts of the Old Testament have been translated into Kambaata. Initially, they were published using the Ethiopian syllabary (New Testament in 1992), but later they were republished using Latin letters to match new policies.

Sandpipers are a large family of birds that live near the shore. They include species called sandpipers, curlews, and snipes. These birds eat small creatures they find in the mud or soil. Different species have different bill lengths, which let them feed in the same area without competing. Sandpipers have long bodies and legs, and narrow wings. Their bills are sensitive, helping them find food. Most are small to medium-sized, ranging in size. They have plain colors, usually brown or gray, but can be brighter during breeding. Sandpipers nest in open areas and lay 3 to 4 eggs. Their young can move around soon after hatching.
Lantsch/Lenz is a town in the Albula area of Graubünden in Switzerland. Most people there speak Romansh.
Gadfly most commonly refers to a fly that annoys animals. Gadfly may also refer to someone who criticizes or disturbs.

Denis Farkasfalvy was born on June 23, 1936, and died on May 20, 2020. He was a Hungarian-American Catholic priest and monk in the Cistercian order. He was also an abbot, theologian, author, and translator.

Olga Maria Elisabeth Schwarzkopf, born on December 9, 1915, and died on August 3, 2006, was a German-born singer who worked in Britain. She was known for singing lieder, and was famous for her performances of Viennese operetta, as well as Mozart, Wagner, and Strauss operas. After stopping performing, she taught singing around the world. She is considered one of the best sopranos of the 20th century.

The Sri Lankan civil war lasted from 1983 to 2009. It started on July 23, 1983, when Tamil Tiger rebels, led by Velupillai Prabhakaran, began an armed struggle against the government. They wanted to create an independent Tamil state called Tamil Eelam in Sri Lanka's north and east because Tamils faced discrimination from the Sinhalese-dominated government. This was partly due to violent attacks on Tamils in 1956, 1958, 1977, and 1981. The war ended in May 2009 when the Sri Lankan army defeated the Tamil Tigers. The war caused many deaths and problems. Over 80,000 people died during the conflict. The Sri Lankan forces tried to retake areas captured by the Tamil Tigers. The Tigers were listed as a terrorist group in 32 countries because of their violent tactics. The Sri Lankan government was accused of human rights abuses, like detaining people without trial and disappearing people. Peace talks failed for many years. In 2001, a ceasefire was declared, but fighting continued. The government broke the ceasefire in 2008. In 2009, the Sri Lankan army drove the Tamil Tigers out of the eastern province and then from the north. The Tamil Tigers admitted defeat on May 17, 2009. After the war, the Tamil National Alliance, which supported the Tamil Tigers, dropped their demand for a separate state. The Sri Lankan government set up a commission to look into the conflict. However, the end of the war was marked by accusations of human rights violations, including killing and ethnic cleansing. The Tamil Tigers were known for doing very bad attacks, like suicide bombings. A day is now remembered each year to honor those who died in the final stages of the war.

The team captain in association football is a chosen player who leads the team on the field. They are often one of the older or more experienced players, or someone who can strongly affect the game. The captain is usually identified by wearing a armband.
Mitrović comes from the name "Saint Demetrius" or "Sveti Dimitrije" (in Cyrillic: "Свети Димитрије"). This name might refer to:

A rhetorical question is one where the person asking doesn't expect a direct answer. Often, such a question is used to begin a conversation or to show the speaker's opinion. For example, the question "Can't you do anything right?" is meant to point out the listener's lack of ability, not to ask about their skills.
Morrowcourt is a commune in the Aisne department, which is in Hauts-de-France in northern France.

piedmont blues, also called east coast or southeastern blues, mainly refers to a guitar style known as piedmont fingerstyle. This style uses fingerpicking, with a steady bass pattern from the thumb on the lower strings and a syncopated melody on the higher strings, usually picked with the forefinger. It sounds similar to ragtime or stride piano. The term was created by blues researcher Peter B. Lowry, with help from Bruce Bastin. The piedmont style has different rhythms compared to the Mississippi Delta blues.
Moore Haven is a city in Florida, United States. It is the county seat of Glades County. The population was 1,680 in 2010. Moore Haven is on the southwest side of Lake Okeechobee.

In the 1980 Democratic primaries, voters chose the party's presidential nominee. The incumbent president, Jimmy Carter, was chosen again through primary elections and caucuses. This process led to the 1980 Democratic National Convention in New York City from August 11 to 14. Senator Ted Kennedy from Massachusetts was Carter's main opponent. Kennedy won 12 contests and got over seven million votes. He refused to give up the nomination until the second day of the convention. This was the last time an incumbent president's party nomination was contested before the convention.

Sin City is a series of comics. American writer-artist Frank Miller created it. The first story came out in 1991. Other stories followed. The stories are set in a place called Basin City and often feature the same characters. A film based on Sin City was made in 2005 by Robert Rodriguez and Frank Miller. A sequel was released in 2014. A new TV series based on Sin City is being developed. It will have new characters and timelines, and will be more like the original comics.

Villach is the seventh-largest city in Austria and the second-largest in the state of Carinthia. It is an important place for transportation in southern Austria and the Alpe-Adria region. The population is 61,887. Villach works with other mountain towns in the Alpine Town of the Year association. This is to help achieve sustainable development in the Alpine Arc. Villach was the first town to receive the Alpine Town of the Year award in 1997.

Lindsey Nelson was born on May 25, 1919, and died on June 10, 1995. He was an American sportscaster known for his long career. Nelson called the play-by-play for college football and New York Mets baseball. He worked with the Mets for 17 years and with the San Francisco Giants for 3 years. For 33 years, Nelson covered college football, including 26 Cotton Bowls, 5 Sugar Bowls, 4 Rose Bowls, and 14 years of Notre Dame games. He was inducted into 13 separate halls of fame. Fans remember Nelson as a talented broadcaster, an excellent storyteller, and a true sports lover. His colorful broadcasts and enthusiastic speaking style made him one of the best in the industry.

Brooke Shields, born on May 31, 1965, is an American actress and model. She began her career as a child model and got a lot of praise when she was 12 for her role in the movie "Pretty Baby" (1978). In this film, she played a child prostitute in New Orleans at the start of the 20th century. Shields became well-known for this role and kept modeling until her late teens. She also acted in some dramas during the 1980s, such as "The Blue Lagoon" (1980) and "Endless Love" (1981). Lorenzo Cherubini, born on September 27, 1966, performs under the name Jovanotti. Jovanotti means "young man" in Italian. potsdamer platz is a important square and crossing in the middle of berlin, close to the brandenburg gate and the reichstag, and near the southeast corner of the tiergarten park. It is named after the city of potsdam, southwest of berlin. This place used to be where an old road from potsdam went through the old walls of berlin at a place called the potsdam gate. In about 100 years, it grew from a simple intersection to one of the busiest traffic crossings in europe. During world war ii, it was completely destroyed. After the war, it was left empty until the berlin wall was built, dividing its area. Since berlin became one country again, lots of new buildings and projects have been built at potsdamer platz.

Sir John Grant MacKenzie Laws lived from May 10, 1945, to April 5, 2020. He was a Lord Justice of Appeal. He worked from 1999 to 2016. He taught as the Goodhart Visiting Professor of Legal Science at the University of Cambridge. He was also an honorary fellow of Robinson College, Cambridge.

Massimo Mattioli, born on September 25, 1943, and died on August 23, 2019, was an Italian artist and cartoonist. He started his career in 1965 in the comic book "Il Vittorioso," with a work called "Vermetto Sigh." He also worked on "Corto Maltese" and "Frigidaire." Kensington is a town in Montgomery County, Maryland, United States. It had 2,213 people in 2010. Greater Kensington includes the whole area with the zip code 20895, and has 19,054 people.
patrick dennistoun mcgorry, born on September 10, 1952, is an Australian psychiatrist. He is known for creating early intervention services to help young people with mental disorders.

Fratton Park is a football ground in Portsmouth, a city in England. It is the original home of Portsmouth F.C., founded on April 5, 1898. Fratton Park is special because it is on an island, Portsea Island, and not on the mainland of Great Britain. The stadium was built in 1899 on a potato field in Milton, a village that later became part of Portsmouth. Fratton Park opened on August 15, 1899, and hosted its first match on September 6, 1899, against Southampton F.C., with 4,141 people watching. The stadium is named after the nearby Fratton railway station, which is about one mile away. This helped fans think it was closer and easier to reach by public transport. Fratton Park could hold up to 58,000 people in 1935, but the highest number of people who watched a match was 51,385. Since 1996, it can hold fewer people because of all-seated seating. Fans call the ground "The Old Girl." Recently, it has been called "Fortress Fratton" because it is known for having many people watching matches and a strong football atmosphere.

Naomie Melanie Harris, born on September 6, 1976, is an English actress. She started her acting career as a child, appearing in the TV series "Simon and the Witch" in 1987. She acted in the zombie movie "28 Days Later" in 2002. In the "Pirates of the Caribbean" series, she played the witch Tia Dalma in the second and third films. She also acted as Winnie Mandela in a 2013 film. In the "James Bond" films "Skyfall" (2012) and "Spectre" (2015), she played Eve Moneypenny. She will reprise this role in the upcoming film "No Time to Die" in 2020. In 2016, she starred in the movie "Moonlight," which received great reviews. Her performance earned her nominations for a Golden Globe, BAFTA, and Academy Award for best supporting actress. In 2017, she was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire for her services to drama.

The grand tour was a tradition in the 17th and 18th centuries where young, wealthy European men from upper-class families traveled through Europe when they were about 21 years old. They usually went with a family member, like a chaperone. This trip helped them learn about history and culture, and it was seen as an important part of growing up. Wealthy young men from other Northern European countries, and some from North and South America, also made similar trips. By the mid-18th century, this journey was common among the aristocracy in Central Europe too, but mostly for higher nobility. The grand tour became less popular as interest in classical culture decreased. It was largely replaced by easier travel by train and ship, which also saw the rise of group tours like Thomas Cook's "Cook's Tour." By 2008, the grand tour was seen as a way to learn about ancient and Renaissance art and meet other aristocratic people in Europe. The trip could last from a few months to several years, and a knowledgeable guide or tutor, called a cicerone, often accompanied these young men. Even today, the idea of the grand tour still influences travel choices and ideas about culture. While the grand tour was mostly for aristocrats, artists also started traveling to learn about painting and sculpture. Guides like Jonathan Richardson and his son published books that made these trips more popular. In Rome, tourists could buy and take home marble statues, coins, and medals. Some artists, like Pompeo Batoni, painted these tourists with Roman antiquities. Many travelers also went to Naples to see Herculaneum and Pompeii, but few ventured much further south in Italy, and even fewer traveled to Greece, which was still under Turkish rule.

The banker horse is a breed of wild horse living on barrier islands in North Carolina's Outer Banks. They are small, strong, and gentle. These horses came from domesticated Spanish horses that might have been brought to America in the 1500s. They may have become wild after surviving shipwrecks or being left on the islands by explorers. These islands include Ocracoke, Shackleford Banks, Currituck Banks, Cedar Island, and the Rachel Carson Estuarine Sanctuary. The horses can stay on the islands because of their history, even though they might damage plants and animals. They eat marsh grass, which gives them water and food. They also get temporary freshwater pools. To stop too many horses and inbreeding, and protect their habitat, the horses are managed by the National Park Service, the state of North Carolina, and some private groups. They check the horses for sickness, like equine infectious anemia, which was found and stopped in Shackleford in 1996. The horses are also protected from traffic on North Carolina Highway 12. Horse numbers on the islands are controlled by adopting some horses and using birth control. Some wild banker horses that are trained can be used for riding, driving, and sometimes for patrols.

Miriam Margolyes, born on May 18, 1941, is a British-Australian actress and comedian. She started her career in theater. Later, she had supporting roles in films and TV shows. For her role in "The Age of Innocence," directed by Martin Scorsese, she won a BAFTA award in 1993. She is also known for playing Professor Sprout in the "Harry Potter" films. Margolyes spends time in England, Australia, and Italy. She has acted in plays in both countries. She became an Australian citizen in 2013.
Chavenon is a commune in the Allier department, which is in Auvergne, in central France.

An eagle is a common name for many large birds of prey in the family Accipitridae. These birds are from different groups, but they are not all closely related. Most of the 60 eagle species live in Eurasia and Africa. Only 14 species can be found outside this area—2 in North America, 9 in Central and South America, and 3 in Australia.

A chemical substance is a type of matter that always has the same makeup and typical properties. Sometimes, it can't be separated into simpler parts using physical methods, meaning chemical bonds stay intact. Chemical substances can be simple elements, compounds, or alloys. Depending on how you look at it, they might also include chemical elements. People often call pure chemical substances 'pure' to show they are different from mixtures. For example, pure water, carbon, gold, salt, and sugar are common pure chemical substances. Even though they might not be completely pure in real life, their use depends on what we need them for. Chemical substances can be solids, liquids, gases, or plasma. They can change forms depending on temperature or pressure. Chemical substances can turn into others through chemical reactions. Energy forms like light and heat are not matter and thus not considered substances in this way.

NBC is an American TV and radio network owned by NBCUniversal, a part of Comcast. Its main offices are in New York City, Los Angeles, Chicago, and Philadelphia. NBC is one of the three major TV networks in the U.S. and is called the "Peacock Network" because of its peacock logo introduced in 1956. The network was founded in 1926 by RCA and has been operating longer than most major TV networks in the U.S. In 1932, RCA had to sell NBC due to antitrust issues. In 1986, General Electric (GE) bought NBC. Bob Wright became CEO in 1986 and stepped down in 2007, replaced by Jeff Zucker. In 2003, NBCUniversal was formed when GE combined its entertainment assets with French company Vivendi. Comcast bought a controlling stake in 2011 and fully acquired GE's share in 2013. Under Comcast, Steve Burke became CEO. NBC has 13 stations it owns and operates and nearly 200 affiliates in the U.S. and its territories, with some also in Canada and Mexico.
multiple-camera setup uses several cameras to film or broadcast a scene at the same time. This is different from a single-camera setup, which uses just one camera.

Lopp Lagoon is a tidal lake located north of Cape Prince of Wales on the Seward Peninsula in Alaska. Many small rivers flow into it, but the most water comes from the Mint River. Some salt water from the Pacific Ocean also enters the lagoon through several channels. It was named in 1900 after William Thomas Lopp, a missionary and leader who helped Inuit people and supported an overland expedition in 1897-98. Historically, Lopp Lagoon has been an important source of food, such as salmon and waterfowl, for people living in the Wales area of Alaska.

Paulo César Wanchope Watson, known as Paulo Wanchope, was born on July 31, 1976. He is a former Costa Rican footballer and used to coach the Costa Rica national football team. Wanchope is the second highest goalscorer for Costa Rica in international matches, behind Rolando Fonseca. He scored 45 goals in 73 games for his country. Wanchope scored against Brazil in 2002 and had two goals against Germany in 2006. He is the top goalscorer for Costa Rica in the FIFA World Cup, a record he shares with Rónald Gómez.

Poygan is a town in Winnebago County, Wisconsin, United States. The town had 1,301 people living there in 2010.

Port Vila, or simply Vila, is the capital and largest city of Vanuatu. It is on the island of Efate. In 2009, its population was 44,040, up from 29,356 in 1999. In 2009, Vila made up 18.8% of Vanuatu's population and 66.9% of Efate's population. Located on the south coast of Efate in Shefa Province, Port Vila is Vanuatu's economic and commercial center. The mayor is Erick Puyo Festa from the Vanua'aku Pati, elected in January 2018. His deputy is Jenny Regenvanu from the Graun Mo Jastis Pati. In March 2015, Port Vila was damaged by Cyclone Pam.

The Division of Brisbane is an electoral area in the state of Queensland, Australia.

Municipalities, or "municipios" in Spanish, are the second-level administrative divisions in Mexico. The first-level division is called a "state" or "estado" in Spanish. As of September 2017, there are 2,448 municipalities in Mexico, not counting the 16 "delegaciones" in Mexico City. The internal political organization and responsibilities of municipalities are described in Article 115 of the 1917 constitution and detailed in the constitutions of the states. Municipalities are different from cities. Some municipalities can be as large as states, while cities are measured in blocks.

Equivalent weight, also called gram equivalent, is the mass of a substance that reacts with or combines with a fixed amount of another substance. For an element, its equivalent weight is the mass that combines with or displaces 1.008 grams of hydrogen, 8.0 grams of oxygen, or 35.5 grams of chlorine. These values are calculated by dividing the atomic weight by the usual valence, such as 16.0 grams divided by 2 for oxygen. In acid-base reactions, the equivalent weight of an acid or base is the mass that provides or reacts with one mole of hydrogen ions. In redox reactions, it is the mass that supplies or reacts with one mole of electrons. Equivalent weight is measured in units of mass, like grams. Atomic weight, in contrast, has no dimensions. Equivalent weights were originally found through experiments, but now they are calculated from molar masses. The equivalent weight of a compound can be found by dividing its molecular weight by the number of positive or negative electrical charges it forms when dissolved.

Pegomastax, meaning "strong jaw," is a type of heterodontosaurid dinosaur found in South Africa. It is based on a partial skull, including a postorbital bone, lower jaw bones, and a predentary. This herbivore, which looked like a parrot, was only about 60 cm long. It was found in Voyizane, Joe Gqabi District, in the upper Elliot Formation. This rock layer is from the early Jurassic period, about 200 to 190 million years ago. It was discovered in 1966-1967 but wasn't named until 2012 by Paul Sereno, who first noticed it was special in the 1980s. The type species is Pegomastax africana. Pegomastax had a robust lower jaw with a short beak. Like other heterodontosaurids, it had a large, canine-like tooth at the start of its lower jaw, possibly for defense.

Ándres Muschietti, born on August 26, 1973, is an Argentine filmmaker. He gained recognition in 2013 with the film "Mama," which he made with his sister, Barbara Muschietti, who is a producer and screenwriter. This film, which he directed at age 39, caught the attention of Guillermo del Toro, who then worked as an executive producer. Muschietti became even more famous for directing two films in the "It" series. The first, "It" in 2017, was based on Stephen King's novel and became the highest-grossing horror film ever. The second film, "It Chapter Two" in 2019, was also successful. Both were made by Warner Bros. and produced by New Line Cinema. Muschietti is planning to direct two more films for Warner Bros.: "The Flash," a movie about the DC superhero, and an adaptation of "Attack on Titan." He will also direct a remake of "The Howling" for Netflix.

Chamely Khatun, born on November 11, 1988, is a Bangladeshi cricketer. She plays for the Bangladesh national women's cricket team. She bats with her right hand and bowls with her right arm as a slow bowler.

Anizy-le-Grand is a town in the Aisne department, which is in Hauts-de-France, a region in northern France. It became a single town on January 1, 2019, by combining Anizy-le-Château, Faucoucourt, and Lizy.

The Hanshin Tigers (Japanese: 阪神タイガース "hanshin taigāsu") are a professional baseball team in Japan. They play in the Central League and are based in Nishinomiya, Hyōgo Prefecture. Dokaor toongtong is a Thai singer from the Isan region. She performs "luk thung" and "mor lam sing" music. Her popular songs are "Ber Tho Jao Choo," "Oak Hak Wan Hae Tiean," "Miea Kao," and "Rak Phay Thee Kaeng Saphue." She is also known as Aor or "Sao Sieng Sor."

Bad Doberan was a former district in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Germany. It got its name from its biggest town, Bad Doberan, where "bad" means "spa" in German. The district surrounded Rostock and touched the Baltic Sea in the north. It also bordered the former districts of Nordvorpommern, Güstrow, and Nordwestmecklenburg. Efficiency measures how well input is used to achieve a task. It is about producing a desired result with minimal waste. Effectiveness, on the other hand, is about achieving the desired result, which is simpler to measure. Efficiency can be expressed as a percentage, showing how much of an ideal outcome is reached. Effectiveness can be measured without complicated math, focusing on whether the desired result is achieved. Efficiency and effectiveness are often confused. Efficiency is about doing things correctly, while effectiveness is about doing the right things. The saying “efficiency is doing things right, while effectiveness is doing the right things” highlights that choosing goals is as important as the process. Efficiency is measured by the ratio of useful output to total input. This can be shown with the formula: \( r = \frac{p}{c} \), where \( p \) is the amount of useful output and \( c \) is the resources used. For example, in engines, the output is work, and the input is heat. Efficiency can never be more than 100% because energy cannot be created. In summary, efficiency focuses on how well resources are used to achieve results, while effectiveness focuses on whether the desired results are achieved.

"Beautiful Inside" is Louise's 10th solo song released in 2000. It's from her third solo album called "Elbow Beach." The song uses a part from another song called "Different Strokes" by Syl Johnson. It also used by the Wu-Tang Clan. The song reached number 13 on the UK singles chart.

The World Trade Organization (WTO) is an international group that makes rules about trade between countries. It started on January 1, 1995, after a big meeting in Marrakesh. Before that, there was an organization called GATT that began in 1948. The WTO is the biggest group of this kind in the world. The WTO helps countries make trade agreements and solve arguments about them. It stops countries from treating each other unfairly in trade, but allows some exceptions. Disputes are handled by judges who work for the WTO. The WTO has a leader called the Director-General. Now, Roberto Azevêdo leads a team of over 600 people from their offices in Geneva, Switzerland. In 2013, all countries agreed on the first big new rule since the WTO started. This rule is about making trade easier. In 2017, they also changed a rule about protecting inventions, which helps developing countries get cheaper medicines and other things. Studies show that the WTO has made trade better and helped countries trade more. Many new trade agreements mention the WTO because it has such a big influence on how trade rules are made.

Julian Clare May, born on July 10, 1931, and died on October 17, 2017, was an American writer. She wrote stories in science fiction, fantasy, horror, science, and children's genres. She used several pretend names when publishing her work. She is most famous for her "Saga of Pliocene Exile" series and the "Galactic Milieu" series.

Maurice Petty was born on March 27, 1939, and passed away on July 25, 2020. He was from the United States. Maurice worked as a crew chief and engine builder for Petty Enterprises. He was one of the owners. In 2011, he was honored by being inducted into the International Motorsports Hall of Fame. He was also honored in 2014 by being inducted into the NASCAR Hall of Fame. He was the first engine builder to receive this honor.
Saint-Julien-de-Mailloc was a village in Calvados, in Normandy, in northwestern France. On January 1, 2016, it became part of a new village called Vorbiquet.

West Palm Beach is a city in Palm Beach County, Florida, United States. It is located to the west of Palm Beach, which is on a barrier island across Lake Worth Lagoon. In 2010, the population was 99,919. West Palm Beach is part of the Miami metropolitan area, which had about 6,158,824 people in 2017. It is the oldest city in South Florida, incorporated in November 1894, two years before Miami. West Palm Beach is roughly north of downtown Miami.

Andromeda is one of the 48 constellations listed by the 2nd-century Greco-Roman astronomer Ptolemy and is still one of the 88 modern constellations. Named after Andromeda, the daughter of Cassiopeia in Greek mythology, who was chained to a rock to be eaten by the sea monster Cetus, it is best seen in autumn evenings in the northern hemisphere. Andromeda is mostly visible north of 40° south latitude. This constellation is large, covering 722 square degrees, which is over 1,400 times the size of the full moon and more than 10 times the size of the smallest constellation, Crux. Its brightest star, Alpha Andromedae, is a binary star. Gamma Andromedae is a colorful binary and popular among amateur astronomers. Beta Andromedae, which is only slightly less bright, is a red giant visible to the naked eye. Andromeda's most obvious deep-sky object is the Andromeda Galaxy (M31), the closest spiral galaxy to our Milky Way and one of the brightest Messier objects. Other galaxies, like M110 and M32, and more distant NGC 891, are also found within Andromeda. The Blue Snowball Nebula, a planetary nebula, can be seen in a telescope. In Chinese astronomy, Andromeda's stars belonged to four different constellations with astrological and mythological significance. Andromeda is also the location of the radiant for the Andromedids, a weak meteor shower that happens in November.

ncaa division ii (D-II) is a middle-level division in the national collegiate athletic association. It gives schools a choice between larger, better-funded division i and the no-scholarship environment of division iii. Before 1973, the ncaa's smaller schools were in the college division. In 1973, the college division split into two when the ncaa started using numbers. Schools that wanted to offer scholarships became division ii, while those that did not became division iii. Now, espn televises the football championship game, cbs shows the men's basketball championship, and espn2 broadcasts the women's basketball championship. Stadium televises six regular-season football games on Thursdays and one men's basketball game each Saturday during the regular season. The official slogan for ncaa division ii is "make it yours," which was introduced in 2015.
Bartholomäberg is a municipality and a popular tourist destination in the Bludenz district of Vorarlberg, Austria.

A steel mill is a factory where steel is made. It can be a place that does all the steps from melting iron ore to making rolled steel products. Alternatively, it can refer to a plant that makes steel semi-finished products from molten iron or scrap.

SAG was a union in America for actors and actresses in films and TV. It had more than 100,000 members worldwide. On March 30, 2012, SAG decided to merge with AFTRA, forming SAG-AFTRA. SAG’s goal was to make sure its members got fair pay and good working conditions. They also protected their members when their performances were used without permission. The union wanted to help its members find more work. SAG was created in 1933 to stop actors from being forced into unfair contracts by big movie studios. These contracts didn’t have rules about working hours or rest. They often automatically renewed, giving studios control over actors' lives. SAG was part of AAAA, which is a group for actors' unions in America and is connected to AFL-CIO. SAG worked with AFTRA, which had 44,000 members in common. SAG had offices in Hollywood and many big cities in the US, like Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Dallas, Denver, Detroit, Honolulu, Houston, Las Vegas, Miami, Nashville, New York City, New Orleans, Philadelphia, Phoenix, Portland, Salt Lake City, San Diego, San Francisco, Seattle, and Washington, D.C. Since 1995, SAG gave out Screen Actors Guild Awards yearly. These awards are seen as a sign of success for Oscar nominees. After the merger, SAG-AFTRA continued to give these awards.

Thomas P. Tiffany was born on December 30, 1957. He is an American businessman and politician. Tiffany has been the U.S. representative for Wisconsin's 7th congressional district since 2020. He is a member of the Republican Party. Before becoming a federal representative, Tiffany served in the Wisconsin State Assembly from 2011 to 2013 and in the Wisconsin Senate from 2013 to 2020. Tiffany took over the seat from Republican Sean Duffy after winning a special election against Democrat Tricia Zunker.

Ronald Gabriel Palillo was an American actor and teacher. He was born on April 2, 1949, and passed away on August 14, 2012. He is best known for playing a silly, not-so-smart character named Arnold Horshack in a TV show called "Welcome Back, Kotter" from 1975 to 1979.

Arch Enemy is a Swedish melodic death metal band. They were formed in 1995 in Halmstad. Some of the band members came from other bands like Carcass, Carnage, and Mercyful Fate. It was started by Michael Amott, a guitarist from Carcass, and Johan Liiva, who was from Carnage. The band has made ten studio albums, three live albums, three video albums, and four EPs. Initially, Johan Liiva was the lead singer. He was replaced by Angela Gossow from Germany in 2000. Angela left the band in 2014 to manage it and was replaced by Alissa White-Gluz from Canada.

Canadian National Railway is a big train company in Canada. It is based in Montreal, Quebec, and it operates in Canada and parts of the United States. CN is the largest railway company in Canada by both money earned and the length of its tracks, covering most of the country from the east coast to the west coast, spanning about 50,000 kilometers. In the late 20th century, it grew bigger in the United States by taking over other train companies, including the Illinois Central. CN is a public company with about 24,000 workers. As of July 2019, its value was about $90 billion Canadian dollars. Before 1995, CN was owned by the Canadian government as a crown corporation. In 2019, Bill Gates owned the most shares of CN stock. CN was known as Canadian National Railways (CNR) from 1919 to 1960, and as Canadian National (CN) from 1960 to now.

Jefferson County is in the state of Iowa. In 2010, it had 16, 843 people. The county seat is Fairfield. Jefferson County was created in January 1839 and is named after President Thomas Jefferson. It includes the Fairfield, IA micropolitan area.

Lester Bruce McDonald was born on September 19, 1914, and died on July 26, 1971. He played American football as an end in the National Football League (NFL). Lester played for the Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions, and Philadelphia Eagles. He played college football at the University of Nebraska. He was chosen as the eighth player in the first round of the 1937 NFL draft.
