Princeton is a city in Mercer County, West Virginia, United States. It is the county seat. People often call Princeton the "jewel of the south" or the "heart of Mercer County." In 2010, the city's population was 6,432. Princeton is part of the Bluefield, WV-VA micropolitan area, which has 107,342 people. The city also has a baseball team called the Princeton Rays that plays in the Appalachian League.

The Inca civil war, also known as the Inca war of succession or the war of the two brothers, was a conflict between half-brothers Huáscar and Atahualpa. They were sons of Huayna Capac and fought over who would rule the Inca Empire. The war began in 1529 and lasted until 1532. Huáscar started the war because he claimed to be the rightful king. Atahualpa was better at fighting and had stronger armies in the north part of the empire. Different sources give different details about the war. After Atahualpa won, Spanish forces led by Francisco Pizarro invaded. They captured and killed Atahualpa after he paid a ransom to be freed.

Raymond Poulidor, nicknamed "Pou-Pou," was a French professional cyclist born on April 15, 1936, and died on November 13, 2019. He rode bicycles for his entire career. Poulidor's career was notable, even though he rode during the time of great cyclists Jacques Anquetil and Eddy Merckx. He was often seen as the underdog, which made people like him a lot. People called him "the eternal second" because he never won the Tour de France but came in second place three times and third place five times, including when he was 40 years old. Despite his consistent performance, Poulidor never wore the yellow jersey as the leader in any of the 14 Tours he finished, completing 12 of them. However, he did win one grand tour, the 1964 Vuelta a España.

Electronic paper, sometimes called electronic ink or electrophoretic display, is a type of display that looks like regular ink on paper. Unlike other flat screens that give off light, electronic paper reflects light, making it easier on the eyes and offering a wider viewing angle. By 2008, electronic displays had a contrast similar to newspapers. Some new electronic paper displays improved on this. An ideal electronic paper display can be read clearly in bright sunlight. Many electronic paper technologies can show text and images without needing electricity. Flexible electronic paper uses plastic materials. It can be used in various ways, such as shelf labels, digital signs, bus timetables, billboards, smartphone screens, and e-readers displaying digital books and magazines.
Torcy is a town in the Pas-de-Calais area of northern France.

Tali Tali Pompey was an Aboriginal artist from Central Australia. She started painting in 2002. By the time she stopped, her work was in many important galleries. She lived from about 1945/47 to November 16, 2011.

The Bridgeport Sound Tigers are a professional ice hockey team. They play in the American Hockey League (AHL). The Sound Tigers are connected to the New York Islanders, which are in the National Hockey League (NHL). The Sound Tigers began playing in 2001-2002 and were bought by the New York Islanders in 2004. The team is from Bridgeport, Connecticut, and they play their home games at the Webster Bank Arena.

Rutgerus Johannes Martinus van Nistelrooy, born on July 1, 1976, is a Dutch football coach and former player. He is currently coaching the PSV Eindhoven under-19s team and works as an assistant manager for the Netherlands. Van Nistelrooy was a top striker and is often considered one of the best of his era. He was the top scorer in three UEFA Champions League seasons and is the sixth-highest goalscorer in the competition's history with 56 goals. He also led the top scorer in three different European domestic leagues. Van Nistelrooy started his career with Den Bosch, then moved to Heerenveen and eventually gained fame at PSV Eindhoven, winning two Eredivisie titles. His goal-scoring at PSV caught the attention of Manchester United, who signed him in 2001 for a record fee of £19 million. His time at United was successful; he won the Premier League, FA Cup, Football League Cup, and FA Community Shield, and was named Sir Matt Busby Player of the Year twice. He scored 150 goals in 219 games for United and became their all-time European record goalscorer. However, his later years at United were less successful. Real Madrid signed van Nistelrooy in 2006. He won La Liga twice and the Supercopa de España but was injured at the end of his time there. He then played for Hamburger SV from 2010 to 2011, before joining Málaga in 2011. He retired from football on May 14, 2012. Internationally, van Nistelrooy played for the Netherlands 70 times and scored 35 goals. He was part of the Netherlands teams for Euro 2004, the 2006 World Cup, and Euro 2008.

Fana Hlongwane is a South African politician and businessman. He advised Defence Minister Joe Modise from 1995 to 1998. His companies, including Ngwane Defence, Truvelo, and Les Amis, are suspected of receiving money from British Aerospace, which is believed to be bribes given to the African National Congress (ANC). Swedish authorities claim that Hlongwane received 24 million rand in 2003. In 2007, a former British Aerospace manager named Bernard Collier paid 7 million rand to Hlongwane through a company called Ivema, which Hlongwane partly owned.

Gopinath Pandurang Munde, born on December 12, 1949, and died on June 3, 2014, was an Indian politician from Maharashtra. He was a popular leader known as 'lokneta'. Munde was a senior leader in the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and served as the Union Minister for Rural Development and Panchayati Raj in Narendra Modi's cabinet. He was the fourth-ranking minister but died in a road accident shortly after taking office. He was a Member of the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly (MLA) for five terms, from 1980 to 1985 and 1990 to 2009. Munde was the Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly from 1992 to 1995. He also served as Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra from 1995 to 1999. Munde was elected to the Lok Sabha in 2009 and 2014, and was the Deputy Leader of the BJP in the Lok Sabha. He was appointed to Modi's cabinet on May 26, 2014, but died in New Delhi a week later. According to media reports, he died in a road accident. However, in January 2019, a US hacker claimed that Munde was murdered. Munde was the shortest-serving cabinet minister in Indian history.

Mazdak, also known as Mazdak the Younger, lived around 524 or 528. He was a Zoroastrian priest and an Iranian reformer who became influential during the rule of Sasanian Emperor Kavadh I. Mazdak claimed to be a prophet of Ahura Mazda and introduced social welfare programs. He is considered a proto-socialist.

Janne Lucas, born on October 3, 1947, in Gothenburg, Sweden, is a Swedish pianist and singer. He had several chart hits in Sweden during the 1970s and 1980s. In 1980, he participated in Melodifestivalen with "Växeln Hallå" and came in second place. The following year, he sang "Rocky Mountain" and finished third. For many years, he played piano for the group "Vi I Femman." He also sang with the vocal group "Noviserna," where Anna-Lisa Cederquist was a member. His stage name "Lucas" comes from a pop band he was in during the late 1960s. The band won Sweden's pop band competition in 1967 and had a hit song called "Anti-Social Season." Before that, they had a chart hit with "Go Now." In a 2009 issue of Bildjournalen, he performed "Växeln Hallå" on Doobidoo. He also directs the Onsala and Mölnlycke Gospel Choir.
Bulgarians are a group of people who live in Bulgaria and nearby areas. They are from the South Slavic ethnic group.

My Family is a British sitcom created and written by Fred Barron. It was produced by DLT Entertainment and Rude Boy Productions. The show was broadcast on BBC One for 11 series between 2000 and 2011. From 2002, there were Christmas specials. In 2004, it was ranked 24th in the BBC's "Britain's Best Sitcom." It was the most watched sitcom in the United Kingdom in 2008. By 2011, it was one of only twelve British sitcoms with over 100 episodes. In April 2020, BBC One started airing the show, beginning with the first episode, at 8 pm on Friday nights. All 11 series are now available on BBC iPlayer. The show is set in Chiswick, West London. Robert Lindsay plays Ben Harper, and Zoe Wanamaker is his wife Susan. Kris Marshall, Daniela Denby-Ashe, and Gabriel Thomson play their children Nick, Janey, and Michael. Janey left the show in 2002 but returned from 2004 to the end. Nick left in 2005 but made occasional guest appearances and was often mentioned by other characters. Siobhan Hayes played the character Abi from 2002 to 2008. Roger, played by Keiron Self, and Alfie, played by Rhodri Meilir, were introduced in 2003 and 2005, respectively.

James Barnes Wyngaarden was born on October 19, 1924, and died on June 14, 2019. He was an American doctor, researcher, and worked as an academic leader. Wyngaarden helped write a very important book about medicine called "Cecil Textbook of Medicine." He also led a group called the National Institutes of Health from 1982 to 1989. Wyngaarden had four daughters and one son. He was part of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.

Pashupati Sharma is a Nepalese folk singer born on October 31, 1982, in Putalibazar Municipality, Ward 3, Syangja District, Nepal. In 2003, he moved to Kathmandu for further studies. He started singing in a duet folk singing club called Saptakoshi Dohori Sanjh and released his first official song in the same year. Sharma has sung over 1000 songs during his career. His songs are about patriotism, love, and satire. One of his latest satire songs, "Lutna Sake Lut," was removed from YouTube. Sharma is considered a living legend in Nepal's folk music industry. In 2018, he released a song called "Chhata Harayo" with Devi Gharti Magar.

Shahid Afridi, born on March 1, 1975, is a famous Pakistani cricketer and the former captain of Pakistan's national team. Known as Shahid Afridi or Boom Boom in the media, he is known for being a skilled all-rounder. He is respected for his consistent bowling that relies on changing the pace of the ball rather than spin. His aggressive batting style also made him famous. Afridi holds the world record for the fastest one-day international (ODI) century, made in just 37 deliveries, and is the player who hit the most sixes in ODI history. He considers himself a better bowler than a batsman and has taken over 350 wickets in ODIs and 48 in Tests. He ranks second on the list of most T20 international (T20I) wickets, with 98 from 99 matches. Afridi retired from international cricket on February 19, 2017, but made a brief return in 2018 when he was chosen to captain the World XI against the West Indies in a charity match to help those affected by hurricanes. He officially retired on May 31, 2018, at Lord's Cricket Stadium. On June 13, 2020, Afridi shared on Twitter that he had tested positive for COVID-19 after feeling severe body pain since June 11, 2020. Before contracting the virus, he had been helping people in remote areas of Balochistan during the country's lockdown.
Saúl Asael Martínez Álvarez, born on January 29, 1976, is a Honduran football player who plays as a forward. He is on the Miami United team, which is in the fourth tier of the USA.

Satanic Majesties' Request is an album by the English rock band The Rolling Stones. It was released in December 1967 in the UK by Decca Records and in the US by London Records. This was their sixth British and eighth American studio album, and the first to be released the same way in both countries. The album's title is a joke on the phrase "Her Britannic Majesty requests and requires..." that appears in British passports. The band tried new sounds, using things like the mellotron, unusual sounds, strings, and African rhythms. After their manager/producer Andrew Loog Oldham left, the band produced the album themselves. Recording took a long time and was difficult. Members often used drugs, went to court, and even spent time in jail. The album cover shows a special image by photographer Michael Cooper. Critics and band members had mixed feelings about the album. Some said it sounded like the Beatles' album Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band from 1967. However, over time, people have come to like it more. After the album came out, The Rolling Stones changed their style. They returned to simpler, blues-based music.

Hadrian, born on January 24, 76, and died on July 10, 138, was the Roman emperor from 117 to 138. He came from a family with roots in Spain. His family originally came from a town called Atri in Italy. His father was a senator. Trajan, a famous emperor, was his first cousin. Hadrian married Trajan’s grand-niece, Vibia Sabina, before Trajan became emperor. Trajan’s wife, Pompeia Plotina, and his close friend, Lucius Licinius Sura, liked Hadrian. When Trajan died, his wife claimed he chose Hadrian as the new emperor. The Roman military and senate agreed, but four senators were punished. They didn't like Hadrian, and the senate never forgave him. Hadrian didn't continue Trajan's plans to expand the empire. Instead, he focused on making the borders safe and joining different peoples together. He built Hadrian's Wall in Britain. He traveled to many parts of the empire and supported building projects and institutions. He rebuilt the Pantheon and the temple of Venus and Roma in Rome. He also built temples in Greece. His relationship with a young Greek man named Antinous led him to create a new religious group. He defeated a rebellion in Judaea but his rule was mostly peaceful. Hadrian had health problems in his later years. He punished two more senators for planning against him. His marriage to Vibia Sabina was unhappy and childless. He adopted Antoninus Pius and asked him to be his successor. Antoninus promised to adopt Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus. Hadrian died in Baiae in 138. Antoninus had him declared a god despite the senate's opposition. Edward Gibbon saw him as one of the “five good emperors,” but the senate thought he was distant and strict. Hadrian was seen as complex, sometimes generous and sometimes cruel, driven by curiosity and ambition.

The dram is the money used in Armenia and Artsakh, a nearby country. It used to be split into 100 luma. The word "dram" means "money" in English and is similar to words like drachma in Greek and dirham in Arabic. It is also like the English weight unit dram. The first dram coins appeared between 1199 and 1375.

Rosemary Clooney, born on May 23, 1928, and passed away on June 29, 2002, was an American singer and actress. She became famous in the early 1950s with the song "Come on-a My House." Other popular songs she performed include "Botch-a-Me," "Mambo Italiano," "Tenderly," "Half as Much," "Hey There," and "This Ole House." She also sang jazz. Her career slowed down in the 1960s because of depression and drug problems. In 1977, her career got better when Bing Crosby, her co-star from "White Christmas," asked her to perform with him at a show celebrating his 50th year in show business. She kept making music until she died in 2002.

Eupen is a city and municipality in the Belgian province of Liège, near the German border (Aachen), the Dutch border (Maastricht), and the "High Fens" nature reserve (Ardennes). The town is the capital of the Euroregion Meuse-Rhine. It was first mentioned in 1213 as part of the Duchy of Limburg. Over time, Eupen changed hands among Brabant, Burgundy, the Holy Roman Empire, and France before being given to Prussia in 1815. Prussia became part of the new German Empire in 1871. After World War I, the Treaty of Versailles transferred Eupen and nearby Malmedy from Germany to Belgium. German is the official language in Eupen, and the city is the capital of Belgium’s German-speaking community. Eupen has a small university, "Autonome Hochschule in der Deutschsprachigen Gemeinschaft," offering degrees in education and nursing. In 2010, Eupen’s football team, K.A.S. Eupen, became the first club from the German-speaking community to play in the Belgian Pro League. As of January 1, 2006, Eupen had a population of 18,248 (8,892 males and 9,356 females), with a population density of 175.90 inhabitants per km². Eupen is considered a Roman Catholic region with conservative views.
The name Ana has been used for seven tropical cyclones in the Atlantic Ocean and one in the Central Pacific.

Alan Abel, born on August 2, 1924, and died on September 14, 2018, was an American man who made hoaxes, wrote books, and made mock documentaries. He is known for creating hoaxes that attracted a lot of media attention.

Lodano is a village and former municipality in Vallemaggia, which is in Ticino, Switzerland. It was first mentioned in 1224 as "Lodino." In 1709, Lodano had 70 people. By 1801, the population grew to 85. In 1850, there were 140 people, and by 1900, the number was 141. The population then decreased to 134 in 1950 and 86 in 1970. However, it increased again, reaching 171 in 2000 and 191 in 2003. Lodano covered an area of 13.76 square kilometers. In 2004, it became part of the larger nearby municipality, Maggia.
Salavre is a town in Ain, which is in eastern France.

A volcanic belt is a large area with active volcanoes. Smaller areas of activity are called volcanic fields. These belts appear over zones with very hot temperatures, where magma is created in the Earth's crust and upper mantle. They usually form along tectonic plate boundaries, about 10 to 50 kilometers deep. For example, Mexico and western North America have many volcanoes in volcanic belts like the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt and the Northern Cordilleran Volcanic Province. Older, inactive volcanic areas can be found in flat regions, such as the Canadian Shield. It has more than 150 ancient volcanic belts, mostly between 600 and 1200 million years old. These belts contain different types of volcanic rocks and related sediments, often forming greenstone belts. Scientists believe they formed at ancient oceanic spreading centers and island arcs. One of the largest greenstone belts is the Abitibi in Ontario and Quebec, Canada. Volcanic belts are like mountain ranges, but instead of regular mountains, they consist of volcanoes.

Ellen Schwiers was a German actress born on June 11, 1930, and she died on April 26, 2019. She acted in plays, movies, and TV shows. She performed in important play premieres at the Schauspielhaus Zürich and played Buhlschaft in "Jedermann" at the Salzburg Festival. She had a long career from 1949 to 2015, appearing in over 200 films and TV shows, including popular series like "Tatort." She also directed plays, started a touring theatre company in 1982, and was in charge of a festival from 1984.

Deinocheiridae is a family of dinosaurs called ornithomimosaurians. These dinosaurs lived in Asia and North America from the Albian period until the Maastrichtian period. In 1970, Halszka Osmólska and Ewa Roniewicz named this family, including only the type genus "Deinocheirus." In 2014, a study by Yuong-Nam Lee and colleagues found that Deinocheiridae is a valid family. Lee's team used new skeletons of "Deinocheirus" and other dinosaurs like "Garudimimus" and "Beishanlong" to study. They found that these dinosaurs form a group, with "Beishanlong" being the most basic and "Deinocheirus" the most advanced. The family Garudimimidae, named in 1981 by Rinchen Barsbold, is now considered a junior synonym of Deinocheiridae. The group lived from about 115 to 69 million years ago. "Beishanlong" lived from 115 to 100 million years ago, "Garudimimus" from 98 to 83 million years ago, and "Deinocheirus" from 71 to 69 million years ago. Other dinosaurs in this group include "Paraxenisaurus," and possibly "Harpymimus" and "Hexing."

Italian (or "italiano") is a Romance language from the Indo-European language family. It is very similar to Latin, the language from which it evolved through Vulgar Latin. Italian is an official language in Italy, Switzerland, San Marino, and Vatican City. It has official minority status in Western Istria, Croatia, and Slovenia. Formerly, it was an official language in Albania, Malta, Monaco, Montenegro, and Greece. It is widely understood in Corsica and Savoie due to similarities with Tuscan, a regional language. In former Italian colonies in East Africa and North Africa, Italian still plays a significant role. Many Italian speakers also use other regional languages. Italian is one of the major languages in Europe. It is the second most widely spoken native language in the European Union with about 67 million speakers (15% of the EU population). Including non-EU countries like Switzerland, Albania, and the United Kingdom, and other continents, there are around 85 million Italian speakers. Italian is the main working language of the Holy See and is used as a common language in the Roman Catholic Church. It is also the official language of the Sovereign Military Order of Malta. Italian is known as the "language of music" because of its use in musical terms and operas. Many musical terms are taken from Italian. It is also influential in the arts and in the food and luxury goods markets. Italian became the official language after the unification of Italy. It was previously based on Tuscany's spoken language, mainly used by the upper class in Florence. The language's development was influenced by other Italian languages and, to a lesser extent, by Germanic languages from post-Roman invaders. Italian retains Latin's contrast between short and long consonants. Most Italian words end in vowels, making it easy to rhyme. It has a seven-vowel sound system, compared to Latin's ten.

Chen Meng was born on January 15, 1994. She is a Chinese table tennis player. She won the women's singles championship in the ITTF World Tour Grand Finals three times—2017, 2018, and 2019. In 2019, she won a silver medal in the women's singles at the World Championships. She also won the girls' singles championship at the World Junior Table Tennis Championships in 2011.

Jõgeva county, or Jõgevamaa, is one of Estonia's 15 counties. It is located in the eastern part of the country. Jõgeva county borders Ida-Viru county to the northeast, Lake Peipus to the east, Tartu county to the south, Viljandi county to the southwest, Järva county to the northwest, and Lääne-Viru county to the north.
Eastland is a city in Eastland County, Texas, United States. According to the 2010 census, it has 3,960 people. Eastland is also the county seat of Eastland County.

Grand Island is a town in Erie County, New York, United States. As of the 2010 census, its population was 20,374, which was 9.41% more than in 2000. The town's name comes from the French term "la grande île," as Grand Island is the largest in the Niagara River and the third largest in New York State. This name is also on the town's seal. Over time, Grand Island has been home to the Attawandaron nation and was part of French and English colonial efforts. In 1945, there was a plan to make Grand Island the site of a new World Peace Capital, near the border with Ontario, Canada. The proposal suggested placing the United Nations headquarters on Navy Island, adjacent to Grand Island, as it was believed to be a good location between two peaceful countries. An artist's drawing showed bridges connecting Grand Island to the Canadian mainland. However, the proposal was rejected, and the United Nations headquarters was built in New York City instead. Grand Island is in the northwest part of Erie County, near the Canada-U.S. border, though there's no direct river crossing to Canada. It's located northwest of Buffalo and south of Niagara Falls. Interstate 190 and New York State Route 324 run through the town.

Margaret Higgins Sanger, born Margaret Louise Higgins on September 14, 1879, and died on September 6, 1966, was an American activist for birth control, educator, writer, and nurse. She used the term "birth control" and opened the first birth control clinic in the United States. She also set up organizations that became Planned Parenthood. Sanger wrote and spoke to promote her ideas. In 1914, she was in trouble for her book "Family Limitation" and had to go to Britain until it was safe to return. Her work helped make contraception legal in the U.S. Sanger was criticized by those who oppose abortion, but she made a clear difference between birth control and abortion and was mostly against abortion. She is still seen as a hero by many who fight for women's right to control their bodies. Sanger was also criticized for supporting eugenics. In 1916, she opened the first birth control clinic in the U.S., which got her in trouble. She was arrested for giving out information about contraception. This led to a lot of debate. She believed women should decide when to have children to be more equal and healthier. She also wanted to stop dangerous illegal abortions that were common because abortion was illegal. She thought contraception was the best way to avoid unwanted pregnancies. In 1921, Sanger started the American Birth Control League, which later became Planned Parenthood. In New York, she opened a clinic with all-female doctors and another in Harlem with an advisory council that included African Americans. She also added African American staff. In 1929, she formed the National Committee on Federal Legislation for Birth Control to push for legalizing contraception. From 1952 to 1959, she was president of the International Planned Parenthood Federation. She died in 1966 and is considered a founder of the modern birth control movement.
coustaussa is a commune in Aude department, which is in the occitanie region of southern France. People who live there are called coustaussans.
Ștefan Andrei was a Romanian communist politician. He served as the foreign minister of Romania from 1978 to 1985. He was arrested after the 1989 overthrow of Nicolae Ceaușescu's government.
