Vulcanodon means "volcano tooth." It is a type of sauropod dinosaur from early Jurassic times in southern Africa. The only known species is called Vulcanodon karibaensis. It was found in 1969 in what is now Zimbabwe. For many years, it was thought to be the earliest-known sauropod. It is still considered one of the most primitive sauropods found. As a four-legged, plant-eating dinosaur, Vulcanodon had a body shape typical of sauropods, with pillar-like legs and a long neck and tail. It was smaller than most other sauropods, measuring about 15 meters long. Its skeleton includes parts of the pelvis, hind legs, forearms, and tail, but lacks the trunk and neck vertebrae and skull. At first, scientists thought it was a prosauropod because of the knife-shaped teeth found nearby. These teeth belonged to an unidentified theropod that might have eaten the carcass of a Vulcanodon. Now, it is known to be a true sauropod. When related Tazoudasaurus was discovered, both were grouped in the family Vulcanodontidae, though this is not widely accepted.

The Texas Ranger Division, often called the Texas Rangers or "Los Diablos Tejanos" (the Texan Devils), is a statewide law enforcement agency in Texas. Based in Austin, they have investigated crimes like murder and political corruption, controlled riots, protected the Texas governor, captured fugitives, and acted as a paramilitary force. Created by Stephen F. Austin in 1823, the Rangers were officially recognized in 1835 by Daniel Parker. They were briefly dissolved after the Civil War but quickly reformed. Since 1935, they've been part of the Texas Department of Public Safety, serving as the state bureau of investigation. As of 2019, there are 166 Rangers. They've been in many important Texas events, such as stopping attempts on the lives of presidents William Howard Taft and Porfirio Díaz, and famous cases like John Wesley Hardin, Sam Bass, and Bonnie and Clyde. Many books have been written about them, contributing to the Wild West mythology. The Lone Ranger, a famous fictional character, was inspired by a Texas Ranger. The Rangers are culturally important in Texas and legally protected. A museum in Waco, Texas, celebrates their significance.

Santa Rosa is a city in New Mexico, United States. It is the county seat of Guadalupe County. In 2010, it had 2,848 people living there. Santa Rosa is between Albuquerque and Tucumcari. It sits next to the Pecos River where Interstate 40, U.S. Route 54, and U.S. Route 84 cross. The city is on the western edge of the Llano Estacado, also known as the "Staked Plains," in eastern New Mexico and western Texas.
Yeager is a town in Hughes County, Oklahoma, United States. In 2010, it had 75 people. The town was established early in the 1900s. Oil and gas helped it grow, but it has always been small.
The following is a list of Guinea's presidents since the country gained independence from France in 1958. Guinea voted not to join the French community in a referendum.

Johnnie Lee Cochran Jr. (October 2, 1937 – March 29, 2005) was an American lawyer and civil rights activist. He is famous for leading the defense team that helped O.J. Simpson, who was accused of killing his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ron Goldman. Cochran used memorable phrases like "if it doesn't fit, you must acquit!" during the trial. He also defended Sean Combs in a trial for gun and bribery charges. Cochran worked with many other famous people, including Michael Jackson, Tupac Shakur, Stanley Williams, Todd Bridges, Jim Brown, Snoop Dogg, Riddick Bowe, Reginald Oliver Denny, and Geronimo Pratt. He represented Marion Jones when she faced doping charges from her high school days. Cochran was known for his courtroom skills and his work to help people hurt by the police.

Grandview Heights is a city in Franklin County, Ohio, United States. The population was 6,536 in 2010. Originally, it was part of Marble Cliff, one of Columbus's first suburbs. Marble Cliff became a community in 1890 and was called the "hamlet of Marble Cliff" when it was officially recognized in 1901. Grandview Heights became a separate village in 1906 and a city in 1931. It has its own police and fire departments and an independent school district. Its neighbor, Marble Cliff, shares these services with its residents.

Uppsala City IBK was a floorball club in Uppsala, Sweden. The men's team played in Sweden's top division during the 1990s. In the same decade, the women's team took Storvreta IBK's place in the Swedish league system. The women's team played well in the Swedish championship playoffs during the 1996-1997 season. They won the first semifinal game against Högdalens IBF but lost the series overall.

Bernard Le Bovier de Fontenelle, also known as Bernard Le Bouyer de Fontenelle, was a French writer who lived from February 11, 1657, to January 9, 1757. He was an important member of three academies of the Institut de France. He is known for making science easier to understand during the Enlightenment.
Hohentannen is a municipality in Weinfelden district, which is in the canton of Thurgau in Switzerland.
Neuenhof is a municipality in the district of Baden, in the canton of Aargau, Switzerland. It is situated in the Limmat Valley (in German, "Limmattal").

Hurricane Hortense was the first hurricane to hit Guadeloupe and Puerto Rico since 1989. It was the second strongest hurricane in the 1996 Atlantic hurricane season. It was the eighth tropical cyclone, named storm, and hurricane of that season. Hortense started as a tropical wave in the Atlantic Ocean on September 3. It became a tropical storm on September 7 after the wind conditions improved. On September 8, it hit Guadeloupe and entered the Caribbean Sea. It became a hurricane on September 9 and hit Puerto Rico, then the Dominican Republic. In the Atlantic, Hortense got much stronger, reaching a peak speed of 140 mph on September 13. It weakened as it moved north-northeast and hit Nova Scotia as a Category 1 hurricane on September 15. It turned into an extratropical storm and joined another system the next day. In the Lesser Antilles, Hortense caused heavy rain and strong winds. On Guadeloupe, most banana plants were destroyed. In Puerto Rico, 11,463 houses were damaged and about 1.4 million people lost power. The damage cost about $153.4 million. There were 19 deaths, mostly from flash floods. In the Dominican Republic, strong winds damaged buildings and power lines, and flooding closed roads. In the Bahamas, Turks and Caicos, and Bermuda, there were strong winds. In Nova Scotia, heavy rain and hurricane-force winds caused many power outages and road damage. In New Brunswick, Newfoundland, and Prince Edward Island, the damage was less severe. Total damage in Atlantic Canada was about $3.64 million.

Mark Alan Webber, born on August 27, 1976, is an Australian former racing driver. He won the FIA World Endurance Championship in 2015 while driving for Porsche. Webber also won nine Formula One races and came third in the championship. He started his racing career in Australia with Formula Ford and Holden, then moved to the UK in 1995. Webber worked with Paul Stoddart, who later bought the Minardi team. Webber beat Fernando Alonso in the 2000 International Formula 3000 season. Webber made his Formula One debut in 2000 for Minardi, scoring the team's first points in three years. Jaguar took him on as their lead driver after his first season. In 2009, he won the German Grand Prix and had several second and third-place finishes. By 2010, he was third in the championship. In 2011, he won the Brazilian Grand Prix and finished third again. Webber then partnered with Sebastian Vettel at Red Bull but performed better in the first half of 2011 and won in Monaco and Britain. He finished the 2011 season in sixth place. Webber also served as a long-term director of the Grand Prix Drivers' Association. In 2013, he announced he would retire from Formula One at the end of the season. He then started racing for Porsche in 2014, competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship. Webber won the World Endurance Championship in 2015 with the #17 car. After retiring from driving, he worked as a pundit for BBC and Channel 4's Formula One coverage. In October 2016, he announced he would retire from driving at the end of the 2016 season to focus on media roles with Channel 4.

Hämeenkoski is a former municipality in Finland. It merged with the municipality of Hollola on January 1, 2016. Hämeenkoski is in the province of Southern Finland and part of the Päijänne Tavastia region. The municipality covered an area, of which was water. It had a population of. The population density was. Hämeenkoski spoke only Finnish. Lake Pääjärvi is near the border between Hämeenkoski and Hämeenlinna (formerly Lammi).

The M65 is a motorway in Lancashire, England. It starts just south of Preston and passes through the junctions of the M6 and M61 motorways. It goes east, past Darwen, Blackburn, Accrington, Burnley, Brierfield, and Nelson. It ends in Colne.

Al Jazeera is a Qatari state-owned broadcaster based in Doha, Qatar. It originally started as an Arabic news and current affairs TV channel and has since grown into a network with various outlets, including the internet and channels in multiple languages. Al Jazeera has about 80 offices around the world. It was controversial in some Arab Gulf states for allowing different views, like on call-in shows. The station became well-known during the Afghanistan war, as it was the only channel covering the war live. Al Jazeera is a news channel funded by the Qatari government but keeps its editorial independence. Some say it supports the Qatari government's views, but it also produces content critical of Qatar. People think the network mainly supports Islamist ideas and has a bias against Shia groups in its reporting. However, Al Jazeera says it presents all sides of a debate equally. It has shown videos made by Osama bin Laden. In 2017, several countries, including Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, asked Qatar to close Al Jazeera as part of their demands during a crisis. Other media networks supported Al Jazeera. According to The Atlantic magazine, Al Jazeera is much more moderate and Westernized than some other Islamist groups.

Jimmy Wayne Jamison was an American musician, singer, and songwriter. He lived from August 23, 1951, to September 1, 2014. Jamison was the lead singer of the rock band Survivor. He was with the band from 1984 to 1989, for a short time in 1992, from 2000 to 2006, and from 2011 until his death. Jamison also helped write and performed the theme song "I'm Always Here" for the TV show Baywatch in the 1990s.

Ace of Base is a Swedish pop group. Initially, it included siblings Jonas, Linn, and Jenny Berggren, with Ulf Ekberg joining in 1990. They became very successful after their first album, "Happy Nation," came out in 1992. This album, later called "The Sign," sold a lot in the United States and was the top-selling album of 1994. It produced three big hits: "All That She Wants," "The Sign," and "Don't Turn Around." They kept making popular songs in the 1990s, like "Beautiful Life," "Lucky Love," "Cruel Summer," and "Life Is a Flower." By 2002, they sold about 30 million albums from their first four albums, making them the third most successful Swedish group after ABBA and Roxette. Although they stopped working much after 2012, they haven't officially ended. Recently, they've shared some demo tracks, first on Facebook and then on the album "Hidden Gems" in 2015. In 2020, they released a boxset with an expanded version of "Hidden Gems." Jenny Berggren performs their songs in her solo shows around the world.
waltenschwil is a municipality in Muri district, in the canton of Aargau, Switzerland.

The Democratic National Committee (DNC) is the main group that runs the Democratic Party in the United States. It organizes the Democratic National Convention every four years. This convention picks a candidate for president and decides on the party's platform. The DNC helps party candidates but doesn't control elected officials. The chair of the DNC is chosen by the committee members. They also raise money to support their work. The DNC was created during the 1848 Democratic National Convention. Its main partner is the Republican National Committee.

The title is a German translation of an old Norse phrase. In Norse mythology, this phrase refers to a predicted war among various beings and gods. This war leads to the world burning, being immersed in water, and then being renewed. However, Wagner's version in his "Ring" differs significantly from the old Norse stories.

Jumanji is a 1995 American fantasy comedy adventure movie. Joe Johnston directed it. It's based on a 1981 children's book by Chris Van Allsburg. This is the first movie in the Jumanji series. The movie was written by Van Allsburg, Greg Taylor, Jonathan Hensleigh, and Jim Strain. Robin Williams, Kirsten Dunst, David Alan Grier, Bonnie Hunt, Bradley Pierce, Jonathan Hyde, and Bebe Neuwirth acted in it. The story is about a magic board game. It sends dangerous jungle things to players when they move the game pieces. In 1969, a boy named Alan Parrish got stuck inside the game with his friend Sarah Whittle. Twenty-six years later, siblings Judy and Peter Shepherd find the game, start playing, and accidentally let the adult Alan out. They find Sarah and decide to finish the game to stop the trouble and go back to normal. The movie came out on December 15, 1995. It got mixed reviews but was very successful. It made $263 million worldwide, which was one of the top 10 movies of 1995. The movie led to an animated TV show from 1996 to 1999 and later films in the series. Columbia Pictures took over the job of distributing the movies after that.
A reward is: Something given for good work or behavior.

extratropical cyclones, sometimes called mid-latitude cyclones or wave cyclones, are low-pressure areas that help shape the weather in much of the world. They can bring anything from light rain to strong storms, including thunderstorms, blizzards, or heavy winds. These large weather systems, called synoptic low-pressure systems, form in the middle latitudes. Unlike tropical cyclones, they create quick temperature changes around the cyclone center along lines called weather fronts.

Mathieu Pierre Flamini was born on March 7, 1984. He is a French professional footballer who also works in environmental business. Flamini plays as a midfielder. He has played for several teams: Marseille in France, Arsenal and Crystal Palace in England, and Milan in Italy. He also played for Getafe in Spain. At the international level, he has played for France three times. Flamini co-founded GF Biochemicals, the first company in the world to mass-produce levulinic acid.

The Althing, Iceland's parliament, is the world's oldest surviving parliament. It was established in 930 AD near a place called "thing fields" or "assembly fields," which is east of Reykjavík. Even after Iceland joined Norway in 1262, the Althing continued its meetings there until 1800, when it stopped. It was brought back in 1844 and moved to Reykjavík, where it remains today. The current building, made of Icelandic stone, was built in 1881. The Althing has 63 members and holds elections every four years. The Speaker of the Althing is Steingrímur J. Sigfússon. Iceland’s constitution divides the country into six electoral districts, which could become seven. The number of seats per district is set by law, with no district having fewer than six seats. Parties that get more than 5% of the national vote get seats based on their percentage of the total votes. This ensures that seats in the Althing reflect each party's popularity. If there's a big difference in the number of voters per member between districts, the national electoral commission adjusts the seat distribution to make it more equal.

Mneme is a small moon of Jupiter. It was found by a group of astronomers from the University of Hawaii in 2003 and was temporarily called S/2003 J 21. Mneme is about 2 kilometers wide. It orbits Jupiter at an average distance of 21.4 million kilometers, taking 641 days to complete one orbit. Its orbit is tilted about 149 degrees relative to Jupiter’s equator. It moves at an average speed of 2.43 km/s. Mneme was named in March 2005 after Mneme, one of the original Muses. She is sometimes confused with Mnemosyne, the mother of the Muses, who were either three or nine in number, depending on the writer. Mnemosyne was the child of Zeus, who is Jupiter in Roman mythology. Mneme is part of the Ananke group, a group of moons that orbit Jupiter between 19.3 and 22.7 million kilometers, with inclinations close to 150 degrees.

Sigma Octantis, also written as σ Octantis, is the current south star. It is the pole star of the southern hemisphere because it is near the southern celestial pole. This star is in the constellation Octans, which is in the southern sky. Located about 281 light-years from Earth, Sigma Octantis is a giant star with a spectral type of F0 III. It is a Delta Scuti variable star, with its brightness changing by about 0.03 magnitudes every 2.33 hours.

Matthew Nagy (born April 24, 1978) is an American football coach. He used to play as a quarterback in college and professionally. He played college football for the University of Delaware from 1997 to 2000, setting some school records. He couldn't get an NFL contract, so he played in the Arena Football League for six seasons. He played for several teams including the New York Dragons, Carolina Cobras, Georgia Force, and Columbus Destroyers. After stopping his playing career, Nagy became an assistant coach with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2009. He worked there for five years in different offensive roles under head coach Andy Reid. When Andy Reid moved to the Kansas City Chiefs in 2013, Nagy followed and became the quarterbacks coach. He was promoted to offensive coordinator in 2016. In 2018, Nagy became the head coach of the Chicago Bears. In his first year, he led the team to their first NFC North championship and playoff appearance since 2010.

Potosí is a department in southwestern Bolivia. It covers 118,218 square kilometers and has 823,517 people (2012 census). The capital is the city of Potosí. It is mostly a barren, mountainous area. To the west, there is a large plateau where the world's largest salt flat, Salar de Uyuni, is located. Cerro Potosí was one of the richest provinces in the Spanish Empire. It provided a large amount of silver that was sent to Europe. Potosí is also known for its silver, zinc, and lead mines. These mines were developed by the U.S. company Apex Silver Mines Limited from Colorado. In November 2008, the mines were sold to the Japanese Sumitomo Corporation.

Pind Dadan Khan tehsil (Urdu/Punjabi: پنڈ دادن خان) is a part of Jhelum district in Punjab, Pakistan. Its headquarters is the town of Pind Dadan Khan, located near the River Jhelum, about 22 kilometers from the M2 motorway. Pind Dadan Khan is famous for the Khewra Salt Mines, the largest salt mines in Asia, which have been in use for over 2,000 years and include an underground mosque. The area has a long history, dating back to the time of Alexander the Great's invasion (see Punjab, Pakistan). A small town called Jalalpur Sharif, known for burying Alexander the Great's horse, Bucephalus, is also located here. The town is named after Dadan Khan, a devoted Sufi saint from the Awan tribe.

Bellaire is a village in Belmont County, Ohio, United States. It is part of the Wheeling, West Virginia metropolitan area. Wheeling is located across the Ohio River to the east. In 2010, Bellaire had 4,278 people. Its population was largest in 1920. Bellaire is by the Ohio River. The Bellaire Toll Bridge, which is now closed, was used in the 1991 movie "The Silence of the Lambs." The curved railroad bridge over the Ohio River and the B&O railroad bridge were featured in the 2010 film "Unstoppable." Both bridges are historic structures. A logo with the historic stone bridge is on official village papers and police uniforms. It was designed by former resident Michael A. Massa, who also created the Belmont County seal, during the time when Mayor Fitch was in office.
Lionel Guérin is a French boss and politician.

An antimicrobial stops or kills tiny organisms called microorganisms. There are different kinds of antimicrobial medicines depending on the type of microbe they target. For example, antibiotics fight bacteria, and antifungals fight fungi. Antimicrobial medicines can also be divided into two groups: ones that kill microbes are called microbicidal, and ones that just stop them from growing are called biostatic. Using antimicrobial medicines to treat infections is called antimicrobial chemotherapy. Using them to prevent infections is called antimicrobial prophylaxis. Antimicrobial agents are divided into three main types: disinfectants, which kill many microbes on surfaces; antiseptics, which help stop infections during surgeries; and antibiotics, which fight microbes inside the body. The term "antibiotic" used to mean only medicines made from microorganisms but now includes synthetic ones like sulfonamides and fluoroquinolones. It also usually refers to antibacterials. Antibacterial agents are further split into two: bactericidal agents, which kill bacteria, and bacteriostatic agents, which slow bacterial growth. New advancements have led to antimicrobial solutions that can directly kill microbes when they touch them.
In June 2011, Shibasaki was chosen to be part of the Japan team that played against Peru. However, he did not get to play in the match.

The 1944 Great Atlantic Hurricane was a strong tropical storm that hit the eastern U.S. coast in September. It had the biggest impact in New England but also affected the Outer Banks, mid-Atlantic states, and Canadian Maritimes. It was as fierce as the 1938 Long Island Express, one of the worst storms in New England history. The storm began as a disturbance on September 4, east of the Lesser Antilles, and became a tropical cyclone on September 9, northeast of the Virgin Islands. It moved northwest and intensified, reaching its strongest on September 13 north of the Bahamas. On September 14, it passed the Outer Banks and hit Long Island and Rhode Island on September 15 as a weaker hurricane. After landfall, the storm changed into an extratropical cyclone and continued northeast. It merged with another system off Greenland on September 16.

Mostafa Pour-Mohammadi was born on March 9, 1960, in Qom. He is an Iranian politician and prosecutor. Pour-Mohammadi held important government positions. He was the Minister of Interior from 2005 to 2008 and the Minister of Justice from 2013 to 2017. He is said to be involved in the 1988 massacre of Iranian prisoners.

The office of minister president, or prime minister, of Prussia was created in 1848. King Frederick William IV made this office during the 1848–49 revolution. It lasted until 1947, when the Allied Control Council abolished Prussia.
Sarat Pujari was an Indian actor, director, and producer in Odia films from 1934 to 2014. He was born on August 8, 1934, and passed away on May 12, 2014. He was originally from Jhaduapada, Sambalpur.

John Dixon was born on February 20, 1929, and passed away on May 7, 2015. He was an Australian comic book artist and writer. Dixon is famous for creating the comic strip "Air Hawk and the Flying Doctors," which appeared from 1959 to 1986.

Wind power uses wind to make electricity through turbines that spin generators. It is a clean, renewable energy with less environmental impact than burning fossil fuels. Wind farms have many turbines connected to power grids. Onshore wind farms are cheaper than coal or gas plants but need more land and can change rural areas. Offshore wind farms are stronger and have less view impact but are more expensive to build and maintain. Small onshore farms can provide some grid power or energy to remote places. Wind power is unreliable and varies, so it needs other power sources or storage to keep the lights on. In 2018, wind supplied 4.8% of global electricity, with 591 GW installed capacity. It provides 15% of Europe's electricity, and at least 83 countries use it for power.

Jon Llewellyn Kyl, born on April 25, 1942, is an American politician who was a U.S. Senator for Arizona. He served from 1995 to 2013 and again in 2018. Kyl is from the Republican party. He held both of Arizona's Senate seats at different times, serving with John McCain during his first term. Kyl was the Senate minority whip from 2007 to 2013. His parents were John Henry Kyl and Arlene Kyl. Kyl was born and raised in Nebraska and lived in Iowa for some time. He studied at the University of Arizona, where he got his bachelor's and law degrees. Before becoming a senator, Kyl worked in Phoenix, Arizona, as a lawyer and lobbyist. He was first elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 1987 and served there until 1995. Kyl won a Senate seat in 1994 and was re-elected until he retired in January 2013. In 2006, he was named one of America's ten best senators by Time magazine. Kyl was considered the fourth-most conservative U.S. senator in 2007. He led Republican policy committees and was Senate minority whip from 2007 to 2013. In 2011, Kyl decided not to run for re-election in 2012 and planned to retire after his third term. He didn't want to run for other positions except possibly vice president. After leaving the Senate in 2013, Kyl worked as a lawyer and helped nominate Brett Kavanaugh to the Supreme Court. In 2018, Kyl was chosen by Governor Doug Ducey to fill John McCain's vacant Senate seat. Kyl said he wouldn't run for the remaining term in 2020. Kyl was the first person to return to the Senate by appointment since 1975. He left the Senate in December 2018, and Martha McSally replaced him.
Andelsheim is a town in Haut-Rhin, which is in Grand Est, in northeastern France.

Quintana Roo, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Quintana Roo, is one of Mexico's 32 states. It is split into 11 municipalities and its capital is Chetumal. Located on the eastern part of the Yucatán Peninsula, it borders Campeche to the west and Yucatán to the northwest. It also shares a border with Belize to the south. Quintana Roo is Mexico's easternmost state, with coastlines along the Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of Mexico. It used to share a small border with Guatemala but that changed in 2013. Quintana Roo includes cities like Cancún, islands such as Cozumel and Isla Mujeres, and towns like Bacalar, Playa del Carmen, and Akumal. It also has ancient Mayan ruins like Chacchoben, Cobá, Kohunlich, Muyil, and Tulum. The Sian Ka'an Biosphere Reserve is also in this state. The population of Quintana Roo is growing fast because of new hotels and job needs. Many people move there from Yucatán, Campeche, Tabasco, and Veracruz. The state often gets hit by strong hurricanes due to its location. The worst recent hurricane was Dean in 2007, which had very strong winds.

Geoffrey L. Duncan, born on April 1, 1975, is an American businessman and politician. He is the 12th Lieutenant Governor of Georgia. Before that, he was a member of the Georgia House of Representatives. After playing college baseball for the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets, Duncan played professional baseball for six years. He stopped playing due to a shoulder injury. After that, he went into business and was elected to the Georgia House in 2012.

recruitment is about finding and choosing people for jobs in a company. This involves looking for candidates, getting them interested, checking if they are suitable, and interviewing them. It can also include picking people for unpaid roles. Managers, HR staff, and recruitment specialists can do this. Sometimes, public agencies or professional recruitment companies help with parts of the process. Online tools, including AI, are used to support all parts of recruitment.

The Belize Barrier Reef is a series of coral reefs along Belize's coast. It extends from northern to southern Belize, just offshore. It is part of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef System, which runs from Cancún in Mexico to Honduras, making it the second largest coral reef system in the world after Australia's Great Barrier Reef. It's Belize's top tourist spot, popular for scuba diving and snorkeling, and attracts almost half of its 260,000 visitors. The reef is also important for fishing. Charles Darwin called it "the most remarkable reef in the West Indies" in 1842. Besides the barrier reef, Belize has three Caribbean atolls: Turneffe Atoll, Glover's Reef, and Lighthouse Reef. Lighthouse Reef is the easternmost area for diving in Belize and features the Great Blue Hole, famous from Jacques Cousteau's visit in 1970. Turneffe Atoll is located east of Belize City, the capital. These different reefs offer diverse scuba diving opportunities, including walls, pinnacles, and reef flats across a large area of the sea.
James Faulkner could be: A person with that name

Wesley Allison Clark was born on April 10, 1927, and died on February 22, 2016. He was an American physicist known for designing the first modern personal computer. Clark was also involved in creating the LINC computer with Charles Molnar in 1962, which is considered one of the first minicomputers and an inspiration for personal computers. Clark was born in New Haven, Connecticut, and grew up in Kinderhook, New York, and northern California. His parents moved to California, and he studied physics at the University of California, Berkeley, graduating in 1947. He started his career as a physicist at Hanford Site. In 1981, Clark received the Eckert–Mauchly Award for his work on computer architecture. In 1984, he was given an honorary degree by Washington University. Clark was elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 1999 and was a recipient of the IEEE Computer Society Computer Pioneer Award for his pioneering work on the first personal computer.

In physics, the center of mass is the unique point where the mass of an object is evenly distributed. This point is important because if a force is applied there, the object will move straight without spinning. Calculations in mechanics often become easier when based on this point. The center of mass is like a single point where you can imagine all the mass of an object is concentrated, making it easier to understand its motion. For a solid object with uniform density, the center of mass is at its geometric center. However, it can also be outside the object, like in a horseshoe. For a group of separate objects, the center of mass is the point where their masses balance each other. This point is crucial in studying the movement and rotation of objects. In space, planets are treated as point masses at their centers of mass to simplify calculations. The center of mass frame is a reference point where the center of mass is not moving.

Eight Cousins, or The Aunt-Hill was written in 1875 by American author Louisa May Alcott. The book tells the story of Rose Campbell. Rose is a lonely and sick girl who has lost her parents. Now, she lives with her great aunts, who are her family's leaders in Boston. Rose has a guardian named Uncle Alec, who comes back from a trip. Uncle Alec has new ideas about raising children. Under his care, Rose feels happier and healthier. She also spends time with her seven boy cousins and many aunts and uncles. Rose makes a friend named Phebe, who works as a young housemaid for her aunts. Phebe's cheerful spirit, even though she is poor, helps Rose appreciate her own good fortune.

Cristina Deutekom was a Dutch operatic coloratura soprano who lived from August 28, 1931, to August 7, 2014. She sang with many famous tenors of her time, including Carlo Bergonzi, José Carreras, Franco Corelli, Plácido Domingo, Nicolai Gedda, Alfredo Kraus, Luciano Pavarotti, and Richard Tucker.

The Wiener Sport-Club, often called WSC, was founded in 1883 in Vienna, Austria. It is one of the oldest sports clubs in the country. Their main location is in the Dornbach area of the city, which is the 17th district.

The Battle of Leipzig, also known as the Battle of the Nations, took place from October 16 to 19, 1813, in Leipzig, Saxony. The coalition of Austria, Prussia, Sweden, and Russia, led by Emperor Alexander I and Karl von Schwarzenberg, defeated Napoleon's French army. Napoleon's army included Polish, Italian, and German troops from the Rhine Confederation. This battle was part of the German campaign in 1813 and involved 500,000 soldiers, 2,200 cannons, and 127,000 casualties, making it the largest battle in Europe before World War I. After this defeat, Napoleon had to leave for France. The Sixth Coalition continued its efforts, dismantled the Rhine Confederation, and invaded France the following year. Napoleon abdicated and was exiled to Elba in May 1814.

Helene & Gänget was a dance band in Kristianstad, Sweden. It was formed in 1990 by members of the Färmarna dance band. The band became popular in 1995 with their album "Segla Din Båt I Hamn." In 2002, the band stopped performing, and their singer, Helene Persson, started working as a host for the Kristianstad program. Some famous songs by the band include "Segla Din Båt I Hamn," "En Korg Med Blommor," and "Nånstans Så Finns Du."

Sheringham is a town in Norfolk, England. It has 7,367 people. In 1953, the town council got a motto: "The sea enriches and the pine adorns." This means the sea makes the town rich, and pine trees make it beautiful.
A château is a large house owned by a noble or important person. It was originally a manor house in France and still mostly is. The plural is châteaux.

Phoenix is a minor constellation in the southern sky. It was first shown by Johann Bayer in 1603 in his atlas "Uranometria." Nicolas Louis de Lacaille mapped brighter stars there in 1756. Phoenix, along with Grus, Pavo, and Tucana, is part of the group known as the Southern Birds. The brightest star, Alpha Phoenix, is called Ankaa. It is an orange giant with a magnitude of 2.4. Beta Phoenix is actually two yellow giant stars that together have a magnitude of 3.3. Nu Phoenix has a dust disk, and the constellation has ten star systems with known planets. It also includes two recently discovered galaxy clusters, El Gordo and the Phoenix Cluster, which are among the largest objects in the visible universe. Phoenix is where we see the Phoenicids in December and the July Phoenicids meteor showers.

Calfreisen was a former municipality in the Plessur district of the canton of Graubünden in Switzerland. On January 1, 2013, Calfreisen merged with Castiel, Langwies, Lüen, Molinis, Peist, and St. Peter-Pagig to form the new municipality of Arosa.

County Armagh, named after its county town Armagh, is one of the traditional counties of Ireland. It is part of Northern Ireland, along with five other counties. Located near Lough Neagh's southern shore, County Armagh is 1,326 square kilometers in size and has about 174,792 people. It's called the "Orchard County" because it has many apple orchards. County Armagh is part of the historic province of Ulster.

Chini Modi (also known as Irshad) was a poet, novelist, short story writer, and critic who lived in Gujarat, India. He was born on September 30, 1939, and passed away on March 19, 2017. His pen name was Irshad (in Gujarati: ઈર્શાદ). Educated in languages, he taught at different schools and became well-known for his poetry and writing. He received several awards, including the Sahitya Akademi Award, the Vali Gujarati Award, and the Narsinh Mehta Award.

Bell Canada, commonly known as Bell, is a telecommunications company in Canada. Its headquarters are in Montreal, Quebec, at 1 Carrefour Alexander-Graham-Bell. Bell is an ILEC in Ontario and Quebec, and a founding member of the Stentor Alliance. It's also a CLEC for enterprise customers in the western provinces. Its subsidiary Bell Aliant serves the Atlantic provinces. Bell provides mobile service through Bell Mobility (including Virgin Mobile Canada) and TV through Bell Satellite TV and Bell Fibe TV. Bell's main competitors are Rogers Communications in Ontario, Telus and Shaw Communications in Western Canada, and Quebecor (Videotron) and Telus in Quebec. Bell serves over 13 million phone lines and is headquartered at the Bell complex in Montreal. Bell Canada is part of BCE Inc., formerly Bell Canada Enterprises. BCE owns Bell Media, which includes the CTV television network, and has significant investments in the Montreal Canadiens hockey club and Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment, owner of several Toronto sports teams. BCE was ranked 262 on the 2011 Forbes Global 2000 list.

Lager Norderney was a Nazi concentration camp on Alderney, an island in the Channel Islands. It was named after the East Frisian island of Norderney. The German Organisation Todt (OT) built four labor camps on Alderney to house workers for planned fortifications. "Lager Norderney" was located in Saye. "Lager Borkum" was at Platte Saline, "Lager Sylt" was near the old telegraph tower at La Fouleré, and "Lager Helgoland" was in the northwest corner of the island. From March 1943 to June 1944, "Lager Norderney" was run by the SS-Baubrigade. After that, it became a subcamp of the Neuengamme concentration camp, which was in Hamburg, Germany.

Portage la Prairie is a small city in Manitoba, Canada. In 2016, it had 13,304 people. It is located in the central plains region. Portage la Prairie is about west of Winnipeg, on the Trans-Canada Highway, near the borders of Saskatchewan and Ontario. The city sits by the Assiniboine River, which used to flood often. To stop this, a channel was built to divert floodwaters north to Lake Manitoba. Portage la Prairie is surrounded by the Rural Municipality of Portage la Prairie. According to Environment Canada, it has the most sunny days during warm months in Canada. The city is also the administrative headquarters for the Dakota Tipi First Nations reserve.

Khunjerab Pass is a high mountain pass in the Karakoram Mountains. It is located in Pakistan's Gilgit–Baltistan region, specifically in Hunza and Nagar districts. The pass is also near the border with China's Xinjiang province. It is in a strategic position on the northern border of Pakistan.

A photoreceptor cell is a special kind of cell in the retina that turns light into signals. These cells are very important because they help convert visible light into signals that can start biological processes. Photoreceptor proteins in the cell absorb light, which changes the cell's electrical state. There are three main types of photoreceptor cells in mammals: rods, cones, and intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs). Rods and cones are the classic types. They provide information to the visual system, helping us see. Rods are thinner and spread out differently in the retina, but they work similarly to cones in terms of light conversion. ipRGCs were discovered in the 1990s. They don't help us see directly but are thought to support circadian rhythms and pupil reflexes. Rods and cones differ in how they work. Rods are very sensitive and can be activated by a single photon. They are used in low light conditions. Cones need more light to work. In humans, there are three types of cone cells that respond to different wavelengths of light, which help us see colors. At low light levels, only rods are active, so we can't see colors. The three types of cone cells are called s-cones (short wavelengths), m-cones (medium wavelengths), and l-cones (long wavelengths, or "red"). The firing of a cell depends on the number of photons absorbed. Each type of cone cell has proteins that are more likely to absorb certain wavelengths of light. For example, l-cones are more likely to absorb longer wavelengths of light, or "red" light. Shorter wavelengths can also activate l-cones, but the light must be much brighter. The human retina has about 120 million rod cells and 6 million cone cells. The number and ratio of rods to cones vary among animals, depending on whether they are mostly active during the day (diurnal) or at night (nocturnal). Certain owls, like the tawny owl, have many rods. In the human visual system, there are about 2.4 to 3 million ganglion cells, with 1 to 2% of them being photosensitive. The ganglion cell axons form the optic nerves. Photoreceptor cells are arranged in a roughly hexagonal pattern called the retinal mosaic. In mammals, the pineal and parapineal glands are not photoreceptive, but in non-mammalian vertebrates, these glands can detect light. Birds have light-sensitive neurons in the paraventricular organ that respond to light without eye input. Invertebrates like insects and molluscs have different photoreceptors in terms of structure and biochemical processes.

Ahmed Jibril is the founder of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine – General Command (PFLP-GC). During the Syrian civil war, he supported the Assad government. PFLP-GC members helped government forces fight the Syrian opposition. However, in Yarmouk camp, clashes with rebels led to PFLP-GC members leaving. As a result, Jibril had to leave the city.

Homa Rousta, born on September 26, 1946, and passed away on September 26, 2015, was an Iranian actress who performed in films and on stage. She was married to Hamid Samandarian, a stage director. She studied theater at the School of Dramatic Arts in Bucharest and began her acting career in 1971. Her most famous role was in "From Karkheh to Rhine" in 1992, for which she was nominated for the best actress award at the Fajr Film Festival. She died of cancer in a hospital in Los Angeles, California, and her body was later taken back to Iran and buried in Behesht Zahra next to her husband's grave.

Saint-Étienne is a city in eastern central France, in the Massif Central, near Lyon. It is part of the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region. Saint-Étienne is located on a road connecting Toulouse to Lyon. The city is the capital of the Loire department. In 2017, the city had 172,565 people, and the urban area had over 520,000. In recent years, Saint-Étienne has changed a lot. It is working to become a modern city, moving from an industrial past to a design-focused future. This has led to big changes in the city, especially in its main areas.

Elliott County is in Kentucky, a state in the U.S. In 2010, it had 7,852 people. By 2018, the number went down to 7,508. Sandy Hook is the county seat. The county was made in 1869 from parts of Morgan, Lawrence, and Carter counties. It is named after John Lyle Elliott, who was a U.S. congressman and a Confederate justice. Elliott County does not allow selling alcohol anywhere in the county.
Saint-Jouin is a town in the Calvados department, which is in Normandy, a region in northwestern France.

Active transport is the movement of molecules across a cell membrane from a less crowded area to a more crowded area—against the concentration. This process needs energy from the cell. There are two kinds of active transport: one uses adenosine triphosphate (ATP), and the other uses an electrochemical gradient. An example of active transport in humans is how glucose is taken up in the intestines.
The Akrisios is a tragedy written by Sophocles, an Athenian playwright from the 5th century BCE. Only fragments of this play survive.

Bob Beckwith was born on September 21, 1933. He used to be a member of the New York City Fire Department. After the September 11, 2001 attacks, he stood next to President George W. Bush at the World Trade Center ruins. Pictures of Beckwith and the president were on the front page of the "New York Daily News" and on the cover of "Time" magazine. This made Beckwith famous. He has met President Bush several times since then. He also gave many public speeches and helped raise money for charities.

The ECW World Heavyweight Championship was a professional wrestling title used in Extreme Championship Wrestling (ECW) and later in WWE. It was the first world title for ECW, coming from the NWA World Heavyweight Championship. The title was created in 1994 but was first introduced in 1992 by ECW's predecessor, Eastern Championship Wrestling. Jimmy Snuka was the first champion. In 2001, ECW ended, and the title was inactive. In 2003, WWE bought ECW. In 2006, WWE brought back the title for their ECW brand. It was the third active world title in the promotion, alongside the WWE and World Heavyweight Championships from the Raw and Smackdown brands. In 2008, the title became the sole world title for Raw for a short time. When WWE stopped the ECW brand in 2010, the title was retired, with Ezekiel Jackson holding it last.
Carlos Oscar Reichenbach Filho was a filmmaker from Brazil. He was born on June 14, 1945, and passed away on June 14, 2012.
Örkelljunga is a small town in Sweden. It is the capital of Örkelljunga municipality in Skåne county. In 2020, it had about 10,300 people living there.

Cory Scott Gardner, born on August 22, 1974, is an American lawyer and politician. He has been a U.S. senator for Colorado since 2015. Gardner is a Republican. From 2011 to 2015, he served as the U.S. representative for Colorado's 4th congressional district. From 2005 to 2011, he was a member of Colorado's house of representatives. In 2014, Gardner won a close election against Democratic incumbent Mark Udall for the U.S. Senate seat. Gardner was the chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee from 2017 to 2019. After the 2018 midterm elections, Gardner and Heidi Ganahl, a University of Colorado regent, were the only Republicans holding statewide elected offices in Colorado. Gardner was seen as one of the most likely senators to lose his seat in 2020.

The Fulbright program, including the Fulbright-Hays program, is one of several U.S. cultural exchange programs. It aims to improve understanding and friendships between people in the U.S. and other countries by exchanging people, knowledge, and skills. Through this program, American citizens, including students, scholars, teachers, professionals, scientists, and artists, can receive scholarships or grants to study, research, teach, or showcase their talents abroad. Similarly, citizens from other countries can participate in the program in the United States. The Fulbright program was created in 1946 by U.S. Senator J. William Fulbright and is known as one of the most famous and respected scholarships globally. It gives around 8,000 grants each year, including about 1,600 for U.S. students, 1,200 for U.S. scholars, 4,000 for foreign students, 900 for foreign visiting scholars, and several hundred for teachers and professionals. The program is managed by organizations like the Institute of International Education and operates in over 160 countries. It is funded by the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs, which gets money from the U.S. Congress. Other partners, such as governments, foundations, corporations, and host institutions, also support the program. In 49 countries, a bi-national Fulbright commission oversees the program, while in other countries, the U.S. embassy handles it. Over 370,000 people have taken part in the program since it started. Sixty Fulbright alumni have won Nobel Prizes, and 86 have won Pulitzer Prizes.

The 1st United States Congress, made up of the Senate and the House of Representatives, met from March 4, 1789, to March 4, 1791. This was during George Washington's first two years as president. They first met at Federal Hall in New York City and later moved to Congress Hall in Philadelphia. With the first meeting of the Congress, the U.S. government began operating under the new Constitution, written in 1787. The number of seats in the House was decided by the Constitution. Both the Senate and the House mostly supported the president. This Congress sent twelve proposed changes to the Constitution to the states. Ten of these changes, known as the Bill of Rights, were ratified on December 15, 1791.

Colonel Reginald Edward Harry Dyer, CB, was a military officer who served in the Bengal Army and later in the Indian Army. He started his career in the British Army before moving to the presidency armies of India. As a temporary brigadier-general, he was in charge when the Jallianwala Bagh massacre happened in Amritsar, Punjab. He is known as "the butcher of Amritsar" because he ordered soldiers to shoot at a peaceful crowd. The official report said at least 379 people died, and over a thousand were injured. Some people who gave evidence to the inquiry said even more people died. Dyer was taken off duty and widely criticized in Britain and India. However, some people in the British Raj saw him as a hero. Some historians think this event was a key moment leading to the end of British rule in India.

The Millennium Dome, also called simply the Dome, was a big round building used for a special exhibition in the year 2000. The exhibition celebrated the start of the new millennium. It's one of the nine largest buildings in the world by volume. Located in Greenwich, London, the Dome opened on January 1, 2000, and closed on December 31, 2000. It was a political project, and it didn't attract as many visitors as expected—only about 6 million people came, not the 12 million predicted. The press considered it a failure. After the exhibition, all the original parts were sold or taken apart. In 2005, it cost £28.7 million to sell the Dome and nearby land (which increased to 170 acres from the original 48 acres). The 48 acres inside the Dome were worth about £48 million, but it was better to keep the Dome standing. The Dome is now part of the O2 venue. The Prime Meridian passes near its western side, and the nearest London Underground station is North Greenwich on the Jubilee Line.
Gene Autry is a town in Carter County, Oklahoma, United States. In 2010, the population was 158, an increase from 99 in 2000. It is part of the Ardmore, Oklahoma, micropolitan statistical area.

Sabayon Linux is an Italian Linux distribution based on Gentoo. It was formerly known as RR4 Linux and RR64 Linux. Sabayon is created by Fabio Erculiani and the Sabayon development team. This distribution follows the "out of the box" philosophy, providing a wide range of ready-to-use applications and a self-configured operating system. Sabayon uses a rolling release cycle and has its own software repository and package management system called Entropy. It is available for both x86 and AMD64 architectures, with ARMv7 support for the BeagleBone in development. The name Sabayon comes from an Italian dessert called zabaione, made from eggs. Its logo features an impression of a chicken foot.
Patrick Burke Mayhew, Baron Mayhew of Twysden, was born on September 11, 1929, and died on June 25, 2016. He was a British lawyer and politician.

Alumpeedika is a small village in Oachira, Kollam district, in Kerala, India. It is part of Clappana Panchayath and is in the South Kerala division. Alumpeedika is 31 km north of Kollam, 1 km from Oachira, and 101 km from the state capital, Thiruvananthapuram. Nearby towns include Kayamkulam, Oachira, and Karunagappalli. It is close to the border of Kollam and Alappuzha districts and is near the Arabian Sea.

Better known by his ring name, he was a Japanese professional wrestler who mostly worked for All Japan Pro Wrestling (AJPW). He is famous for being the first triple crown heavyweight champion. He won the PWF Heavyweight Championship, the NWA United National Championship, and the NWA International Heavyweight Championship. He unified all three titles. He is also known for being part of the first-ever world tag team champions with Yoshiaki Yatsu. Together, they won the NWA International Tag Team Championship and the PWF Tag Team Championship, and unified the two titles.

Clean and Sober is a 1988 American drama film. Glenn Gordon Caron directed it. Michael Keaton plays a real estate agent who has a problem with using substances. This was Keaton's second dramatic role after "Touch and Go." The supporting actors include Kathy Baker, M. Emmet Walsh, Morgan Freeman, Luca Bercovici, and Tate Donovan. Ron Howard, who directed Keaton in comedies like "Night Shift" and "Gung Ho," helped produce this film.

Conficker, known as Downadup and Kido, is a computer worm that targets Windows operating systems. It was first found in November 2008. Conficker uses weaknesses in Windows software and tries passwords from a list to spread while creating a network of infected computers. This made it hard to stop because it uses many advanced techniques. Conficker infected millions of computers in over 190 countries, more than any other computer worm since 2003's Welchia. Despite infecting so many computers, the worm did not cause much damage. This might be because the people who made it—thought to be Ukrainian criminals—were afraid of getting caught. Four men were arrested, and one was sentenced to 48 months in prison.

The Seattle Sounders FC are an American soccer team in Seattle, Washington. They play in Major League Soccer (MLS) in the Western Conference. The club started in 2007 and began playing in 2009. They are called "phoenix" because they named themselves after an old team that existed from 1974 to 1983. Adrian Hanauer is the main owner, with other owners including Paul Allen's family, Drew Carey, and 11 Seattle families. Brian Schmetzer became the head coach in 2016. They play at CenturyLink Field, which holds about 37, 722 people. A band called 'Sound Wave' also performs at their home games. The Sounders have strong rivalries with the Portland Timbers and Vancouver Whitecaps, competing for the Cascadia Cup. Their first game was on March 19, 2009, where they won against the New York Red Bulls. They have won the U.S. Open Cup four times, the MLS Cup twice, and the Supporters' Shield once. They made the playoffs every year, reached the final three times, and played in the Concacaf Champions League five times, reaching the semifinals once. They had the highest attendance in MLS for five years. The team is one of the most valuable in North America. Key players include Clint Dempsey, Fredy Montero, Osvaldo Alonso, and Nicolás Lodeiro. The Sounders also have a players' academy and lower division teams that have produced homegrown players like Jordan Morris and DeAndre Yedlin.

Darrell Clayton Hammond was born on October 8, 1955. He is an American actor, stand-up comedian, and impressionist. From 1995 to 2009, he was a regular cast member on "Saturday Night Live." He became the announcer in 2014. When he left, Hammond was the oldest cast member in the show's history at 53 years old. He made more appearances on "SNL" than any other cast member and impersonated over 107 celebrities, with Bill Clinton being his most frequent impression. On September 19, 2014, Hammond was announced as the new announcer for "Saturday Night Live," replacing Don Pardo, who had died the month before.

Töfflen is a town in the Bern-Mittelland district, part of the Bern canton in Switzerland. It is about 10 km south of Bern. There is a castle there called Töfflen Castle. This castle is a very important historical site.

Chadwell Heath is a suburban area in northeast London, England. It's near the boundary of Barking and Dagenham and Redbridge boroughs. It's about west of Romford and east of Ilford, and northeast of Charing Cross. The name "Chadwell Heath" was first used in the 17th century for a place in Dagenham, Essex. Later, it included a nearby settlement called Chadwell Street, which was in Barking (now part of Ilford). Chadwell Heath has a railway station called Chadwell Heath, which opened in 1864. The station connects the area to central London. After World War I, the area grew as a residential suburb. It became part of the Becontree estate, leading to more people living there. In 1965, the area became part of Greater London. There's a school called Chadwell Heath Academy in the area. Also, a local pub is named after Eva Hart, a survivor of a notable event.

McClure is a small community in Dickenson County, Virginia, United States. It is near the McClure River and Virginia State Route 63, southeast of Clintwood. McClure used to have a post office from 1919 until it closed on July 6, 2011. The town still has its own zip code, 24269. People say McClure was named after a pioneer who was killed by Indians.

Aho'eitu Tupou VI (born July 12, 1959) is the king of Tonga. He is the younger brother and successor of the late King George Tupou V. His brother had no children, so Aho'eitu was officially named the heir in 2006. Aho'eitu worked as Tonga's high commissioner in Australia. He lived in Canberra until King George Tupou V died on March 18, 2012. After that, Aho'eitu Tupou VI became the king of Tonga.

Harold & Kumar Go to White Castle, also known as Harold & Kumar Get the Munchies in the UK, is a 2004 American stoner comedy film. It's the first movie in the Harold & Kumar series. Jon Hurwitz and Hayden Schlossberg wrote the film, and Danny Leiner directed it. In the story, Harold Lee, played by John Cho, and Kumar Patel, played by Kal Penn, go to White Castle after smoking marijuana. They have many funny adventures. The film includes actors like Fred Willard, Paula Garcés, Anthony Anderson, and many others. Neil Patrick Harris plays himself in the movie.

Vitis, a genus of grapevines, includes 79 species. These plants mainly grow in the northern part of the world. Grapevines are important because they produce grapes for eating and making wine. Studying and growing grapevines is called viticulture. Most grapevines have flowers that can be both male and female. These flowers grow together in bunches called inflorescences. In many grapevine species, like Vitis vinifera, each flower that is successfully pollinated turns into a grape. The inflorescence then becomes a cluster of grapes. Even though grapevine flowers are usually small, the grapes are often large and colorful, attracting birds and animals to spread their seeds. In viticulture, grapevines usually only produce fruit on shoots from the previous growing season. This is why in viticulture, the previous year's growth, called "one-year-old wood," is pruned. Vines are pruned into canes that hold 8 to 15 buds or into smaller spurs that hold 2 to 3 buds.

Eric Walter Elst, born in 1936, is a Belgian astronomer at the Royal Observatory of Belgium in Uccle. He has discovered many asteroids. The Minor Planet Center lists him as one of the top 10 asteroid discoverers, with thousands of discoveries. He made these discoveries using observatories in Chile and Bulgaria between 1986 and 2009. An asteroid named 3936 Elst, which is about 6 kilometers in diameter, was named after him.

Negligence is failing to be careful when expected to. In law, "negligence" is when someone causes harm because they were careless. People should be careful and think about how their actions might hurt others or damage things. If someone gets hurt because of another person's carelessness, they can try to get money to help. This money can cover things like injuries, broken things, mental health problems, or losing money. To decide if someone was negligent, the law looks at five main ideas: if there was a duty, if it was broken, if it caused the harm, if it was the main cause, and what damages to award.

Voeren is a Flemish municipality in the Dutch-speaking part of Belgium. It has services for French-speaking people. Voeren is in the province of Limburg. It borders the Netherlands to the north and the Walloon province of Liège to the south. Geographically, Voeren is separate from the rest of Flanders, making it an exclave. Voeren's name comes from a small river called Voer, which runs through the area. The current Voeren municipality was created in 1977. On January 1, 2008, Voeren had 4,207 people living there. The area is about 13.43 square kilometers. The population density is about 313 people per square kilometer. About 25% of the people living there are from other countries, mostly Dutch.
Goodnight can mean goodnight or goodnight and goodnight. In music, it might refer to songs with those titles. In taxonomy, it could refer to classifications with those names.

Kelowna is a city on Okanagan Lake in the Okanagan Valley of British Columbia, Canada. It is the head office of the Central Okanagan Regional District. The city's name comes from an Okanagan language word meaning "grizzly bear." Kelowna is the third-largest metropolitan area in the province, after Vancouver and Victoria. It is the largest inland city and the seventh-largest city overall. It is also Canada's 22nd-largest city. Kelowna's city proper has 142,146 people. The metropolitan area has about 217,229 people. Neighboring communities include West Kelowna to the west, Lake Country and Vernon to the north, Peachland to the southwest, and Summerland and Penticton to the south.

The Mi-38 is a transport helicopter. It was designed by the MILOM Moscow Helicopter Plant and is now developed by Kazan Helicopters. It was meant to replace the Mi-8 and Mi-17. It is sold for military and civilian use. It first flew on December 22, 2003, and was certified on December 30, 2015.

Reginald Howard White (December 19, 1961 – December 26, 2004) was an American football player. He played defensive end in the NFL for 15 seasons in the 1980s and 1990s. He played college football at the University of Tennessee and was named an All-American. After playing two seasons for the Memphis Showboats in the USFL, he joined the Philadelphia Eagles, Green Bay Packers, and Carolina Panthers in the NFL. He became one of the most awarded players in NFL history. He was the NFL Defensive Player of the Year twice, played 13 times in the Pro Bowl, and was selected as an All-Pro 13 times. He holds second place in career sack leaders with 198 sacks. He was also known for his Christian ministry and was nicknamed "the minister of defense." He is a member of both the College Football Hall of Fame and the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

Six Flags Discovery Kingdom is an animal theme park in Vallejo, California. It used to be called Six Flags Marine World, Marine World, The New Marine World Theme Park, and Marine World Africa USA. The park covers 135 acres, about the size of 55 football fields. It's near Interstate 80 between San Francisco and Sacramento. Six Flags Discovery Kingdom has many roller coasters and fun rides. It has been part of the Six Flags amusement parks since 1999.

"Usual Suspects" is a 1995 movie in a style called neo-noir, directed by Bryan Singer and written by Christopher McQuarrie. It stars Stephen Baldwin, Gabriel Byrne, Benicio Del Toro, Kevin Pollak, Chazz Palminteri, Pete Postlethwaite, and Kevin Spacey. The story focuses on Roger "Verbal" Kint, a small-time trickster who survived a ship fire and massacre. Through flashbacks and narration, Kint tells the interrogator about his criminal friends and a mysterious boss named Keyser Söze. The movie was made with a budget of $6 million and was inspired by a "Spy" magazine column and a famous line from the film "Casablanca." It premiered at the 1995 Cannes Film Festival, then was shown in a few theaters. It got good reviews and was later shown in more theaters. McQuarrie won an Academy Award for best original screenplay, and Spacey won for best supporting actor. The Writers Guild of America ranked it as the 35th best screenplay of all time.

Hälleforsnäs is a village in Flen municipality, Södermanland county, Sweden. It has around 2,000 people living there as of 2020. The village is about 15 km (9 miles) from Flen, 32 km (20 miles) from Eskilstuna, 40 km (25 miles) from Katrineholm, and 150 km (93 miles) south-west of Stockholm. Hälleforsnäs used to be a busy place because of a foundry that was there for 350 years, starting in 1659. The foundry closed in the early 1990s. Now, the foundry is a cultural center and there's lots of activity there again. The foundry began as a place to make cannons for the Swedish army. In the early 20th century, it started making radiators and stoves. Between 1920 and 1980, they mostly made pipes and other things for plumbing. In the 1960s, there were over 1,000 people working there, and many others were employed nearby. In the 1980s, Electrolux bought the foundry and started making plates for cookers. They stopped production in 1990. Some of the workers took over the foundry, which is now a center for artists. Today, the area around the foundry is still busy, but not like it used to be when the foundry was the main center of the village. Hälleforsnäs has become a cultural center for the whole of Sörmland. There's a restaurant there, and during the summer, there's also a herbal shop. There's also a cheese-making company called Jurss Dairy, which makes and sells award-winning cheese on site.

Nguyễn Văn Cao, born on November 15, 1923, and died on July 10, 1995, was a Vietnamese composer. One of his famous works is "Tiến Quân Ca," which is now Vietnam's national anthem. Along with Phạm Duy and Trịnh Công Sơn, he is known as one of the three most important figures in modern Vietnamese music. He was also a poet and painter.
The vice-president of Egypt is an important government official.

isonoe is a small moon of Jupiter, known as a retrograde irregular satellite. It was discovered by a team from the University of Hawaii, led by Scott S. Sheppard, in 2000. The temporary name for this moon was Given. Isonoe is about 3.8 kilometers in diameter. It takes 751.647 days to orbit Jupiter at an average distance of 23,833,000 kilometers. Its orbit is tilted 166 degrees from the ecliptic (169 degrees from Jupiter's equator) and moves in the opposite direction to Jupiter's rotation. The moon's orbit is slightly elliptical, with an eccentricity of 0.166. Isonoe was named in October 2002 after Isonoe, a figure from Greek mythology. Isonoe was a lover of Zeus (Jupiter). Isonoe is part of the Carme group, a group of irregular, retrograde moons orbiting Jupiter at a distance between 23 and 24 GM, with an inclination of about 165 degrees.

In the Middle Ages, Ostabat-Asme was a commune in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department. It was in the region known as Lower Navarre, in southwestern France. This place was where four roads to Santiago de Compostela met. Three of these roads came together there: Paris-Tours- Poitiers-Dax, Limoges, and Genoa and Lyon via Moissac. The fourth road, the Toulouse Way, connected central Italy to the Languedoc region and Béarn, passing through Lescar-Oloron to Somport in Spain. From there, three of the connected roads went through Larceveau-Arros-Cibits, Ainhice-Mongelos, Gamarthe, Lacarre, and Iriberry to Saint-Jean-le-Vieux (43º09'57'' N, 1º11'32'' W), also known as Donazaharre, and then to Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port, before reaching the Spanish border at Roncesvalles (42º59'23'' N, 1º20'4'' W). Ostabat-Asme was in the former province of Lower Navarre and is named after the region of Ostabarret.

"Too Good at Goodbyes" is a song by English singer Sam Smith. It was written by James Napier, Tor Hermansen, Mikkel Eriksen, and Smith. The song was produced by Napes, Steve Fitzmaurice, and Stargate. It was released on September 8, 2017, through Capitol Records. This song was the first single from Smith's second album, "The Thrill of It All," released in 2017. The song reached number one in the UK and number four on the Billboard Hot 100. It also topped the charts in Australia, South Africa, and New Zealand. It was in the top 10 in Belgium, Canada, Denmark, France, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Sweden, and Switzerland. It was in the top 20 in Austria, Finland, Germany, and Spain.

Johanna Kristina "Hanna" Grönvall was born on December 10, 1879, in Västra Sallerup, Malmöhus County, and died on May 22, 1953. She was a Swedish politician and worked as a trade union worker. Grönvall was a Social Democrat. From 1900 to 1934, she worked as a maid. In 1933, she joined a committee to study the working conditions of maids. In 1934, she became the deputy chairman of the Stockholm Maids' Union. In 1936, she founded the Central Committee of Maids. Grönvall was also a member of Stockholm Municipality's city council for the Social Democrats.

Peter Brian Hegseth, born on June 6, 1980, is an American contributor for Fox News. He used to be in the Army National Guard and worked as the executive director for two political groups: Vets for Freedom and Concerned Veterans for America. The latter group supports making more parts of the Department of Veterans Affairs private and is funded by the Koch brothers. In the Trump administration, Hegseth was considered for leading the Department of Veterans Affairs. However, major veterans' groups did not agree, and David Shulkin was chosen instead in January 2017.

Troup County is in the central part of Georgia, U.S. According to the 2010 census, its population is 67,044. The county seat is Lagrange. Troup County is part of the Lagrange, GA micropolitan statistical area. It is also part of the Atlanta-Athens-Clarke County-Sandy Springs, GA combined statistical area.

A creed is like a statement of shared beliefs in a community, often religious. The earliest Christian creed, "Jesus is Lord," came from Saint Paul's writings. One widely used Christian creed is the Nicene Creed, created in 325 at the Council of Nicaea. It is based on the New Testament and some parts of the Old Testament. Most Christian groups consider agreeing with this creed, which explains the concept of the Trinity, important for being seen as correct. Another accepted creed is the Apostles' Creed. Some Christian groups do not follow these creeds. Muslims say the Shahada, which means "I believe there is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is his messenger." Whether Judaism uses creeds is debated. Some think Judaism does not use them, while others say it has a main creed called the Shema, which says "Hear O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one."

The University of Greenland is the only university in Greenland. It is located in the capital city, Nuuk. Most classes are taught in Danish, some in Greenlandic, and others by visiting lecturers in English. In 2018, it had about 205 students, mostly Greenlandic. There are around fourteen academic staff members and five technical-administrative employees. The small student body partly results from many Greenlandic students attending universities in Denmark.

Dr. Siti Musdah Mulia is an Indonesian women's rights activist. She was the first woman to become a research professor at the Indonesian Institute of Sciences, where she still works. She also teaches about Islamic political ideas at the School of Graduate Studies at Syarif Hidayatullah State Islamic University in Indonesia. Since 2007, she has been the chair of the NGO called Indonesian Conference on Religion for Peace. In 1997, she was the first woman to earn a PhD in Islamic thought from Syarif Hidayatullah Islamic State University. From 1999 to 2007, she was a senior advisor to the minister of religious affairs. During this time, she helped create a legal draft in 2004 that recommended against child marriage and allowed interfaith marriage. However, the minister had to cancel the project due to protests. From 2000 to 2005, she led the research division at the Council of Indonesian Ulama. She has written books like "Islam Criticizes Polygamy" (2003), "Reformist Muslimah" (2004), and "Islam and the Inspiration of Gender Equity" (2005). Dr. Mulia received several awards, including the 2007 International Women of Courage Award, the 2009 Yap Thiam Hien Award, and the 2009 Woman of the Year award from the Italian government.

palaeognathae, or paleognaths, comes from ancient Greek "palaió-" meaning "old" and "gnáthos" meaning "jaw." This group is one of two living bird families, the other being neognathae. Together, they form a group called neornithes. Palaeognathae includes five types of flightless birds (like ostriches and kiwis) and one type that can fly (tinamous). There are 47 species of tinamous, 5 species of kiwis, 3 species of cassowaries, 1 species of emu, 2 species of rheas, and 2 species of ostriches. Recent studies suggest that paleognaths are a single group, and the idea that flightless and flighted birds are separate is not correct. Tinamous are part of the group of flightless birds, showing that flightlessness developed independently multiple times. Three extinct groups, lithornithiformes, dinornithiformes (moas), and aepyornithiformes (elephant birds), are confirmed as part of the palaeognathae. Other extinct birds are sometimes linked to palaeognathae, but this is debated. The term "paleognath" means "old jaws" and refers to the bird's jaw structure, which is more like reptiles than other birds. Although paleognathae has some old characteristics, their DNA continues to evolve at the same rate as other bird groups under similar pressures. There are also debates about how these birds evolved.

Vermilion is a city in Ohio, in Erie and Lorain counties near Lake Erie. It is about 35 miles west of Cleveland and 17 miles east of Sandusky. In 2010, it had 10,594 people living there. The part of Vermilion in Lorain County is in the Cleveland-Elyria-Mentor area. The part in Erie County is in the Sandusky micropolitan area. Both parts are also part of a bigger area called the Cleveland-Akron-Canton combined statistical area.

In computing, a parallel port is a connection for peripherals on computers. It sends data using multiple lines at once, unlike serial ports, which send one bit at a time. This requires more space and lines in cables and connectors, making it larger than serial ports. There are different types of parallel ports, but the term is most often used for printer ports or Centronics ports on personal computers from the 1970s to the 2000s. These became a standard for many years and were finally standardized as IEEE 1284 in the late 1990s. Today, parallel ports are rare because USB devices and network printing with Ethernet and Wi-Fi are more common. Originally called the parallel printer adapter on IBM PC-compatible computers, this port was mainly for printers that used IBM's eight-bit extended ASCII character set to print text, but could also connect other devices. Now, graphical printers and many other devices communicate using different methods.

Dexter in the Dark is a 2007 book by Jeff Lindsay. It's the third book in the Dexter series, after Darkly Dreaming Dexter in 2004 and Dearly Devoted Dexter in 2005. The book came out on September 18, 2007, in the U.S. and October 3, 2007, in the U.K. It was supposed to come out earlier that year. The first two chapters of Dexter in the Dark can be seen when you watch the first season DVD of the TV show on a computer.

Jorge Zavala Baquerizo lived from May 13, 1921, to May 9, 2014. He was an Ecuadorian politician. Zavala was the vice president of Ecuador from 1968 to 1970 during the presidency of José María Velasco Ibarra. He also served as the president of the National Congress from 1987 to 1988. He belonged to the Democratic Left party. Zavala passed away in Guayaquil, Ecuador, due to natural causes at the age of 92.

The new year is when a new calendar year starts, and the year number increases by one. Many cultures celebrate this event, and January 1 is often a national holiday. In the Gregorian calendar, the most used today, the new year starts on January 1, also known as New Year's Day. This was the first day of the year in the Julian calendar and the Roman calendar after 153 BC. In the Middle Ages, in Western Europe, authorities moved New Year's Day to different dates depending on the place, such as March 1, March 25, Easter, September 1, or December 25, while using the Julian calendar. After 1582, the adoption of the Gregorian calendar meant many places now use January 1 for New Year's Day. Other cultures celebrate their own new year according to their traditions or religions, sometimes alongside the Gregorian calendar. Examples include Chinese New Year, Islamic New Year, Traditional Japanese New Year, and Jewish New Year. India and some other countries also celebrate New Year on different dates.

Romain Rolland was born on January 29, 1866, and died on December 30, 1944. He was a French writer, known for his plays, novels, essays, and writings about art. It works similarly to brakes on cars, but is more complex because it needs to manage multiple connected carriages and still be effective without an engine. M*A*S*H is an American story with many parts, including books, a movie, and TV shows. It is owned by 20th Century Fox (now 20th Century Studios) and is based on Richard Hooker's stories. The story is about a group of characters who work at a pretend hospital called "4077th Mobile Army Surgical Hospital" during the Korean War.
