Earl Wilbur Sutherland Jr. was born on November 19, 1915, in Burlingame, Kansas. He was an American pharmacologist and biochemist. Sutherland won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1971. He got this prize for his discoveries about how hormones work, especially with epinephrine. His work focused on second messengers, specifically cyclic AMP, or cyclic AMP.
G levelsberg is a town in Ennepe-Ruhr-Kreis district, which is in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.

Francisco Waldir Pires de Souza, born on October 21, 1926, and died on June 22, 2018, was a Brazilian politician. He worked as the Minister of Defence under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Later, he was fired because he was considered too incompetent and inactive during Brazil's aviation crisis from 2006 to 2007. Some Brazilians thought he was becoming senile at the time. He was replaced by Nelson Jobim, who was a former president of the Supreme Court. During his time, Souza also led the Brazilian mission to Haiti under MINUSTAH. This mission caused chaos in Haiti after a rogue former police chief removed President Jean-Bertrand Aristide.

Patrick James Riley, born on March 20, 1945, is an American basketball executive. He was also a coach and player in the NBA. Riley has been the Miami Heat's team president since 1995 and coached them twice (1995-2003, 2005-2008). As a player, he was on the Lakers' championship team in 1972. Riley is one of the best NBA coaches of all time. He coached five championship teams, including four with the Lakers during their successful period in the 1980s and one with the Heat in 2006. He was named NBA Coach of the Year three times (1989-90, 1992-93, and 1996-97). He coached the NBA All-Star game nine times, mostly with the Lakers (1982, 1983, 1985-1990) and once with the Knicks (1993). Riley is the first North American sports figure to win championships as a player, assistant coach, head coach, and executive. In 1996, he was named one of the top 10 NBA coaches of all time. Recently, Riley won the 2012 and 2013 NBA championships as the Heat's team president. He received the Chuck Daly Lifetime Achievement Award from the NBA Coaches Association in 2012.

Bloomsburg is a town in Columbia County, Pennsylvania, United States. It is southwest of Wilkes-Barre and near the Susquehanna River. Bloomsburg is the county seat of Columbia County and the only Pennsylvania town named as such. In 2010, the population was 14,855. By 2019, it was estimated to be 13,811. Bloomsburg is part of the Bloomsburg-Berwick, PA micropolitan area, which includes Columbia and Montour counties. In 2010, the combined population was 85,562.
Walala Tjapaltjarri, born Walala Tjapangati, is an Australian Aboriginal artist.

The United States has many types of laws. The most important is the U.S. Constitution, which sets up the federal government and protects people's rights. Federal laws include acts of Congress, treaties, rules made by the executive branch, and decisions from the courts. The U.S. Code is a book of the main federal laws. Federal laws and treaties, if they don't go against the Constitution, can override state laws in the 50 states and territories. However, the federal government doesn't have power over everything. In the U.S. system, states have a lot of power too, as long as they don't break the Constitution. States can give their citizens more rights than the federal government, as long as those rights don't conflict with the Constitution. Most laws that people use every day, like those about contracts, injuries, property, crimes, and family matters, come from state laws. These laws can be very different from state to state. The U.S. legal system mainly comes from the common law system of England, which was in place when the United States became independent. But American law has changed a lot from English law in both what it says and how it works. American law has also added some ideas from civil law.

Meresankh I, who lived long ago, was a wife of an Egyptian king and the mother of King Sneferu. She might have also been married to King Huni, the last king of the 3rd dynasty. Her name is on an old stone piece called the Palermo stone. An estate might be named after her in a place called Saqqara. Her name is also found in graffiti in the Pyramid Temple at Meidum, alongside her son Sneferu. This graffiti dates back to when King Tuthmosis III ruled during the 18th dynasty. The text there says a wish for the "ka" of King Sneferu and Queen Meresankh.

Gerald Götting was a German politician born on June 9, 1923, and died on May 19, 2015. He was the leader of the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) in East Germany from 1966 to 1989. Götting also served as the president of the People's Chamber from 1969 to 1976. From 1960 to 1989, he was the deputy chairman of the State Council in East Germany.

In economics, a free market is a system where prices for goods and services are set by buyers and sellers in the open market. In a free market, the government does not interfere, and there are no special advantages or monopolies. Advocates of free markets see it as different from a regulated market, where the government uses methods like tariffs to control trade and protect local businesses. In an ideal free-market economy, prices are set by supply and demand, without government rules. Experts compare free markets to coordinated markets, which consider external rules and institutions that affect how supply and demand work. These rules help control production and distribution. Free markets are often linked to capitalism, but they are also supported by anarchists, socialists, and some who believe in cooperatives and profit sharing. Some critics argue that systems with significant power or unfair information can be unfair, and that rules are needed to make markets work better and achieve better social results.

Lipscomb County is in Texas, a state in the U.S. The 2010 census showed 3,302 people lived there. Lipscomb is the county seat. The county was created in 1876 and officially set up in 1887. It is named after Judge Abner Smith Lipscomb, who was a secretary of state of the Republic of Texas.
Didier Bezace was a French actor who was born on February 10, 1946, and passed away on March 11, 2020.

Nadap is a village in Fejér County, central Hungary. It has 460 people living there. Nestled among low hills, Nadap is a starting point for countryside tours. There is an obelisk nearby called "Ancient Mark of Nadap." It is used as a reference point and stands at 173. 8 meters high. Mihály Vörösmarty was baptized in the Catholic church of Saint Rosalia in Nadap. The baptismal basin is still in the church.

Surya Bahadur Thapa was Nepal's only five-time prime minister. He lived from March 21, 1928, to April 15, 2015. Thapa served as prime minister under three different kings for over 50 years. He first became acting prime minister in 1955 but was not well-known at the time. He later became respected and well-liked. In 1959, he was elected to the upper house and served as chair of the council of ministers from 1963 to 1964. Thapa then served as prime minister four more times: from 1965 to 1969, 1979 to 1983, 1997 to 1998, and 2003. He left his Rastriya Prajatantra Party in November 2004. In his later years, he led the Rastriya Janashakti Party. Thapa passed away from respiratory failure during surgery on April 15, 2015.

A mast cell is a type of cell found in connective tissue. It has many granules filled with histamine and heparin. Mast cells are a kind of granulocyte that comes from myeloid stem cells. They are part of the immune and neuroimmune systems. Dr. Paul Ehrlich discovered mast cells in 1877. Mast cells are known for their role in allergies and severe reactions like anaphylaxis. However, they also help in wound healing, blood vessel growth, stopping harmful substances, and protecting the blood-brain barrier. Mast cells look and function similarly to basophils, another type of white blood cell. But research shows they develop differently and are not the same cells.

Amanda Michelle Seyfried, born on December 3, 1985, is an American actress, singer, and model. She grew up in Allentown, Pennsylvania. Seyfried started modeling at 11 and acted for the first time when she was 15. She played Lucy Montgomery in the TV soap opera "As the World Turns" from 1999 to 2001, and Joni Stafford in "All My Children" in 2003. Her acting career took off after she was in the movie "Mean Girls" in 2004 and acted in "Veronica Mars" from 2004 to 2006. She had roles in films like "Nine Lives" and "Alpha Dog" and acted as Sarah Henrickson in "Big Love" from 2006 to 2011. Seyfried then starred in several popular films, including "Mamma Mia!" in 2008, "Jennifer's Body" in 2009, "Red Riding Hood" in 2011, and "Les Misérables" in 2012, where she was nominated for a Screen Actors Guild award. She continued her acting career with roles in "Gone," "Lovelace," "The Big Wedding," "A Million Ways to Die in the West," "Ted 2," "Pan," "Fathers and Daughters," "First Reformed," "The Clapper," "Anon," "Gringo," "Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again," and "The Art of Racing in the Rain." She also did voice work in animated films like "Epic" and "Scoob!"
Ellen Marie Elze Anthing Vogel, born on January 26, 1922, and died on August 5, 2015, was an actress from the Netherlands. She performed in films, on stage, and on television.

The question mark is a punctuation mark that shows a question. It is also called an interrogation point, a query, or an eroteme in journalism. It is used for direct questions but not for indirect ones. People also use the question mark to show missing or unknown information. In Unicode, it is represented by a specific code.
In the United States politics and government, the term "presidential nominee" can have two different meanings.

Alois Hitler Sr., born Alois Schicklgruber on June 7, 1837, died on January 3, 1903. He was an Austrian civil servant and the father of Adolf Hitler, who became the dictator of Nazi Germany. Alois was born out of wedlock, and his father was never known. This led some to believe that Adolf Hitler's mother, Klara, might have been Alois's cousin. Because of this, Adolf could not prove his grandfather's identity, making it hard for him to show he had "Aryan descent." When Alois was promoted, he changed his name to Hitler, for reasons that are unclear. Alois and Adolf had a bad relationship, often punishing Adolf severely.

Rock of Ages Corporation is a granite quarry and finishing company in Graniteville, Vermont. It started in 1885. The company has about 230 workers. In 2009, they earned about $800,000 from sales of $21.6 million, improving from a loss of over $2 million in 2008. On October 19, 2010, Swenson Granite from Concord, New Hampshire, agreed to merge with Rock of Ages. Swenson paid Rock of Ages shareholders $39 million. On September 16, 2016, Polycor Inc., a stone producer in Quebec, Canada, bought Swenson Granite and Rock of Ages Corporation. This made Polycor the biggest granite and marble producer in North America. They also took over Rock of Ages in Stanstead, Quebec. Rock of Ages has the world's largest "deep hole" granite quarry, called the "E.L. Smith Quarry." They mine Devonian Barre granite there. In the past, they used simple tools like hand saws and explosions. Now, they use machines with diamond-tipped saws and water jets. Visitors can watch the quarriers at work. The company was featured in a 2005 PBS documentary about cemetery-related businesses.

The mighty Bosstones, often just called Bosstones, is an American ska punk band from Boston, Massachusetts. They started in 1983. Since then, Dicky Barrett (lead singer), Joe Gittleman (bass), Tim Burton (tenor sax), and Ben Carr (dancer) have always been part of the band. Other regular members include Joe Sirois (drummer), Leon Silva (sax), Lawrence Katz (guitar), John Goetchius (keyboard), and Chris Rhodes (trombone). The Bosstones are known for creating ska punk and a subgenre called ska-core. Their first album, "Devil's Night Out," came out in 1989. They played and recorded a lot in the 1990s, and they were very important for the American ska scene. Their 1997 album "Let's Face It" and the hit song "The Impression That I Get" were their biggest successes. They made seven studio albums, three EPs, and a live album before taking a break in 2003. In 2007, the band came back and have since made three more albums. They also host a yearly music festival called the Hometown Throwdown in Boston around Christmas time, from 1994 to 2002, and again since 2007.

The Regional Representative Council, or DPD (short for Dewan Perwakilan Daerah), is one of two chambers in Indonesia's parliament. Along with the DPR (Dewan Perwakilan Rakyat), it forms the Indonesian national legislative body known as the MPR (Majelis Permusyawaratan Rakyat). The DPD's main role is to focus on regional government matters. It can suggest and advise on bills to the DPR but cannot make laws directly. Members of the DPD are often called senators instead of DPD members.
An antacid neutralizes stomach acid and is used to ease heartburn, indigestion, or an upset stomach.

Taiwan, also known as the Republic of China (ROC), is a country in East Asia. It neighbors the People's Republic of China (PRC) to the northwest, Japan to the northeast, and the Philippines to the south. The main island of Taiwan is large, with mountain ranges covering most of the eastern part and plains in the western part where many people live. Taipei is the capital and largest city. Other big cities include New Taipei, Kaohsiung, Taichung, Tainan, and Taoyuan. With 23.7 million people, Taiwan is densely populated and the most populous non-UN member country with the largest non-UN economy. Taiwanese people first settled the island about 6,000 years ago. In the 17th century, Dutch colonization started, leading to more Han Chinese migration. In 1683, the island became part of the Qing Dynasty of China. It was then given to Japan in 1895. After Japan surrendered in 1945, the ROC, which had replaced the Qing in 1911, took control of Taiwan. The loss of the mainland to the Communist Party of China led the ROC government to move to Taiwan in 1949. Since then, the ROC has ruled Taiwan and some smaller islands. In the 1960s, Taiwan experienced rapid economic growth and industrialization. In the late 1980s and early 1990s, the ROC became a multi-party democracy. Today, Taiwan's economy is the 21st-largest in the world, with major industries in steel, machinery, electronics, and chemicals. It is a developed country with a high GDP per capita and good records in freedom, education, health, and human development. The political status of Taiwan is uncertain. The ROC is not a UN member, replaced by the PRC in 1971. The PRC claims Taiwan and doesn't allow countries to recognize the ROC. Taiwan has official ties with 14 UN member states and the Holy See. The PRC doesn't let Taiwan join international organizations or participate fully. However, Taiwan is part of the World Trade Organization, Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, and the Asian Development Bank under different names. Neighboring countries and large economies have unofficial ties with Taiwan through offices that act as "de facto" embassies and consulates. Domestically, the main political debate is between those who support eventual unification with China and those who favor independence for Taiwan.
Aulnois-sous-Laon is a town in the Aisne department, in Hauts-de-France, which is in northern France. The people who live there are called Aulnoisiens or Aulnoisiennes.

Jacques Houplain was a French painter and engraver. He was born on September 10, 1920, and died on February 22, 2020.

Mahākāla is a deity found in Hinduism, Buddhism, and Sikhism. In Hinduism, Mahākāla is a form of Shiva and is Mahākālī's partner. He is a key figure in Shaktism. In Vajrayana Buddhism, especially in Tibetan traditions, he is called Citipati. He also appears as a protector in Chinese and Shingon Buddhism. In these cultures, he is known as "dàhēitiān" and "daaih'hāktīn" in Chinese, "daeheukcheon" in Korean, "đại hắc thiên" in Vietnamese, and "daikokuten" in Japanese. In Sikhism, Mahākāla is known as Kal, who rules over Maya.

The Gulf of Gonâve is a large area in the Caribbean Sea, next to Haiti. Haiti's capital, Port-au-Prince, is near the Gulf. Other cities by the Gulf include Gonaïves, Saint-Marc, Miragoâne, and Jérémie. There are some islands in the Gulf. The biggest is Gonâve Island, with smaller Cayemites islands nearby.

Fillmore is a small city in Ventura County, California. It is in the Santa Clara River Valley and is in an area that is good for farming because the soil is rich and fertile. Fillmore has an old downtown area that started in 1887. That's when the Southern Pacific Railroad built a line through the valley. The town got its name from J. A. Fillmore, who was a general manager for the company's Pacific system. In 2010, Fillmore had 15,002 people. That was more than in 2000, when it had 13,643 people.

Ivy Queen, born Martha Ivelisse Pesante Rodríguez on March 4, 1972, is a singer, songwriter, rapper, actress, and record producer from Puerto Rico. She first gained attention as a member of the Noise in Puerto Rico. Her first song there was "Somos Raperos pero no delincuentes" (We are rappers, not delinquents). In 1996, she went solo and released her first album "En mi imperio (In My Empire)" in 1997, which Sony Discos started selling. Her second album "The Original Rude Girl" had a hit song "In the Zone." Ivy Queen gained more fame in 2003 when she released "Diva" on an independent label. Her albums "Diva," "Flashback," and "Sentimiento" were all very successful, getting gold and platinum awards. In 2010, she released "Drama Queen," which had a top ten hit "La Vida Es Así." Her 2012 album "Musa" was nominated for a Grammy. Ivy Queen's music often talks about strong women, cheating, and relationships. She is known as the queen of reggaeton. She also acts and has a doll made to look like her. In 2012, she appeared in a play called "The Vagina Monologues." In 2017, she was one of the richest reggaeton artists with a net worth of $10 million.

In mathematics, a real number is a value that can show a distance on a line or an infinite decimal. The term "real" was first used by René Descartes in the 17th century to distinguish between real and imaginary roots of polynomials. Real numbers include rational numbers, like -5 and 4/3, and irrational numbers, such as the square root of 2. Transcendental numbers, like pi, are also irrational. Real numbers can measure things like time, mass, and speed. Real numbers can be thought of as points on a number line. Any real number can be shown as a decimal, like 8.632, where each digit is smaller by a tenth. Real numbers are part of complex numbers and are also part of the complex plane. To be precise in math, real numbers are defined as the unique complete ordered field. They can also be defined using Cauchy sequences, Dedekind cuts, or infinite decimals, with clear interpretations for operations and order. The set of all real numbers is uncountable, meaning there are more real numbers than natural numbers. The size of the real numbers is called the cardinality of the continuum, denoted by the symbol 2^ℵ₀, which is greater than the cardinality of natural numbers, ℵ₀. The continuum hypothesis states that there is no set whose size is strictly between the size of the natural numbers and the size of the real numbers. This hypothesis cannot be proven or disproven using standard math rules.

In Djibouti, there have been two presidents since 1977. The president is like the country's leader and also runs the government. They are in charge of the armed forces too. The current president is Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, who has been in this role since 1999.

Affoltern district, also called Knonauamt or Säuliamt, is one of twelve districts in the canton of Zurich, Switzerland. The capital of this district is the city of Affoltern am Albis.

The Co-operative Party is a centre-left political party in the UK that supports co-operative values and principles. It was founded in 1917 by co-operative societies to campaign for fair treatment of co-operative businesses and to elect 'co-operators' to Parliament. Its origins go back to a parliamentary committee of the Co-operative Union created in 1881. Since 1927, the Co-operative Party has had an agreement with the Labour Party. Both parties won't compete against each other and instead, candidates from both parties run using the "Labour and Co-operative Party" label. The Co-operative Party is legally separate from the Labour Party but is registered as a political party with the Electoral Commission. Co-operative Party members can't be part of any other UK political party except the Labour Party or Northern Ireland's Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP). The Co-operative Party has 26 members of Parliament, which makes it one of the largest parties in the House of Commons. However, all its MPs are part of the Parliamentary Labour Party, so this status is rarely mentioned. The party also has representatives in the House of Lords, the Scottish Parliament, the Senedd, the London Assembly, and local government. Following its co-operative values, the Co-operative Party doesn't have a leader. Instead, Joe Fortune serves as the general secretary, and Jim McMahon is the chair of the Co-operative Party group in Parliament.
Rickenbach is the name of several places. In Germany, there is a place called Rickenbach. In Switzerland, there is also a place called Rickenbach.

Jesse Lawrence Ferguson was an American actor born on June 8, 1941, and died on April 26, 2019. He is best remembered for his role as a police officer who was not happy with himself in the movie "Boyz n the Hood," which was directed by John Singleton and was nominated for an Academy Award.
Ebnat-kappel is a municipality in the constituency of Toggenburg in the canton of St. Gallen in Switzerland.

In 2001, there was an American movie based on a true story. It tells about a woman who became a mom at a young age and later got a master's degree. The film covers the years from 1961 to 1986. It stars Drew Barrymore, Steve Zahn, Brittany Murphy, and James Woods. This was the last movie directed by Penny Marshall. While the movie was made with the help of the author, Beverly Donofrio, some parts of the story are different from her book.

Dargai is an administrative area in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, located in the Malakand District. Another area in the same district is Batkhela. Dargai is on the main highway connecting Peshawar, Swat, Dir, and Chitral. The town of Dargai is growing economically because it is a trade hub between the northern and southern parts of Pakistan. It is known for selling timber. Historically, Dargai was the last train station before entering northern Pakistan. Dargai used to be part of the Malakand Agency tribal area until 1970. In 1970, Chitral, Dir, and Swat were combined into the Malakand Division. This division was then divided into districts, one of which was the Malakand Protected Area, now known as the Malakand District. In 2000, the Malakand Division was abolished. Since 1970, the name "Malakand Agency" is sometimes still used for the entire former agency area.

A gravitational singularity is a place in space where gravity is so strong that the laws of normal space do not work. It's mainly talked about in two ways: inside black holes and at the start of the universe during the Big Bang. Scientists aren't sure if these singularities really exist or if we just don't know enough to explain them yet. In a black hole, if a star collapses beyond a certain point, a singularity forms inside, covered by a boundary called the event horizon. According to general relativity, the path of light or anything falling into a black hole would end at the singularity. At the start of the Big Bang, the universe might have been a singularity too. But the early universe was very different from stars, so the rules that work for stars might not apply. We can't use current knowledge to fully describe what happened at the beginning of the universe. Neither general relativity nor quantum mechanics can explain the very first moments of the Big Bang. However, quantum mechanics tells us that particles can't exist in spaces smaller than their wavelengths.

Mirosława Litmanowicz, born Kałęcka on September 6, 1928, was a Polish chess player. She won the Polish women's chess championship in 1968. In 1967, she became a FIDE Woman International Master. She passed away on August 18, 2017.

Throckmorton County is in Texas. In 2010, it had 1,641 people. The county seat is Throckmorton. It was created in 1858 and organized in 1879. The county is named after William Throckmorton, an early settler. Throckmorton County is one of six counties in Texas where alcohol is not allowed.

Dmitry Vladimirovich Strakhov, born on May 17, 1995, is a Russian professional racing cyclist. He currently rides for a UCI ProTeam. In 2017, he competed in the men's point race event at the UCI Track Cycling World Championships. In May 2019, he was included in the list of cyclists for the 2019 Giro d’Italia. On March 11, 2020, it was reported that Strakhov had been infected with SARS-CoV-2, the virus causing coronavirus disease 2019. He was hospitalized in an Abu Dhabi hospital after being placed in quarantine following the 2020 UAE Tour.

The Limbourg brothers, Herman, Paul, and Johan, were famous Dutch miniaturists. They lived and worked between about 1385 and 1416 in Nijmegen. They were active in France and Burgundy during the early 15th century. Their art was part of the International Gothic style. They are best known for creating the "Très Riches Heures du Duc de Berry," a famous late medieval illuminated manuscript.

A hypodermic needle, from the Greek words "under" and "skin," is a thin, hollow tube with a sharp tip. It has a small opening at one end. This needle is often used with a syringe, a hand-operated tool with a plunger, to inject substances like saline solution or medicines into the body. It can also be used to take fluids out of the body, such as blood. Hypodermic needles help take blood from veins during a process called venipuncture. They are especially useful for quick liquid delivery or when substances cannot be taken by mouth, like insulin. Arm areas are commonly used for injections. In research, hypodermic needles are very important. They help keep things clean when putting substances into sterile surfaces. This works because the needle's smooth surface stops tiny germs from sticking, and its sharpness makes tiny holes that keep out larger germs.

Melissa Suzanne McBride, born on May 23, 1965, is an American actress and former casting director. Her most famous role is Carol Peletier on the AMC series "The Walking Dead," which began in 2010 and continues to present. She has been widely praised for her performance and has received several awards and nominations. Initially, she was cast in a small part and only credited in the post-credits. However, her role grew over time, and she became a main cast member. As of 2020, she is the second-billed cast member in the opening credits and appears in every season of the show, along with Norman Reedus.

A.C. Moore was an American store that sold arts and crafts. It was owned by Nicole Crafts. The company had 145 stores in the eastern United States. Its main office was in Berlin, New Jersey. On November 25, 2019, A.C. Moore said it would close all its stores and sell some of its stores and other things to a competitor, Michaels.

Pori is a city and municipality on Finland's west coast. It is near the Gulf of Bothnia, at the mouth of the Kokemäenjoki River, west of Tampere, north of Turku, and northwest of Helsinki, Finland's capital. Pori was founded in 1558 by Duke John, who later became John III of Sweden. The city has about 34,000 people and covers an area of 47.3 square kilometers, with 17.1 square kilometers being water. The population density is high. Pori only speaks Finnish. It is the largest city in Finland and the seventh-largest urban area. Pori is also the capital of the Satakunta region, which has 224,028 people, and the Porinkunta sub-region, which has 136,905 people.

clannad, stylized as clannad, is a Japanese visual novel by Key. It came out on April 28, 2004, for Windows computers. Unlike the company's earlier works, "Kanon" and "Air," which were first made for adults and then censored for younger audiences, "Clannad" was made for all ages from the start. It was later released on many game consoles, such as PlayStation 2, PlayStation Portable, Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, PlayStation Vita, PlayStation 4, and Nintendo Switch. An English version was released on Steam in 2015 by Sekai Project. The story follows Tomoya Okazaki, an average high school student. In his last year, he meets several people, including five girls, and helps them solve their problems. The game lets you make choices that affect the story. It was very popular in Japan and ranked as the best-selling PC game at its release. It also made it to the top 50 in Japan several times afterward. In 2005, Key made a follow-up game called "When They Cry: Clannad -After Story-" which focused on one of the main girls, Tomoyo Sakagami. "Clannad" has been adapted into other media. Four manga adaptations have been published, along with comic anthologies, light novels, and art books. There have also been audio dramas and music albums. An animated film was released in 2007, followed by two anime series with original video animation episodes produced between 2007 and 2009. These anime and their OVA episodes were released in North America by Sentai Filmworks. The animated versions were successful in Japan and got good reviews internationally.

The national flag of Bolivia was first used in 1851. It has three colors: red, yellow, and green. In the middle, there is a coat of arms. Some say red represents brave soldiers, green stands for fertility, and yellow shows the nation's mineral wealth. Bolivia, with six other countries, has a flag with its own design inside. Since 2009, the wiphala is also considered an official flag.

The Saturn Relay is a minivan made by General Motors. It was first introduced in 2005 and was made with sister models: the Buick Terraza, Chevrolet Uplander, and Pontiac Montana SV6 in Georgia. The Relay was special because it was the first Saturn minivan without side panels made of polymer. It was also the first Saturn to be a rebadged Chevrolet or Pontiac. The Relay came with a 3.5-liter engine that could go from 0 to 60 mph in about 9 seconds. In 2006, a 3.9-liter engine was added, which was faster and had more power. By 2007, only the 3.9-liter engine was available, and the optional all-wheel drive was dropped. That year, a flex-fuel engine was also an option for fleet use. The Relay scored well in safety tests and was rated to get good gas mileage. It cost around $22,850. It came in three trim levels, with the highest level, Relay 3, available in both front-wheel and all-wheel drive. It could seat seven people, with removable chairs in the second row and a fold-down third row. Standard features included OnStar and a DVD rear entertainment system. Side airbags were optional. The Relay was made until 2007 and was replaced by the Saturn Outlook.
Willis David Gradison Jr. was born on December 28, 1928. He is an American politician from Ohio. Gradison served in the United States House of Representatives from 1975 to 1993.

The Samsung Galaxy Note 10 is part of a series of Android phones made by Samsung. It was released in August 2019 after the Samsung Galaxy Note 9. People knew a lot about it before it was announced. In 2020, Samsung also introduced a less expensive version called the Galaxy Note 10 Lite.

In gardening and agriculture, companion planting means placing different plants close together for several reasons. These include keeping pests away, helping with pollination, attracting helpful insects, using space efficiently, and increasing crop productivity. Companion planting is a type of polyculture. People use companion planting in both industrial and developing countries for various purposes. The ideas behind companion planting have been around for a long time. They were found in old English cottage gardens and Asian forest gardens many centuries ago, and even thousands of years ago in Mesoamerica.
Melano is a municipality in the Lugano district, which is in the Canton of Ticino, Switzerland.

The 1983-84 NHL season was the 67th season of the National Hockey League. The Edmonton Oilers beat the New York Islanders in the Stanley Cup finals. The Islanders had won the Stanley Cup four times in a row, but in this season, the Oilers won four games to one.

Angular velocity in physics describes how quickly an object turns or moves around another point. There are two types: spin angular velocity and orbital angular velocity. Spin angular velocity is about how fast a rigid body rotates around its center. Orbital angular velocity is about how fast a point moves around a fixed point. Spin angular velocity doesn’t depend on where you measure from, unlike orbital angular velocity. Angular velocity is often measured in radians per second, with the unit being radians per second or 1/s. It’s shown with the letter omega (ω). By convention, a positive omega means the object is moving counterclockwise, and a negative omega means clockwise. For instance, a geostationary satellite above the equator makes one full turn every 24 hours. Its angular velocity is 15 degrees per hour or about 0.26 radians per hour. If the satellite is 42,000 km from Earth’s center, its speed is about 11,000 km/h, calculated by multiplying its orbital radius by its angular velocity. In three dimensions, angular velocity is a pseudovector showing the rate of rotation and the direction perpendicular to the rotation plane. The direction is usually shown using the right-hand rule.
Hinton is a town in Caddo County, Oklahoma, United States. In 2010, the town had 3,196 people, which was more than in 2000 when it had 2,175 people. Hinton is roughly west of Oklahoma City.

ronald tauranac, born on january 13, 1925, and died on july 17, 2020, was a British-Australian engineer and racing car designer. In 1962, he and Jack Brabham, a Formula One driver, started the Brabham team. After Brabham stopped racing in 1970, Tauranac led the Brabham team until 1972, when he sold it to Bernie Ecclestone. In 1973, he helped redesign a racing car chassis for Frank Williams and assisted Trojan in creating a Formula One version of their Formula 5000 car. Tauranac briefly retired in Australia before returning to England. There, he started the Ralt marque, using a name he and his brother had used earlier. The first Ralt chassis, called the Ralt RT1, was used in various racing classes and won championships. In 1978, Tauranac designed the Theodore racing car for the Formula One season. For the 1979 season, he created two new designs: the RT2 for Formula Two and the RT3 for Formula Three. The RT3 won several championships. Tauranac worked with Honda on the RH6 chassis, which also won championships in 1981, 1984, and 1985. He sold the Ralt business to March Engineering in 1988 for £1.25 million. After leaving Ralt, Tauranac continued his involvement in racing, working with Honda, consulting for the Arrows Formula One team, and staying connected with Honda. He also judged the Formula SAE Australia competition in Melbourne. In 2002, Tauranac was honored with the Officer of the Order of Australia for his contributions to motor racing, particularly for his engineering work and for providing young drivers with opportunities to compete at high levels. He passed away in 2020 at the age of 95.
Lovelock is the biggest town in Big Horn County, Wyoming, United States. In 2010, the town had 2,360 people.

Gustavo José Joaquín Noboa Bejarano was born on August 21, 1937, in Guayaquil, Ecuador. He is an Ecuadorian politician. Noboa was the president of Ecuador from January 22, 2000, to January 15, 2003. He also served as vice president during Jamil Mahuad's government.

Vandervoort is a town in Polk County, Arkansas, United States. In the year 2000, the town had 120 people. The town is named after the mother of a significant early-20th-century railway financier named Jan de Goeijen. Her original name was Van der Voort.

Here is a list of the 33 counties in New Mexico. In 1852, there were nine counties formed. One of them, Santa Ana County, was added to Bernalillo County in 1876. Each county has a special code. New Mexico's code is 35, and when combined with any county code, it looks like 35xxx. You can find more information about each county by looking at their codes.

Alexander Stuart "Jock" Sturrock MBE was born on May 14, 1915, in Melbourne and died on July 11, 1997, in Noosa Heads. He was an Australian yachtsman who won many yachting races. He won over four hundred international, national, state, and club championships.

The bleating tree frog, also called Keferstein's tree frog, is a type of tree frog in the family Pelodryadidae. This frog lives along the coast in eastern Australia, from southeast Queensland to Eden in New South Wales.

The National Symphony Orchestra (NSO) was formed in 1930. It is a symphony orchestra in Washington, D.C. They play at the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. The NSO was the official orchestra for the National Memorial Day Concert and the Capitol Fourth.
axes, which is the plural of both "axe" and "axis," can mean different things.

A neural network is a system made up of nodes, or artificial neurons. These can be real biological neurons or artificial ones used to solve AI problems. In artificial neural networks, connections are represented as weights. Positive weights show excitatory connections, while negative ones show inhibitory connections. Each input is changed by a weight and added together. This is called a linear combination. An activation function then controls the output's strength. Outputs often range from 0 to 1, or from -1 to 1. These networks can be trained with data and can learn from experience to draw conclusions from complex information.

On July 15, 2020, between 8 PM and 10 PM UTC, around 130 important Twitter accounts were taken over by outside people to spread a Bitcoin scam. Twitter and other news sources said the hackers used special tools to change the accounts and post messages themselves. They seemed to have gotten access through Twitter workers using social engineering. Three people were arrested on July 31, 2020, and charged with wire fraud, money laundering, identity theft, and unauthorized computer access for the scam. The scam messages asked people to send Bitcoin to a specific wallet, promising they would get their money back doubled as a charity. In just minutes, over 320 transactions happened, and Bitcoin worth more than had been in one account before Twitter removed the scam messages. Also, data from eight non-verified accounts was taken. Cybersecurity expert Dmitri Alperovitch called this "the worst hack of a major social media platform so far." Law enforcement, including the FBI, is looking into the scam and Twitter’s security. Researchers worry this social engineering could affect important online discussions, like before the 2020 US presidential election.

Madeline Gail Kahn, born Madeline Gail Wolfson, was an American actress, comedian, and singer. She was famous for funny roles in movies directed by Peter Bogdanovich and Mel Brooks, such as "What's Up, Doc?" (1972), "Young Frankenstein" (1974), "High Anxiety" (1977), "History of the World, Part I" (1981), and "Blazing Saddles" (1974), where she was nominated for an Academy Award. Kahn started her Broadway career in "Leonard Sillman's New Faces of 1968." She was nominated for a Tony Award for the play "In the Boom Boom Room" in 1974 and for the musical "On the Twentieth Century" in 1978. She was in a TV show called "Oh Madeline" (1983-84) and won a Daytime Emmy Award in 1987 for an "ABC Afterschool Special." Kahn was nominated again for a Tony Award for the play "Born Yesterday" in 1989 and won the Tony Award for Best Actress in a Play in 1993 for the comedy "The Sisters Rosensweig." Other films she appeared in were "The Cheap Detective" (1978), "City Heat" (1984), "Clue" (1985), and "Nixon" (1995).

An oar is a tool used to move boats in water. It has a flat blade on one end. Rowers hold the other end. Oars are used only for rowing. They are connected to the boat through a pivot point, usually an oarlock or a thole. The oar has a small part inside the boat and a larger part outside. When the rower pulls on the inside part, the blade moves through the water, pushing the boat forward. An oar works like a second class lever, with the water as the fulcrum, the oarlock as the load, and the rower as the force. Oars increase the small movement of the rower's hand into a larger movement of the boat. Rowers face the back of the boat, reach toward the back, and place the oar blade in the water. As they lean back, the blade pivots in the oarlock, moving the end in the water toward the back of the boat, providing forward thrust. For many years, boats were moved by sails, rowers, or paddlers. Some old boats used both oars and sails depending on the wind.

A medical abortion, also called a medication abortion, happens when pills are used to end a pregnancy. The usual treatment includes two medicines: first, mifepristone, then misoprostol. Using these medicines, starting with mifepristone and then misoprostol, is both safe and effective for abortions at different stages of pregnancy. If mifepristone is not available, misoprostol can be used alone.

Ji Guobiao was born on March 1, 1932, and passed away on September 5, 2019. He was a Chinese chemical engineer and a member of the Chinese Academy of Engineering. Ji Guobiao was a pioneer in chemical fiber engineering technology in China.
the Berowra division is an area used for voting in Australia. It is in the state of New South Wales.

Phosphorus pentafluoride, PF, is a type of phosphorus halide. It is a colorless, toxic gas that produces fumes when exposed to air.

Ksenia Arturovna Tripolitova was born on May 7, 1915, in Vilna, which was part of the Russian Empire. She became a French ballet dancer. She studied dance with Lyubov Yegorova. Ksenia and her husband performed together in the 1930s and 1940s. In the 1960s, she started her own dance career. During World War II, she performed in France when the Nazis were there. In 1949, she performed in Switzerland. By the end of the 1950s, she and her husband formed a dance group called "Troika." In 1954-1955, she worked at the opera in Tunis. In 1957, she performed with the Ural Cossack choir in Spain. Ksenia turned 100 in 2015. She passed away in Paris on April 9, 2020, at the age of 104.

The Allen Telescope Array (ATA), formerly called the One Hectare Telescope (1HT), is a radio telescope used for observing space and searching for signs of intelligent life elsewhere. Located at the Hat Creek Radio Observatory in Shasta County, northeast of San Francisco, California, it was first built by the SETI Institute and the Radio Astronomy Laboratory (RAL) at UC Berkeley. The project started with a $11.5 million donation from the Paul G. Allen Family Foundation. Paul Allen, a co-founder of Microsoft, added another $13.5 million to complete the first and second phases. The ATA began operating in October 2007 with 42 antennas (ATA-42). While Paul Allen contributed over $30 million, the project didn't build the originally planned 350, 6.1-meter dishes. Due to lack of funding, the ATA stopped working from April to August 2011, but then resumed operations. In 2012, UC Berkeley left the project, and the facility is now run by SRI International, a nonprofit research organization. The SETI Institute uses the ATA from 6 PM to 6 AM daily. In 2014, a forest fire threatened the installation, causing a brief shutdown. However, the ATA survived the fire mostly intact.

BAAFAL, or the British Association for Applied Linguistics, is a society in the UK. It helps people who are interested in language and applied linguistics. BAAFAL holds regular meetings for its members in different places in the UK. They also publish conference proceedings and send out a newsletter. BAAFAL gives scholarships to students. There is an elected executive committee that speaks for the members. Dawn Knight is the current chair. BAAFAL has over 1200 members from around the world and is a registered charity in the UK with the number 246800.

An airliner is a plane used to transport people and goods. Airlines usually operate these planes. Generally, an airliner is a multi-passenger aircraft used for commercial flights. The biggest ones are wide-body jets, which have two aisles and are used for long flights between major cities. Smaller, common airliners, known as narrow-body or single-aisle planes, are used for shorter or medium-length flights with fewer passengers. Regional airliners, seating less than 100 people, can use turbofans or turboprops. These are smaller than the larger planes used by major airlines. They help bring passengers to the main airline hubs. Regional routes form the spokes of the hub-and-spoke model. For short flights, smaller planes called commuter aircraft, commuterliners, or feederliners can have just 19 seats, like the Beechcraft 1900.

Duck Commander is a brand for duck calls and the name of a company in West Monroe, Louisiana, United States. The company makes duck calls and other hunting gear. They also have products for deer hunting under Buck Commander and for turkey hunting under Strut Commander. Phil Robertson, who was a football player, started the company. He made duck calls in an old boat for 25 years using trees from Louisiana. Willie Robertson, Phil's son, is now the CEO and has grown the company into a big business. The Robertson family and their business are in a TV show called "Duck Dynasty" on A&E. Before that, they were on a show called "Duck Commander" on the Outdoor Channel.

Halabja is a city in the Kurdistan region of Iraq. It is the capital of the Halabja governorate. Halabja is located northeast of Baghdad and near the Iranian border. The city is part of the greater Hewraman region, which extends across the Iran-Iraq border. Surrounding Halabja are the Hawraman and Shnrwe ranges in the northeast, the Balambo range in the south, and the Sirwan River to the west. Most people in Halabja speak the Sorani dialect of Kurdish. Some people in nearby villages speak the Hewrami dialect.

The Meissner effect is when a superconductor expels a magnetic field when cooled below a certain temperature. In 1933, Walther Meissner and Robert Ochsenfeld found this by cooling tin and lead samples. When these samples were cooled, they reduced most magnetic fields inside. They saw this by changes in external magnetic fields, as superconductors keep the same total magnetic field. This showed that superconductors are not just good conductors but have a unique property. The Meissner state is when a superconductor has no magnetic field inside. In type-I superconductors, this state ends when the magnetic field is too strong. Type-II superconductors can mix magnetic field and superconducting regions. Most pure superconductors, except niobium and carbon nanotubes, are type-I, while most impure and compound superconductors are type-II.

"Misery" is a song by Maroon 5, an American band. It came out on June 22, 2010, through A&M Octone Records. This song was the first single from their album "Hands All Over," which was released in 2010.

This list includes the cities and towns in North Macedonia. There are 34 cities in total, with 5 having over 50,000 people and 12 having fewer than 10,000. The capital, Skopje, has about one-quarter of the country's population. In 2002, nearly 60% of people lived in urban areas. Twelve small towns in North Macedonia have fewer than 10,000 people: Demir Hisar (2,593), Peševo (3,237), Demir Kapija (3,275), Makedonski Brod (3,740), Valandovo (4,402), Makedonska Kamenica (5,147), Kruševo (5,330), Bogdanci (6,011), Kratovo (6,924), Berovo (7,002), Probištip (8,714), and Resen (8,748). These are sometimes called "small towns" because of their size. North Macedonia has only five cities with over 50,000 people: Skopje (506,926), Bitola (74,550), Kumanovo (70,842), Prilep (66,246), and Tetovo (86,580). These are the biggest cities in the country. Seventeen towns have populations between 10,000 and 50,000: Veles (43,716), Stip (43,652), Ohrid (42,033), Gostivar (35,847), Strumica (35,311), Kavadarci (29,188), Kočani (28,330), Kičevo (27,067), Struga (16,559), Radoviš (16,223), Gevgelija (15,685), Debar (14,561), Kriva Palanka (14,558), Svjetni Nikole (13,746), Negotino (13,284), Delčevo (11,500), and Vinica (10,863). These towns are often called "medium-sized cities".
Cool is a town in Parker County, Texas, United States. In 2010, the population was 157.

The Russian Empire expanded across Europe, Asia, and North America from 1721, after the Great Northern War, until 1917, when the provisional government declared a republic. It was the third-largest empire in history, stretching over three continents. The empire was as large as the British and Mongol empires. The Romanovs ruled from 1721 to 1762, and the House of Holstein-Gottorp-Romanov took over until the end. In the early 19th century, the empire covered from the Arctic Ocean to the Black Sea, and from the Baltic Sea to Alaska and parts of California. With 125.6 million people in 1897, it was the third most populous country, after Qing China and India. The empire included many different groups, with diverse economies, ethnicities, languages, and religions. Dissenters launched many rebellions and assassinations, closely monitored by secret police. The economy was mainly agricultural, with serfs working large estates. Serfs were freed in 1861, but landowning nobles kept power. Industrialization began with foreign investments in railways and factories. Tsar Ivan III laid the groundwork, expanding the territory, and renovating Moscow. Tsar Peter the Great fought wars, expanded the empire, and moved the capital to St. Petersburg. He promoted modernization and a western influence. Empress Catherine the Great ruled from 1762 to 1796, expanding the empire through conquest and diplomacy. Tsar Alexander II freed the serfs in 1861 and protected Orthodox Christians in the Ottoman Empire. The empire joined World War I against Germany, Austria-Hungary, and the Ottomans. After the 1905 revolution, a constitutional monarchy was established, but the empire struggled in World War I. The imperial family was executed in 1918 by the Bolsheviks, who took power in 1922 after a civil war, forcing many aristocrats into exile or execution and setting up the Soviet Union.

Ongar railway station is on the Epping Ongar railway heritage line. It was also a former London Underground station in the town of Chipping Ongar, Essex. The station opened in 1865 by the Great Eastern Railway and joined London Transport in 1949. It closed in 1994. Until then, it was the easternmost point of the Central Line. From there, all distances on London Underground are measured.

Roberts County is in Texas, United States. In 2010, it had 929 people, which is the smallest population among seven counties in Texas. The county seat is Miami, and it is the only town in the county. Roberts County was created in 1876 and organized in 1889. It is named after Oran Milo Roberts, a former Texas governor. This county is one of six in Texas that do not allow alcohol.

Eye contact happens when two animals look into each other's eyes at the same time. In humans, making eye contact is a way of communicating without talking, and it is believed to affect social behavior. The term "eye contact" was first used in the 1960s, often seen as an important sign of confidence and respect. The meaning of eye contact can differ between societies due to religious and social differences. The study of eye contact is called "oculesics."

Pavement lights, also known as vault lights in the US, floor lights, or sidewalk prisms, are flat-topped lights set into the pavement or floors. They let sunlight into the space below. Often, they use special prisms to throw the light sideways under the building. These lights were created in the 19th century. However, their popularity decreased with the introduction of cheap electric lighting. Many older cities and smaller centers around the world have these lights. Most of them are about a century old. Some new constructions are now installing these lights too.

Lancaster is a city in Fairfield County, Ohio, in the south-central part of the state. According to the 2010 census, it has 38, 780 people. Lancaster is near the Hocking River. It is southeast of Columbus and southwest of Zanesville. Lancaster is the county seat of Fairfield County.

The Korean peninsula mostly has mountains along its east coast. So, most of its rivers flow to the west, emptying into the Yellow Sea. Some rivers go through lakes on their way to the coast, but these lakes are artificial reservoirs. There are no natural lakes on the Korean mainland. A few rivers flow south, emptying into the Korea Strait. Other rivers flow east to East Korea Bay, but they are usually small streams. Here is a list of the rivers, with tributaries listed in the order they flow upstream. The list goes counterclockwise, starting from the Amnok to the Duman.

chopicallqui, possibly from the Quechua words "chawpi" meaning center and "kallki" meaning ravine, is a mountain in the Cordillera Blanca area of the Andes in Peru. At over 5, 000 meters above sea level, it is one of the highest peaks in the Cordillera Blanca. The mountain is located in Yungay province, in the region of Ancash, between Huascarán and Contrahierbas mountains.

Ilkka Olavi Suominen was born on April 8, 1939, in Nakkila, Finland. He is a politician from the National Coalition Party. Suominen was the president of the Nordic Council in 1992. He served in the parliament from 1970 to 1975 and from 1983 to 1994. As the chairman of the National Coalition Party from 1979 to 1991, he was also the speaker of the parliament twice, in 1987 and 1991 to 1994. In 1987 to 1991, he was the minister of trade and industry in the Holkeri cabinet. Suominen left parliament to become the CEO of Alko, a state monopoly. He was elected to the European Parliament as an MEP for one term from 1999 to 2004, representing the EPP. Suominen was also the chairman of the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly from 1992 to 1994.

Wofford Heights is a census-designated place in southern Sierra Nevada, California, United States. It is in Kern County, near the West Kern River Valley. Wofford Heights is south-southwest of Kernville. The elevation is not specified. In 2010, the population was 2,200. It was 2,276 in 2000.

Shakib Khan, born on March 28, 1979, is a popular Bangladeshi film actor, producer, singer, and media personality. Known as "King Khan" and "King of Dhallywood," he has been a key figure in Dhallywood for over two decades. His most famous films include "Priya Amar Priya" (2008), "Shikari" (2016), "Swatta" (2017), and "Nabab" (2017). Khan is the highest-paid actor in Bangladesh. He first gained fame in 1999 with the film "Ananta Bhalobasha." His role in "Priya Amar Priya" was very successful, earning him high praise and the highest pay. "Shikari" was a big hit at the box office. "Swatta" won many awards, and "Nabab" was the highest-grossing film of 2017. Khan also produced films like "Password" (2019) and "Bir" (2020). He has won several awards, including four national film awards for his acting.

Wanrong, also known as the Xuantong Empress, lived from November 13, 1906, to June 20, 1946. She was the empress consort of Puyi, the last Chinese emperor and the final ruler of the Qing dynasty. In 1932, when Japan established a puppet state called Manchukuo in northeastern China and made Puyi its nominal emperor, Wanrong became the empress of Manchukuo. During the Soviet invasion of Manchuria at the end of the Second Sino-Japanese War in 1945, Wanrong was captured by Chinese communist guerrillas. She was moved to different places before being put in a prison camp in Yanji, Jilin. She died in prison sometime between June and August 1946, but her body was never found. On October 23, 2006, Wanrong's younger brother, Runqi, performed a ritual burial for her in the Western Qing Tombs.

Uzlomac is a long mountain in Bosnia, east of the line direction from Maslovare to Vrbanjci to Kotor varoš to Čelinac. It goes from southeast to northwest through the mountainous area, starting from the Kruševica River (west of the Borja Mountains) to Jošavka. The mountain is known for its forests and wildlife. It has mixed forests with deciduous oak and deciduous beech trees. Uzlomac also has many sources of water, like springs, streams, and rivers. Many smaller rivers, including tributaries of the Vrbas and Bosna rivers, start from Uzlomac.

thixotropy is a property where some fluids or gels become thinner over time when shaken or stressed. They then take time to return to their original thicker state. Some fluids, like ketchup, become thinner quickly and are called pseudoplastic. Yogurt takes longer to become thin. Many gels and colloids are thixotropic; they stay solid when not moved but become liquid when shaken. This happens because particles in the fluid need time to organize. Anti-thixotropic fluids, on the other hand, get thicker with constant stress. These are less common than thixotropic fluids.

Arjen Anthony Lucassen, born on April 3, 1960, in Hilversum, Netherlands, is a Dutch singer, songwriter, and musician. He is famous for his progressive metal/rock opera project called Ayreon. Lucassen started his career in 1980 as a guitarist and backup singer for a band named Bodine, using the stage name Iron Anthony. In 1984, he joined a band called Vengeance. After eight years, he left the band and released a solo album in 1992 called "Pools of Sorrow, Waves of Joy," under the nickname Anthony. In 1995, Lucassen released an unnamed album called "Ayreon: The Final Experiment," where he sang, wrote songs, and played most of the instruments. This album led to the creation of Ayreon. Despite being unknown at first, Ayreon gained attention and praise, especially with the release of its third album, "Into the Electric Castle." This helped Lucassen become known as a composer of rock operas. After Ayreon's success, Lucassen started other projects. He is the creator and composer of Star One, Guilt Machine, and The Gentle Storm. He was also the creator and guitarist of Ambeon and Stream of Passion. In some projects, he writes the lyrics. Lucassen plays many instruments, including guitar, keyboards, bass, and banjo. Throughout his career, he has released 26 studio albums, four live albums, two EPs, and 17 singles. He has also contributed to over 50 albums with other artists. Since creating Ayreon, Lucassen has been called a "genius" by many critics, praising his musical composition and originality. In a review of "01011001," AllMusic reviewer Cosmo Lee said the music is so over the top that it almost defies criticism.

Rod Piazza was born on December 18, 1947, in Riverside, California. He is an American blues harmonica player and singer. Piazza has been playing with his band, The Mighty Flyers, since 1980. He formed the band with his pianist wife, Honey Piazza. Their music has a boogie sound that mixes jump blues, West Coast blues, and Chicago blues styles.

A disposable product is made to be used only once and then thrown away or recycled. Sometimes, the term is used for products that can last for several months, like disposable air filters. This is to differentiate them from products that can be cleaned and used again and again, such as washable air filters. The word "disposables" is different from "consumables." In the mechanical world, consumables are items that are used up during a process, like welding rods or tips, and need to be replaced. Examples include welding gas and nozzles. Disposables, on the other hand, are items that can be discarded when they are damaged or no longer useful.

Tiko, once known as ‘keka’ by the Bakweris, is a town and important port in Cameroon’s southwest region. It grew as a market town for Duala (or Douala) fishermen, Bakweri (Kpwe) farmers, and hunters from Molyko, Bwenga, Bulu, and Bokova. The main parts of Tiko include streets 1 to 7, Motombolombo, Down Beach, New Quarter, P & T Quarters, New Layout, Long Street, Likomba, Golf Club, Mutengene, and Ombe. As of 2010, Tiko had about 55,914 people. Tiko is a popular place for tourists visiting Cameroon. The town is also an industrial area mainly used by the CDC (Cameroon Development Corporation), which makes rubber, banana, and palm oil. Tiko has a popular golf club called the Tiko Golf Club, located in Likomba. This golf course has 18 holes and hosts major tournaments during the dry season, as it’s one of only two golf courses in Cameroon. Tiko is also home to the Special Forces, which helps keep the area safe. Mutengene, a small town west of Tiko, is a crossroads leading to Buea and Limbe, which used to be called Victoria.

Hugo Boss is a German luxury fashion company based in Metzingen, Baden-Württemberg. They make clothes, accessories, shoes, and perfumes. Hugo Boss is one of the largest German clothing companies, with sales of €2.9 billion in 2019. Its stock is part of the MDAX. The company started in 1924 by Hugo Boss and first made regular clothes. In the 1930s, during the rise of the Nazi Party, Hugo Boss began making and selling Nazi uniforms. This led to increased sales due to supplying uniforms for organizations like the Hitler Youth and Waffen-SS. After World War II and the founder's death in 1948, Hugo Boss shifted focus to making men's suits. In 1988, the company went public and launched a fragrance line. In 1997, they added men's and women's wear lines, a full women's collection in 2000, and children's clothing in 2006–2007. Hugo Boss has grown into a major global fashion brand, with over 1,113 retail stores worldwide.

Nystagmus is a condition where eyes move involuntarily, sometimes also voluntarily, starting in infancy or later. This can cause reduced vision. Due to these eye movements, it is called "dancing eyes." In normal vision, when the head moves, the eyes move in the opposite direction to keep distant objects clear. The semicircular canals in the ear sense head movement and send signals to the brain. The brain then tells the eye muscles to help the eyes focus on an object. Nystagmus happens when the semicircular canals are stimulated, like during a caloric test, or due to diseases, even when the head is still. The direction of the eye movement depends on which canal is affected. There are two main types of nystagmus: pathological and physiological. Within each type, there are different kinds. Nystagmus can be caused by birth defects, lack of sleep, illnesses, toxins, medications, alcohol, or spinning. While once considered untreatable, new drugs have been found to help with nystagmus treatment. It can sometimes come with dizziness.

In the Roman Empire from the 2nd to the 4th centuries, taurobolium meant sacrificing a bull. Starting in the mid-2nd century, this practice was linked to worshipping the great mother of the gods. Before 159 AD, taurobolium wasn't exclusive to her worship. However, after 159 AD, all private inscriptions about taurobolium mentioned the "magna mater."
The Bas-Rhin department has five arrondissements.

Ugur Yucel, born on May 26, 1957, is a Turkish actor, producer, and director. He studied theater at the Istanbul Municipality Conservatory. From 1975 to 1984, he acted in plays at Kenter Theatre, Tef Kabare, Dormen Theatre, and Şan Müzik Holü. He became known for his roles in "Selamsiz Bandosu" and "Muhsin Bey" in 1987. He achieved wider success when he acted in "Eşkıya" in 1996.

Murray was an Australian electoral division in Victoria. It was in the northern part of the state, next to the Murray River, which separates Victoria from New South Wales. The division included towns like Shepparton, Echuca, Cobram, Yarrawonga, Boort, and Bridgewater. In 2018, Murray was renamed Nicholls. The change took effect for the 2019 federal election.

Calhoun County is a name used for several counties in the United States. These counties were named after John C. Calhoun, who was a U.S. Vice President.

Kareem Jaffer Sharief was born on November 3, 1933, and passed away on November 25, 2018. He was an Indian politician. Sharief was a top leader of the Indian National Congress party. He served as the Railways Minister of India from 1991 to 1995.

The Brooks Range (Athabaskan "gwazhał") is a mountain range in far northern North America, stretching from west to east across northern Alaska into Canada's Yukon Territory. It reaches its highest point at Mount Isto, with an elevation of about 1,785 meters. This range is thought to be about 126 million years old. In the United States, these mountains are part of the Rocky Mountains. In Canada, they are considered separate, with the northern border of the Rocky Mountains being the Liard River, far south in British Columbia. The range is mostly uninhabited, except for the Dalton Highway and the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System, which pass through Atigun Pass (1,415 meters, 4,643 feet) on their way to Prudhoe Bay on Alaska's North Slope. The only settlements in the range are the Alaska native villages of Anaktuvuk and Arctic Village, along with the small communities of Coldfoot, Wiseman, Bettles, and Chandalar. In the far west, near the Wulik River in the De Long Mountains, is the Red Dog Mine, the world's largest zinc mine. The range was named in 1925 by the United States Board on Geographic Names after Alfred Hulse Brooks, who was the chief USGS geologist for Alaska from 1903 to 1924. Historically, the range was also called the Arctic Mountains, Hooper Mountains, Meade Mountains, and Meade River Mountains. The Canadian part of the range is officially called the British Mountains. In Canada, the British Mountains include Ivvavik National Park.

The monk parakeet, also called the quaker parrot, is a small, brightly green parrot. It has a grayish breast and a greenish-yellow belly. On average, it lives for 20 to 30 years. It comes from areas in South America, like Argentina, that are not too hot or too cold. In some places, like parts of North America and Europe, there are groups of these parrots that live on their own.

Greifswald, officially called the University and Hanseatic City of Greifswald, is a city in northeastern Germany. It is in the state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, about halfway between Berlin and Hamburg, and 80 km (50 mi) from the Polish border. Greifswald is near the Baltic Sea and has a small river called the Ryck running through it. It is close to Germany's two largest islands, Rügen and Usedom, and near three of Germany's national parks. Greifswald became the capital of the new district of Vorpommern-Greifswald in 2011. It is one of the main cities in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, together with Stralsund. In 2013, Greifswald had about 55, 659 people, including 12, 500 students and 5, 000 employees of the University of Greifswald. Greifswald attracts international attention because of the university, the biocon valley, the Nord Stream gas pipeline, and the Wendelstein 7-x nuclear fusion project.

Balkrishna Vithaldas Doshi, born on August 26, 1927, is an Indian architect. He is considered an important figure in Indian architecture and is known for his work in shaping architectural ideas in India. Working under Le Corbusier and Louis Kahn, he is a pioneer of modernist and brutalist architecture in India. Some of his notable designs include the IIM Bangalore, IIM Udaipur, NIFT Delhi, Amdavad Ni Gufa, CEPT University, and the Aranya low-cost housing development in Indore. This development won the Aga Khan Award for Architecture. In 2018, he became the first Indian architect to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize, a very important award in the field. He has also received the Padma Shri and the Padma Bhushan awards.

Kraftwerk, meaning "power station" in German, is a band from Düsseldorf, formed in 1970 by Ralf Hütter and Florian Schneider. They are known as pioneers of electronic music and were among the first to make this music popular. The group started in West Germany’s experimental rock scene in the early 1970s, using synthesizers, drum machines, and vocoders. On albums like "Autobahn" (1974), "Trans-Europe Express" (1977), "The Man-Machine" (1978), and "Computer World" (1981), Kraftwerk created a style called "robot pop" by combining electronic music with pop melodies, simple arrangements, and repetitive rhythms. They wore matching suits for their performances. Wolfgang Flür left the group in 1987, and Karl Bartos followed in 1990. Florian Schneider left in 2008. Their music has influenced many artists and genres, including synth-pop, hip hop, post-punk, techno, ambient, and club music. In 2014, they received a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award. They won another Grammy in 2018 for their live album "3-D The Catalogue." As of 2020, the band still tours.

Putnam County is in New York, United States. In 2010, there were 99,710 people living there. The main town is called Carmel. Putnam County was created in 1812 from Dutchess County and is named after Israel Putnam, who fought in important wars. It's part of a big area called the New York-Newark-Jersey City Metropolitan Area. Putnam County is in a region called the Lower Hudson River Valley. It's about an hour's drive from Midtown Manhattan. You can also get there by train in about an hour and 20 minutes. Putnam County is one of the wealthiest counties in America. In 2012, it was ranked 21st by median household income and 43rd by per-capita income.

Lee Hyo-ri, born on May 10, 1979, is a South Korean singer, record producer, activist, actress, and TV host. Known as the "nation's fairy" during her early days, she started as a member of the girl group Fin.K.L. Later, she became a solo artist. In 2003, she released her first solo album, "Stylish," and won several "artist of the year" awards. In 2006, Lee was the highest-paid female singer in South Korea after signing a contract with MNet Media.

Violet Brown, born Mosse on March 10, 1900, and passed away on September 15, 2017, was a Jamaican supercentenarian. She became the oldest verified living person in the world after Emma Morano died on April 15, 2017, and held this title for five months. She was 117 years old when she died. At the time of her death, she was the fifth-oldest person in history and one of the last two known people born in the 19th century.

This list includes all 67 counties of Pennsylvania. Philadelphia, the largest city, is part of Philadelphia County. Philadelphia's city and county governments became one in 1854. In 1951, a vote made all county government work part of the city. Eight of the ten most people-filled counties are in the southeast. Four out of the top five are there. Eight of the top ten most populous counties are in either the Philadelphia or Pittsburgh areas.

João Ubildo Ribeiro was born on January 23, 1941, and died on July 18, 2014. He was a Brazilian writer, journalist, screenwriter, and professor. Many of his books and short stories were turned into movies and TV shows in Brazil. Ribeiro joined the Brazilian Academy of Letters in 1994. At the time of his death, many people thought he was Brazil's greatest living novelist.

Zvečan is a town and municipality in the Mitrovica district of Kosovo. In 2015, it had 16,650 people living there. The area covers 35 villages and a town. Zvečan is in North Kosovo, where Serbs make up the majority of the population. This region works mostly separately from the rest of Kosovo, where Albanians are the majority. After the 2013 Brussels agreement, the municipality joined the group of Serb municipalities.

neopterygii comes from the Greek words "new" and "fin." It's a subclass of ray-finned fish (actinopterygii). Only a few changes happened when neopterygians evolved from actinopterygians. They appeared during the late Permian period, before dinosaurs existed. Neopterygians moved faster than their ancestors. Their scales and skeletons became lighter, and their jaws got stronger. Unlike other fish, neopterygians lost the ability to sense electricity, even though some catfish and gymnotiformes later developed this sense differently. A big change for actinopterygian fishes was the evolution of neopterygians. Neopterygians gained better control over their dorsal and anal fins, making them better swimmers. They also developed new features in their skulls, allowing them to feed in different ways and live in new environments. These improvements made neopterygii the most common type of fish and, in fact, the main group of vertebrates. Neopterygii includes teleosts, which are most of the fish we see today.

Numidia (202 BC – 40 BC, Berber: Inumiden) was an ancient kingdom of the Numidians, located in what is now Algeria and a small part of Tunisia and Libya in the Maghreb. It originally had two parts: the Massylii in the east and the Masaesyli in the west. During the Second Punic War (218–201 BC), Masinissa, king of the Massylii, defeated Syphax of the Masaesyli, unifying Numidia into one kingdom. The kingdom was first a sovereign state and later became a Roman province or client state. At its largest extent, Numidia bordered Mauretania to the west, Africa Proconsularis (now part of Tunisia) to the east, the Mediterranean Sea to the north, and the Sahara to the south. It is considered one of the first major states in the history of Algeria and the Berber world.
